title: Harness: the evidence set is built from the same message grep the anomaly scan was fixed for
description:
The corrector fixes which commit the ANOMALY patterns judge. It does not reach the
EVIDENCE set, and the same message-grep defect lives there.

`gather-evidence.sh:39` sets COMMITS from `git log --all -F --grep="$ID"` and `:45`
builds TOUCHED_FILES from it, so any commit whose message cites a bead id donates its
files to that bead's evidence. `research/SESSION-PROMPTS.md` asks every session to cite
its beads in commit messages, so this fires routinely.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED WITH cairn-fi7. TOUCHED_FILES is consumed at `:79-83` as the second
resolver for a path hint taken from the bead body, with a project-wide `rg --files`
fallback at `:94` behind it. Correcting it after the fact means re-running the hint
resolution, which is re-implementing the script rather than correcting its output. The
corrector cannot reach it without a sixth fork of the vendored skill, and cairn-exi's
standing choice is no sixth fork.

BOUNDED, not harmless. A hint has to substring-match a file from the foreign commit
before it matters, and the project-wide fallback would often resolve the same path
anyway. Nobody has measured how often the foreign match wins.

DONE WHEN
- A measurement over the closed beads of how often TOUCHED_FILES resolves a hint to a
  file that came from a commit the bead did not close, and what the fallback would have
  resolved instead. A count, not an impression.
- Either a cairn-owned correction that does not fork, or a recorded decision that the
  measured rate does not justify one.

title: Harness: two gates shell out to br, and CI has no bead database for them to read
description:
CI run 33457369925 on commit a8252a3, the first run after the Actions quota refreshed, failed
with 2 failed / 1916 passed. Both failures are the same cause:

  tests/unit/test_bead_artifact_block.py::test_a_matching_extractor_regex_does_not_deny
  tests/unit/test_theater_patterns.py::test_cli_passes_the_real_tree_under_the_real_policy

  br show cairn-exi exited 6:
    "Sync conflict: Pending sync-merge state is unknown because database
     '/Users/runner/work/cairn/cairn/.beads/beads.db' is missing"

`.beads/beads.db` is untracked derived state. `issues.jsonl` is what the repo carries, and
nothing in the CI job rebuilds the database from it. Both tests pass on a developer machine
because a developer machine has a database, which is the local-green / CI-green privilege
divergence.

The two gates are cairn-owned and both resolve a bead id at runtime:
`scripts/bead_artifact_block.py` verifies a block against the bead body, and
`scripts/theater_patterns.py` resolves `exempt_until_bead` to check whether an exemption is
still live.

WHAT IS NOT YET ESTABLISHED: which fix is right. Two candidates, and they differ in what they
claim.

  Rebuild the database in CI with `br sync --import-only` before the gates run. That is the
  documented recovery path and it makes CI resemble a developer machine. It also means the
  gates keep a hard dependency on a binary and a database to answer a question that
  `issues.jsonl` already answers.

  Read `issues.jsonl` directly. The file is committed, so the dependency disappears, but the
  gates then stop exercising the path a developer's `br` actually takes.

DONE WHEN
- CI green on a commit that exercises both gates.
- A decision, recorded, on whether a cairn-owned gate may depend on `br` at all, since the
  answer binds every future gate that wants to resolve a bead id.
- Whichever is chosen, a test that fails while the defect is present: the gate must be shown
  to work in an environment with no `beads.db`.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
CLOSED. The decision stands; the recipe it named does not, and the measurement that changed it
is the substance of this close.

WHAT WAS DECIDED, AND WHY IT SURVIVED

CI derives the bead store from the tracked JSONL through br, rather than each gate growing its
own parser of a format br owns. issues.jsonl is the tracked source of truth and beads.db is
derived, so a CI job deriving it is CI resembling a developer machine. Reading the JSONL
directly in each gate was rejected: it stops exercising the path a developer's br takes.

THE RECIPE THE BEAD NAMED IS NOT SUFFICIENT

`br sync --import-only` was recorded here as the documented recovery path. Measured on br
0.2.22 in a scratch workspace holding only the four tracked .beads files and no database:

  br show cairn-exi --json    exit 6   SYNC_CONFLICT
  br sync --import-only       exit 6   same refusal
  br init                     exit 6   same refusal

br refuses every storage open while a .beads directory carrying no database is in place.
Bisected across five probes: an empty pre-existing .beads/ is the trigger, and `br init` in a
directory with no .beads at all exits 0. So the CI step moves .beads aside, runs br init,
restores the four tracked files, then imports. Executed verbatim from the workflow text in a
scratch checkout built from `git archive HEAD .beads`: exit 0, 62 issues created, `br show`
resolving afterwards, and the four restored files byte-identical to HEAD by sha256.

THE DEFECT UNDERNEATH, WHICH IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF ONE SHAPE

A database that does not exist was reported as `sync_merge_pending_unknown` -- a pending merge
whose state could not be inspected. A file that is absent is not a conflict, and the
remediation offered was `br list --all`: check the id, for a problem that has nothing to do
with the id. That is an absence given the shape of a verdict, after cairn-8jm, cairn-a30 and
cairn-keq.

The message is br's and cairn does not own it. How cairn's gates react is cairn's.
scripts/br_lookup.py classifies a bead lookup into four conditions, each with its own message
and its own remediation, and a test asserts the four remediations are pairwise distinct:

  br-absent      br is not installed
  no-database    beads.db is derived; issues.jsonl is tracked, with the rebuild recipe
  unknown-bead   the id is not in the store
  unreadable     anything the allowlist does not recognize, which blocks

VERIFICATION, RE-EXECUTED BY THE SESSION

Six tests observed failing against the unfixed gates before the fix.
99 passed with a database present, and 99 passed from an empty mktemp -d cwd with no .beads
anywhere above it -- which is the CI condition, since cwd is what br walks up from.
scripts/check.sh 1958 passed, exit 0.
The planted negatives were re-run by the session AFTER the reformat the implementer's own
NO-CLAIM flagged as unmeasured: removing the ci.yml step kills 3, and neutering
br_lookup.unavailable() kills 8. All four files restored byte-identical.

Two pre-existing tests were repaired in passing: both reached a monkeypatched subprocess only
because a real database happened to exist.

NO-CLAIM

CI behavior after this change is inference. GitHub Actions was not run; what was executed is
the rebuild script's exact text in a macOS scratch checkout, with RUNNER_TEMP set to a temp
dir. The runner differs in ways not reproduced: a real actions/checkout tree, RUNNER_TEMP
semantics, and the br binary from the release tarball rather than the local one. The br
behaviors are measured on 0.2.22 on one machine, and why br refuses is inference from the
error text rather than from its source. CODE_CONDITIONS is an allowlist built from two
observed codes; another code meaning "no database" would land in `unreadable`, which blocks
rather than passes, so the failure is coarse rather than silent. Giving no-database the
warn-not-deny treatment in theater_patterns.py extends an existing documented decision and is
a judgment call this bead did not specify. Whether cairn-o25's br upgrade changes any of the
0.2.22 behaviors measured here is untested, and that bead owns it.

title: Harness: the audit mints completion debt from a phase that did not run
description:
The audit mints a completion-debt bead from its "missing items" list. On the pre-commit
path that list is not a measurement, and two debt beads were minted from it for work that
was done.

WHAT THE LIST ACTUALLY CONTAINS. For cairn-m0-e0s.12 it names five items:

  tests.integration.primary  tests.e2e.primary  tests.fuzz.primary
  tests.metamorphic.primary  telemetry.primary

Read the pass's own spec.json. `code.primary` carries sixteen `expected_path_hints` and
resolves FOUND. Every one of those five carries NO `expected_path_hints` field at all, so
there is nothing for the deterministic extractor to match a bead body against. Nothing
written in a bead's description, notes or ARTIFACTS block can resolve them.

Four of the five sit in the "Required tests" dimension, which the same scorecard reports as

  EXCLUDED from numerator and denominator - WAIVED - Phase 4 ran in stub mode
  (executor='single-bead-stub'); no subagent re-ran the tests

So the phase that would decide whether those tests exist never ran, and its silence is
printed under a heading that reads as a finding.

WHAT IT COST. cairn-m0-e0s.12.1 and cairn-m0-e0s.16.1 were minted at 650 with acceptance
criteria requiring every listed item to gain a cited implementation and a cited passing
test. Both parents score 780 against a threshold of 700, and every file behind the listed
items exists at HEAD. An ARTIFACTS-block sweep across all eighteen M0 beads raised
cairn-m0-e0s.16's extractor path hints from 15 to 22 and its evidence citations from 8 to
15, and moved neither the score nor the missing-items list, because the list does not read
those fields.

This is the same shape as the defect cairn-exi fixed, on the remediation path rather than
the scoring path: `unmeasured_dimensions: full_credit` awarded points for a dimension
nobody measured, and this awards DEBT for one nobody measured.

DONE WHEN
- The remediation path stops minting debt from items whose dimension was excluded as
  unmeasured, or the minted bead states on its face which of its items were measured and
  which were not, so a reader can tell a gap from a stub.
- An item with no `expected_path_hints` is either given them or reported as unresolvable
  rather than missing. Absent and unmeasurable are different verdicts.
- A decision, recorded, on whether the pre-commit path should run a real Phase 4 at all, or
  whether a deterministic pass should simply decline to mint debt.

TEST PLAN

- tests/unit/test_audit_missing_items.py — the classifier and the gate. A searched-for item

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
CLOSED AT d438635. Suite 1876 passed, all gates pass, exit 0 (scripts/check.sh, run alone,
load average 6.82). NOT CI-VERIFIED: the Actions free tier is exhausted until 2026-09-01;
run 33129725789 on the parent 41ecaa1 ran zero steps in four seconds with the annotation
"The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit
needs to be increased." Every close in this session carries that caveat.

WHAT WAS WRONG, ESTABLISHED BY READING THE PRODUCER, NOT THE TABLE

The five items on cairn-m0-e0s.12's missing list are not unresolvable, they are unreachable.
gather-evidence.sh guards its per-test ripgrep with `[ "$NAME" != "primary" ]` where NAME is
the id's last dot-segment, and the spec extractor names every test item tests.<type>.primary,
so the guard is false for the whole population and no search ever runs. Its second loop
iterates documentation, migrations, feature_flags, telemetry and ci_workflows but carries
case arms for two of them, so an item in the other three reaches emit_check with the initial
MISSING untouched. And expected_path_hints has exactly one reader in the file, inside the
code_artifacts loop. score-bead.py:1236 lists all of these under a heading that reads as a
finding, and remediate.sh copies that section verbatim into a minted bead's acceptance
criteria demanding an implementation and a passing test for each.

ACCEPTANCE, EACH RE-EXECUTED

1. "The remediation path stops minting debt from items whose dimension was excluded, or the
minted bead states on its face which of its items were measured and which were not."

MET by the second clause. The corrector rewrites the section into two labeled subsections
with a per-item reason. Replaying remediate.sh:111's own extraction expression over a
rewritten scorecard captured 1234 bytes carrying both subsection headings, both classes of
item, and the per-item annotations, so the text a minted bead would carry states which items
were measured.

2. "An item with no expected_path_hints is either given them or reported as unresolvable
rather than missing."

MET, and the first attempt got this wrong in the direction that matters. It attributed the
no-hints reason to every category, including documentation and ci_workflows, which the
gatherer searches by file and directory existence and which read no hint at all. That
laundered a genuinely measured absence into silence, which is this bead's own defect running
backwards. Reproduced at exit 0 on a two-item fixture: before, 0 measured gaps and 2
unmeasured; after scoping the reason to HINT_DRIVEN_CATEGORIES = ("code_artifacts",),
2 measured gaps and 0 unmeasured. The same fixture marked FALSE-CLOSED no longer trips the
deny, because its verdict rests on a search that ran.

3. "A decision, recorded, on whether the pre-commit path should run a real Phase 4, or
whether a deterministic pass should simply decline to mint debt."

DECIDED: it declines, and it already did. assets/pre-commit-hook.sh:87 passes
--policy report-only; single-bead-audit.sh applies audit-policy.yaml at line 81 and parses
CLI flags at 86, so the flag wins; its Phase 9 calls remediate.sh only for a policy other
than report-only. A real Phase 4 is out of reach regardless: single-bead-audit.sh:152 writes
the stub compliance.json and names the compliance-verifier subagent as the orchestrator's
work, and a git hook spawns no subagent. The reasoning and its citations are recorded at
audit-policy.yaml:52-82. A deterministic pass holds no measurement of the tests dimension and
therefore no standing to mint debt from its own silence.

FILES

scripts/audit_missing_items.py:64-105 the gatherer's unreachable predicates as named
constants, each carrying the condition it rests on; :145 the classifier; :162
excluded_dimensions, parsed from the scorecard's own table rather than hardcoded; :207
spec_item_id_of, both producer line shapes; :281 process, returning the outcome kind; :295
the debt-from-nothing predicate; :299 the atomic in-place rewrite; :346 structural problems
outranking the verdict.
.githooks/pre-commit:205-241 the wiring after the scorecard-coherence block, six outcome
markers to .beads_hook.log, rc other than 0 denying.
audit-policy.yaml:52-82 the recorded decision.
tests/unit/test_audit_missing_items.py:1-351 · tests/unit/test_audit_missing_items_gatherer.py:1-89
· tests/integration/test_audit_missing_items_drift.py:1-48
tests/fixtures/compliance_skill/ the frozen gatherer excerpt and its source digest ·
tests/fixtures/compliance_pass/cairn-m0-e0s.12/ a trimmed real pass, byte-identical to
beads_compliance_audit/passes/2026-08-27T18-09-58Z, sha256 390d904b481cf00b, 3418 bytes.

THE GATE FIRED IN PRODUCTION

The hook run that made this commit printed
  UNCHANGED cairn-o0l — 1 measured gap(s), 2 unmeasured

WHAT THE TEST AUDIT FOUND, AND WHAT IT COST

A fresh Opus /optimal-tests --audit found six confirmed defects. The worst was on this
bead's headline property: every assertion about the two subsection labels reached them
through constants imported from the subject, so the label text sat on both sides of the
comparison. Swapping the two constants' values, so every classification rendered under the
opposite heading, left all 29 tests green. Since remediate.sh copies the section verbatim,
an inverted label would have shipped an inverted claim into the exact artifact this tool
exists to correct. The literals now live in the test file and the swap is KILLED by 10.

Second: the corrector failed open silently on upstream heading drift. With the heading
absent, section_bounds returned None, classify yielded no items, bool(items) short-circuited
the deny, and the tool printed UNCHANGED and exited 0 for a bead it should have refused.
Now a distinct NO-SECTION outcome at exit 3 with its own log line, and the heading render
line is frozen in the fixture and asserted hermetically.

Also fixed: two negative assertions checking for a substring absent from the subject; the
(none) idempotence filter whose fixture could not express its failure; and the same spec item
classified oppositely depending on which producer wrote its line.

MUTATIONS, RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY OF THE IMPLEMENTER

label swap KILLED by 10 · empty gap note KILLED by 1 · hint-category guard KILLED by 4 ·
debt-from-nothing predicate KILLED by 3 · the scorecard write KILLED by 13 ·
searched-categories constant KILLED by 6. No INCONCLUSIVE verdicts. The last three were
re-run after the implementer's outcome refactor, which it had left as an assumption.

CI PARITY

Measured under a fake HOME: the drift file went from 7 skipped and 0 passed to 36 passed and
2 skipped across the three files. Only the two live-vs-frozen comparisons skip, which is the
pair that genuinely needs the machine-local skill.

DECLINED

The auditor flagged .githooks/pre-commit:205-241's three-outcome case as shell logic no test
can reach, against this project's stated convention. Declined: every other gate block in that
hook has the identical shape, the decisions live in Python and the shell maps a return code
to a log line. Changing it here alone makes the file less uniform, not safer. Accepted as a
limitation, owned by cairn-rof's neighborhood rather than left unnamed.

NO-CLAIM

remediate.sh was never executed. Only its awk extraction at line 111 was replayed over a
rewritten scorecard. No bead was minted, and br's handling of a multi-line body containing
### headings is unobserved. Acceptance 1 rests on an extraction-level check plus reading.

The debt-from-nothing deny is proven only on fixtures. No scorecard on disk is FALSE-CLOSED
with every item unmeasured.

The `- check` line shape is a parse gap of unestablished frequency. The parse is fixed and
both shapes are tested, but every compliance.json in the corpus is the stub with empty
checks, so it is unestablished whether Phase 4 ever emits FAIL for an item the gatherer never
searched. Owned by cairn-hzc.

EXIT_UNREADABLE_SPEC covers json.JSONDecodeError only. An unreadable scorecard.md, a
permissions error, or a spec.json parsing to a non-dict still raises uncaught. That exits
nonzero so it fails closed, but it is not a named outcome. Owned by cairn-hzc.

The frozen excerpt is a point-in-time cut. Someone editing gather-evidence.sh and
regenerating the fixture in one step passes both the hermetic and the live tests. Owned by
cairn-hzc.

feature_flags has no row in the corpus, and no extractor here has been observed emitting a
test id whose last segment is not primary, so that branch runs only on an invented shape.

The empty-NAME conjunct of the tests guard is unencoded. It errs conservative: it can fail to
flag silence, never launder a measured absence.

calibrate-bottom-n.sh takes head -40 of this section. Computed in Python, the largest section
in the corpus is 8 item lines and all 8 still land inside the window after the rewrite. That
is measured, not run.

The suite went red once at 1874 passed and 2 failed, both in tests/integration/test_runner.py,
which this change does not touch. Both passed in isolation, 3 passed in 1.30s. The receipt of
the failing attempt reads cpu_s 0.177998 against wall_ms 541.957 with a wall ceiling of
0.5352, which is cairn-x72 firing rather than a defect here. The green run above was obtained
on a second pass at a comparable load average.

title: Harness: the bead database corrupted, and its cleanup debris blocks commits under a misleading message
description:
Two failures on the same surface, both hit while closing cairn-pwj.

ONE. THE BEAD DATABASE CORRUPTED DURING ORDINARY USE.

`br comments add` reported "Mutation succeeded, but automatic JSONL export failed", and
`br doctor` then found:

  sqlite.integrity_check   ERROR  database disk image is malformed: page 16 is referenced
                                  multiple times (freelist trunk[0] leaf[116];
                                  table `issues` root -> child[36])
  sqlite3.integrity_check  ERROR  Tree 2 page 2 cell 36: 2nd reference to page 16; wrong #
                                  of entries in eight indexes

No power loss, no kill, no concurrent writer beyond the session's own. It happened within
the hour after the binary moved from 0.2.10 to 0.5.3 and the database was rebuilt from
JSONL, and `br doctor` had run `fsqlite: applied migration repairs` on the way.

Recovery cost nothing, because the database is untracked derived state and `issues.jsonl`
was intact: 57 records parsed, db and JSONL in sync, the pwj close present. Moving the
family aside and `br sync --import-only` rebuilt it, integrity clean, JSONL byte-identical
at sha256 9dbc90c8. That is the documented path and it worked.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: the cause. One occurrence, no reproduction, and three candidates
that this session cannot separate -- a 0.5.3 defect, damage inherited from the schema-10
database it replaced, or the interrupted write that produced the export failure. Recording
it as an observation rather than a diagnosis.

TWO. HOUSEKEEPING BLOCKS THE COMMIT GATE, AND THIS ONE RECURS.

`.githooks/pre-commit` runs the vendored beads hook, which runs `br doctor` and treats a
non-zero exit as a failed audit:

  ERROR: br doctor failed with exit code 1. Hand off to /fixing-beads-problems.
  [beads-hook] BLOCKED: one or more newly-closed beads failed quick audit (score < 700).

The message names a score, and no score was involved. The actual cause was

  WARN db.recovery_artifacts: Preserved recovery artifacts remain for this database family
                              (21 item(s))

which is a WARN about `.bak` files in `.beads/.br_recovery/`, a gitignored directory. Every
database rebuild and every `br doctor --repair` leaves more of them, so the count only
grows, and `br doctor --repair` reports "No errors detected; nothing to repair" for exactly
this finding. Clearing them by hand is what unblocked the commit, twice in one session.

So a commit that closes a bead can be refused for a pile of backup files, under a message
that says the bead scored below threshold. The diagnosis cost more than the fix both times.

DONE WHEN

title: Harness: cairn doctor accumulates run directories with no gc, and flagged backups resist removal
description:
The doctor's run artifacts accumulate under `.doctor/runs/<run-id>/` and nothing
ever removes them. Every `cairn doctor` invocation, read-only ones included, writes
a run directory, so the tree grows without bound on an agent that runs the doctor
as its first move whenever a command refuses -- which is what `robot-docs` tells it
to do.

Two properties make this more than housekeeping.

`mutate._backup` copies the source file's flags onto the backup, so a backup of the
pin or the attestation log carries `uappnd`. A run directory holding one cannot be
removed until the flag is cleared recursively. This is visible today as eight
`PytestWarning: (rm_rf) ... Directory not empty` lines in the suite, on temp trees
pytest tried to clean.

And the doctor performs no deletion by design: `mutate`'s undo of its own `mkdir` is
the single `os.rmdir` in the codebase, and the code-search gate refuses every other
removal spelling. So collection cannot be a side effect of an existing path; it has
to be a subcommand that is explicitly allowed to remove, with its own gating.

WHAT: `cairn doctor gc --before <date> --yes` from the CLI-SURFACE of
`/world-class-doctor-mode-for-cli-tools`, which `cairn-m0-e0s.18` implemented
without it. Dangerous, gated on `--yes`, dry-run by default, listing what it would
remove and removing nothing without the flag -- the shape `cairn gc` already uses
for blobs (`src/cairn/gc.py`, `cairn-m0-e0s.13`). It must clear `uappnd` before
removing a flagged backup, and it must refuse to remove the run a `latest` symlink
points at.

The same surface also names `cairn doctor diff` and `--since=<run-id>`, neither of
which exists. They are cheap once the run index is readable and belong here rather
than in a bead of their own.

DONE WHEN: a doctor run directory older than a given date is removed by
`doctor gc --before <date> --yes` and left alone without `--yes`; a flagged backup
inside it is removed rather than refused; the run `.doctor/latest` points at is
refused with its own exit code and a message naming it; and the code-search gate
still passes, with the new removal confined to one module the gate names alongside
`mutate.py` and `artifacts.py`.

Surfaced by cairn-m0-e0s.18's audit as F15, recorded there as out of scope for that
bead rather than folded into it.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
RETRACTION. This bead's description and my earlier comment say the compliance audit
"mis-measures this project" and needs fixing. That framing is wrong and I am
withdrawing it. I concluded a defect in the producer from the shape of its output
without reading the producer, which is the exact inference
`absence-is-not-evidence.md` exists to stop.

What I did not check before claiming it: the skill ships
subagents/compliance-verifier.md and subagents/test-depth-auditor.md, the two the
stub banner named as not-run, and subagents/bead-spec-extractor.md, which its own
Phase 2 warning recommends for prose acceptance criteria ("LLM gets 10-49 items vs
deterministic 0-7"). It carries 43 scripts, 63 references and 23 subagents, and
scripts/_load-policy.sh resolves a project-local `audit-policy.yaml` with
precedence hardcoded < YAML < CLI. threshold, weights_by_type, weights_by_label,
project_theater_patterns, subagents and phase_4_environment are all configurable
per project without touching the vendored skill.

So the audit is not broken. We invoked its cheapest path — single-bead-audit.sh
from a git hook, which deliberately runs no subagents because a hook cannot afford
test re-runs — and never wrote a policy file.

What survives, still measured and still worth acting on:

- The hook path awards Phase 4's 250 and Phase 6's 150 without running them, so
  400 of 1000 points are unearned on that path whatever the bead contains.
- cairn-qn9 scored 970 with zero extracted spec items; cairn-m0-e0s.12, which
  carries 108 tests, six metamorphic relations and six killed mutants, scored 760.
  The ordering is inverted on the hook path.
- The cross-bead dimension took cairn-m0-e0s.12 to 0/50 for ten findings, each
  "references non-closed bead X (status=open)", which research/SESSION-PROMPTS.md
  requires a close to do.

The fix is configuration, not a fork. The threshold question is answered the same
way: it is one line in audit-policy.yaml, and it should not move until the waived
phases actually run, because raising a number over a stubbed measurement buys
confidence rather than assurance.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
The configuration path is inert on this machine, and it fails silently. Measured
2026-08-25, and it changes what this bead has to do.

  $ python3 -c "import yaml"
  ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'
  $ which python3
  /opt/homebrew/bin/python3          # Homebrew python@3.14, externally managed

Both readers swallow that:

- scripts/_load-policy.sh:49 runs `python3 - "$1" "$2" <<'PY' 2>/dev/null || true`
  around `import sys, yaml`, so the ImportError is discarded and the function
  emits nothing. The caller's `[ -n "${POLICY_X:-}" ]` then keeps its hardcoded
  default. Proved by sourcing it directly against a file that parses under pyyaml
  and holds `threshold: 700` at top level: POLICY_FILE resolves, THRESHOLD is
  empty.
- scripts/score-bead.py:95 wraps `import yaml` in try/except and sets
  `yaml = None`, so weights_by_type and weights_by_label are read by nothing.

So audit-policy.yaml exists, resolves, and binds nowhere. A reader would take the
file as authoritative; it is decoration until PyYAML is present. That is the
silent-fail-open shape from enforcement-over-instructions.md, in the tool we were
relying on to catch exactly that.

`audit-policy.yaml` now ships at the project root with this stated in its header,
so it does not lie about itself, and the same file is seeded into
beads_compliance_audit/, which is gitignored and had been holding an unmodified
copy of the skill's template since 2026-08-21 — that copy shadows the project-local
file, because the loader prefers the audit-dir path.

The threshold still binds, by luck rather than design: .githooks/pre-commit reaches
single-bead-audit.sh with `--threshold`, and CLI beats YAML.

WHAT
- Operator action, not an agent action: make PyYAML importable by the `python3` on
  PATH. It is Homebrew's externally-managed interpreter, so this is a deliberate
  machine-global change and belongs to whoever owns the machine.
- Then re-audit cairn-m0-e0s.12 and cairn-qn9 and check the ordering inverts back:
  the bead with 108 tests, six metamorphic relations and six killed mutants must
  outscore the cleanup with none. That is the falsifiable test for the weights.
- Only after that ordering is right does the threshold become worth moving.
- Consider reporting the silent-fail-open upstream; a skill whose job is to catch
  unearned green should not have a configuration path that fails open in silence.

DONE WHEN: `python3 -c "import yaml"` succeeds; a re-audit of both beads scores
cairn-m0-e0s.12 above cairn-qn9, with both scorecards pasted; and a deliberate edit
to weights_by_type.task provably moves a score, so the file is shown to bind rather
than assumed to.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
PROVED, by controlled substitution rather than inference, and it is not a Cairn
problem. The same condition holds for every project on this machine.

Baseline, system python3 (Homebrew python@3.14, no PyYAML):

  cairn            THRESHOLD=[]  POLICY=[]
  goddess-engine   THRESHOLD=[]

Then a shim earlier on PATH, `python3` execing `uv run --with pyyaml python`,
changing nothing else:

  cairn            THRESHOLD=[700]  POLICY=[completion-debt]
  goddess-engine   THRESHOLD=[700]

Both projects' policy files are well-formed and both bind the moment the
interpreter can parse YAML. PyYAML is the sole cause. goddess-engine has carried an
inert `.beads/audit-policy.yaml` for as long as this machine has lacked the module,
which nothing reported, because both readers swallow the ImportError.

That makes the fix worth more than one project: one install makes every
audit-policy.yaml on this machine live at once. It also raises the stakes on
reporting it upstream — a skill whose purpose is catching unearned green has a
configuration path that fails open in silence, and two projects here believed they
were configured when they were not.

The shim is not the fix and was removed after the measurement; editing PATH for a
vendored skill is a trick, not a deployment.

title: Harness: the deterministic audit path cannot tell an honest prose bead from a false close
description:
The compliance gate on the pre-commit path cannot separate an honest bead from a
false close, and no threshold, floor or weighting closes the gap. The cause is
extraction: the deterministic extractor reads a bead body with regular
expressions, and a body written as prose yields nothing for it to check.

Measured 2026-08-26. A fixture bead closed with the word "Done." and a body naming
two files that do not exist, beside cairn-cue, a real harness bead:

                       cairn-cue          the "Done." fixture
  Implementation       n/a 250/250        n/a 250/250
  Required tests       WAIVED 300/300     WAIVED 300/300
  Test depth           WAIVED 200/200     WAIVED 200/200
  Docs                 n/a 25/25          n/a 25/25
  Anti-theater         200/200            185/200
  Cross-bead           0/25               15/25
  measured weight      225                225

Identical where it matters. Under audit-policy.yaml's unmeasured_dimensions switch
at any floor that fails the fixture, cairn-cue reports UNVERIFIABLE too, and so
does cairn-qn9. The switch is correct and tested; it is off because turning it on
blocks honest work it cannot distinguish.

Phase 2 has said so all along. Its own warning on cairn-qn9 read "produced only 1
item(s) from a 2689-char body", and spec.json held zero. The skill ships
subagents/bead-spec-extractor.md for exactly this, and its frontmatter claims
10-49 items where the deterministic path gets 0-7.

WHAT
Run the LLM spec extractor on the path that gates commits, or accept that the
pre-commit path is a smoke test and move the gate to a path that can run
subagents. The two are different answers and the choice is the operator's:

  a. The hook invokes the extractor. A hook that calls a model costs seconds and
     tokens on every commit that closes a bead, which is the reason the skill's
     single-bead path runs no subagents.
  b. The hook stays deterministic and stops claiming a verdict. Its banner already
     says the score is an upper bound; the honest form is that a deterministic pass
     cannot return "verified" at all, only "not obviously false".
  c. A bead body must carry a machine-readable artifact block that the
     deterministic extractor can read, and the gate requires one. This puts the
     cost on the author rather than on every commit, and it is the only option that
     keeps the hook fast and the verdict meaningful.

DONE WHEN: a false-closed fixture and cairn-cue, audited on whichever path gates
commits, land on opposite sides of the threshold, with both scorecards pasted.

Surfaced by cairn-cue, which fixed everything upstream of this: the policy file's
weights, threshold and remediation now reach the scorer, and a bead directory with
no spec.json is refused rather than scored 1000.

comments.text:
OPERATOR DECISION, 2026-08-26: option (c).

A bead body must carry a machine-readable artifact block that the deterministic
extractor can read, and the gate requires one. The cost lands on the author, once
per bead, rather than on every commit that closes one.

WHY NOT THE OTHER TWO

  (a) the hook invokes the LLM extractor. Rejected on three counts: it makes a gate
      path non-deterministic; it needs the network, so an offline commit cannot run
      the gate at all, which is fail-open wearing the appearance of enforcement; and
      the vendored skill refuses subagents on the single-bead path by design, so
      this would be a sixth forked call site to re-apply after every upstream update.

  (b) the hook stops claiming a verdict. Honest, and the cheapest to land, but it
      converts the gate into advisory text and a false close commits. It also cannot
      satisfy this bead's own DONE WHEN, which requires two beads to land on opposite
      sides of a threshold; option (b) leaves no threshold that decides anything.

WHAT (c) UNBLOCKS

title: Harness: the anomaly scan attributes another bead's commit, and its verdict moves with unrelated commit messages
description:
`anomaly-scan.sh` pattern 23 decides which commit closed a bead with

    CLOSING_SHA=$(git log --all -F --grep="$ID" --format=%H | head -1)

That is the newest commit whose message *mentions* the bead id, not the commit
that closed it. It then counts every added line in `.gitignore`, `pyproject.toml`,
`.flake8`, `.eslintignore` or `.ubsignore` as an ignore-list suppression and raises
a BLOCKING finding worth -50 on the anti-theater dimension.

TWO DEFECTS, BOTH REPRODUCED

1. MISATTRIBUTION. For `cairn-m0-e0s.16` the pattern selects `dcbe208`, which is
   cairn-cue's commit and merely names .16 in its body. The bead's own closing
   commit is `04289d2 close cairn-m0-e0s.16`. The line counted as a suppression is
   `+.beads_hook.log` added to `.gitignore` -- a log file being ignored, which
   silences no diagnostic at all.

   Exit-0 while the defect is present:

     ID="cairn-m0-e0s.16"
     PICKED=$(git log --all -F --grep="$ID" --format=%H | head -1)
     CLOSING=$(git log --all -F --grep="close $ID" --format=%H | head -1)
     ADDED=$(git show "$PICKED" -- .gitignore pyproject.toml .flake8 | grep -E '^\+[^+]')
     [ "$PICKED" != "$CLOSING" ] && [ -n "$ADDED" ] && exit 0
     exit 1

     pattern 23 picked : dcbe208 give the audit a switch that can fail a false close
     bead's own commit : 04289d2 close cairn-m0-e0s.16
     counted as suppression: +.beads_hook.log
     REPRO EXIT=0

2. THE VERDICT IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE. `cairn-m0-e0s.12` scored 650 with BLOCKING=1 at
   2026-08-26T21:50Z and 750 with BLOCKING=0 forty minutes later, through the same
   `single-bead-audit.sh` against the same bead. Nothing about .12 changed. Two
   commits landed in between whose messages name it, moving what `head -1` selects.
   A gate whose score depends on unrelated later commit messages cannot be a gate,
   and this project's thesis is reproducibility.

WHAT THIS COSTS TODAY

The sweep recorded in `audit-policy.yaml` reported cairn-m0-e0s.12 and
cairn-m0-e0s.16 as FALSE-CLOSED at 650. Both readings are artifacts. Seventeen of
eighteen closed M0 beads pass, and the eighteenth fails on a commit that belongs to
a different bead. The two completion-debt beads the sweep minted rest on the same
artifact.

A second consequence reaches the evidence path, not just this pattern:
`gather-evidence.sh` builds TOUCHED_FILES from the same `--grep` over bead ids, so
any commit message citing a bead id donates its files to that bead's evidence.
Naming beads in commit messages is what `research/SESSION-PROMPTS.md` asks for.

DONE WHEN

- A cairn-owned fix that does not fork the skill. `audit-policy.yaml` is the
  supported surface and `project_theater_patterns` is already known to bind nothing
  (cairn-fur), so the honest options are: an upstream patch, a cairn pre-gate that
  overrides the finding, or accepting the pattern as advisory and subtracting its
  weight. Pick one and record why.
- A closing-commit rule that cannot select a commit belonging to another bead.
- `cairn-m0-e0s.12` and `cairn-m0-e0s.16` re-audited, with the two debt beads
  either substantiated or retired on the record.
- A reproduction that the audit returns the same score for one unchanged bead
  across two runs separated by an unrelated commit.

Depends on cairn-exi, which turned the switch on and made this visible: under
`unmeasured_dimensions: full_credit` the -50 was diluted by 500 of free weight and
never crossed the threshold.

comments.text:
FROM cairn-ofk (commit 1e16fc3): two unbounded waits on the commit-gate path.

`scripts/bead_artifact_block.py:166` runs `git cat-file` and `:178` runs `br show`,
both without a timeout. cairn-ofk swept the test suite and bounded every wait it
found there, but these two sit on the pre-commit gate rather than in the suite, so
they were outside that bead's WHAT and were flagged rather than changed.

Why it belongs here: this bead already owns a defect on the audit-gate surface, and
the failure mode is the same one cairn-ofk exists to prevent one layer down. A `br`
invocation that never returns wedges `git commit` with no output and no deadline --
the suite now has `timeout = 180` from pytest-timeout, and the gate path has nothing
equivalent. A wedged gate is worse than a wedged test, because the author cannot tell
whether the gate refused or died.

`scripts/scorecard_coherence.py` and `scripts/bead-test-plan.sh` are on the same path
and want the same sweep.

cairn-cue (commit cac8ab6) changed `score-bead.py`'s `score_cross_bead` to own a

  owned = [f for f in synthesis_findings if f.get("subject") == bead_id]

each says "bead A references non-closed bead B", and the defect, if any, belongs to A.

test the change against. The reading that a two-bead integration gap belongs to BOTH

It belongs on this bead rather than cairn-fur because both are attribution defects in
the same forked scorer: this bead's own finding is that the anomaly scan attributes
another bead's commit. Same file, same class, same fix surface.

Settling it needs a fixture producing one Integration-gap row and one Contradiction
row, then asserting which bead each is charged to.

pattern surface". That framing is too wide -- cairn-fur owns one policy section and

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
CLOSED 2026-08-27 at the commit this comment ships with.

DONE WHEN, clause by clause.

1. A CAIRN-OWNED FIX THAT DOES NOT FORK THE SKILL, with the choice recorded.

   Chosen: a post-gate that corrects the finding. `scripts/audit_attribution.py` runs after
   the vendored audit in `.githooks/pre-commit`, re-derives the two attributed patterns
   against the resolved commit, re-scores, and supplies the exit code the hook gates on.
   The vendored skill is untouched; both fork markers the hook checks are unchanged.

   Why not the other two. An upstream patch is a sixth forked call site, and an update
   reverts it silently -- the reason `.githooks/pre-commit` already checks two markers.
   Subtracting the pattern's weight discards a real signal: a closing commit that genuinely
   silences a linter is worth flagging. Correcting the attribution keeps the signal and
   moves only code cairn owns. The rationale is in the module docstring and in CLAUDE.md.

2. A CLOSING-COMMIT RULE THAT CANNOT SELECT A COMMIT BELONGING TO ANOTHER BEAD.

   `scripts/closing_commit.py`. The rule is the status flip to `closed` in the
   `.beads/*.jsonl` diff, which only the closing commit carries. Both git hooks read their
   newly-closed list through it; it replaces an inline heredoc duplicated in each.

     $ uv run python scripts/closing_commit.py cairn-m0-e0s.16 cairn-m0-e0s.12 cairn-ofk
     cairn-m0-e0s.16 04289d27eeb979a1ba3bcdf6f6083c6b5fcde9ce
     cairn-m0-e0s.12 79e1398afc1b59913fc1d9514278eeab0846eaa6
     cairn-ofk       e41c047036a2a17727736c12a8159b07a9b3f83e

   `04289d2` is the ground truth this bead names. The grep rule picks `0e56023` for .16 and
   `cac8ab6` for .12, and BOTH have moved since this bead was written -- the .16 pick was
   `dcbe208` when the defect was recorded. The instability is not historical; it is live.

   A bead the pending commit closes resolves to `STAGED` and is judged against the staged
   diff. Across all 24 closed and tombstoned beads the rule resolves 0 UNKNOWN.

3. THE TWO BEADS RE-AUDITED.

   Both 780/1000, BLOCKING=0, above the 700 threshold, through real `single-bead-audit.sh`
   runs. Their earlier 650 FALSE-CLOSED readings were artifacts.

   Demonstrated directly on the pass that still holds the misattributed finding
   (`2026-08-26T16-29-01Z`, copied to a scratch tree):

     OK cairn-m0-e0s.16 CORRECTED 04289d27...: dropped 1 finding(s) raised against
        a commit the bead did not close -> score 760      (was 650 / BLOCKING=1)

   Idempotent: a second run reads UNCHANGED at the same score, and all eight artifacts in
   the bead directory are byte-identical by sha256 across the two runs. That was checked in
   Python deliberately -- the shell `diff` on this machine reports two files of 151 and 82
   bytes as identical, which is now a working note in CLAUDE.md.

   The two [completion-debt] beads were not touched.

4. THE REPRODUCIBILITY CLAUSE.

   `test_the_corrected_verdict_does_not_move_when_an_unrelated_commit_lands`. The first
   version of this test was INERT and an independent audit proved it: run 2 read the file
   run 1 had already scrubbed clean, so the two scores matched no matter what the rule did.
   With the byte-equality line removed and the flip-vs-mention rule broken, it still passed.

   Repaired, it now has teeth on its own:

     mutation: `if status == "closed" and old.get(key) != "closed"` -> `if status == "closed"`
     target:   that one test
     KILLED  by 1 test(s): 1 failed

   Both halves of the drop/keep predicate are gated too: dropping the drop is KILLED by 7
   tests, dropping the re-raise is KILLED by 4.

WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND, and what changed because of it.

Eight findings. Four MAJOR, and one was rejected on the evidence.

  The inert invariance test above -- the bead's headline property, unproven until fixed.

  Neither module's `main()` had a single test, and `main()` is the only surface the hooks
  use. Coverage 58 and 64 percent; now 98 and 94, with a CLI integration file covering all
  four exit codes the hook branches on.

  `_git` discarded git's exit status, so `closing_commit.py --root /tmp` returned UNKNOWN at
  exit 0. In the hook that becomes an empty newly-closed list, which skips the bead audit,
  the artifact-block gate AND the corrector. A silent fail-open in new gate code. Both
  modules now raise, both hooks DENY with a logged reason.

  REJECTED: that the UNKNOWN path silently exonerates a bead. It does not -- UNKNOWN reaches
  UNRESOLVED, scores 0, fails the gate. The auditor's live example `cairn-us2` is a
  deliberate false-close FIXTURE with status `tombstone`, and the census above found 0
  UNKNOWN. The real half of that finding, `git log` -> `git log --all`, was taken; verified
  by execution to leave all 24 resolutions byte-identical.

THREE HARNESS GATES FIXED ALONGSIDE, at the operator's instruction.

  `scripts/mutation_verdict.py` reported a FALSE KILL whenever the check never ran. It read
  ANY nonzero pytest exit as a detection, but 2 is an interruption, 3 an internal error, 4 a
  usage error and 5 no tests collected. Exit 5 is the dangerous one: aim `mutation-check.sh`
  at a path that collects nothing and every mutation reads KILLED, so a suite with no
  coverage reads as fully gated. A third verdict, INCONCLUSIVE, at its own exit code:

     $ printf 'no tests ran in 0.01s\n' | uv run python scripts/mutation_verdict.py 5
     EXIT=3  INCONCLUSIVE  pytest exited 5 without testing the mutation

   This is the mirror of the under-reporting bug fixed in the same file earlier the same
   day, and over-reporting is the worse direction. It had already misled one subagent.

  Three unbounded subprocess waits on the pre-commit path -- `bead_artifact_block.py` at the
  `git cat-file` resolver and the `br show` reader, `theater_patterns.py` at its `br show`.
  A wedged `br` hung the commit forever with nothing in `.check.log`: the shape cairn-ofk
  exists for, on a different surface. Each now carries a named timeout and denies on expiry.

  The amend gap. During `git commit --amend`, `git diff --cached` compares the index to a
  HEAD that already carries the close, so pre-commit saw no newly-closed bead and skipped
  all three gates while post-commit still pushed. `scripts/gate_marker.py` records the beads
  pre-commit gated and the HEAD it gated against, inside `.git`; post-commit reads it once,
  unlinks it, and denies the push when a closed bead is uncovered or the parent disagrees.

     check after amend: DENY the gate record was written for a commit sitting on
                        3a109053... and this one sits on 414e3e12...
     no record, a bead closed: DENY the pre-commit gates left no record, so cairn-fi7
                        closed without them

SUITE: 1744 at e41c047 -> 1835 here, exit 0.

NO-CLAIM

This does not prove either re-audited bead is correctly closed on the merits. It proves
their 650 FALSE-CLOSED readings were attribution artifacts and that both score 780 under
the corrected rule.

The evidence set is NOT fixed. `gather-evidence.sh` builds TOUCHED_FILES from the same
message grep, so a commit citing a bead id still donates its files to that bead's evidence.
Reaching it means a sixth fork. Owned by cairn-2fv, with the measurement it needs named.

The gate-coverage record attests to a parent and a bead list, not to the staged tree, so an
aborted commit leaves a record that a later --no-verify commit on the same parent closing
the same beads would consume. Owned by cairn-rof.

The bash in both hooks has no test and cannot have one here: `tests/conftest.py`'s
`isolation_guard` refuses a `bash` subprocess, so the Python holds the decisions at 94-98
percent coverage and the shell calling it sits at zero. Owned by cairn-pwj, which already
carries this thesis for CI, with a comment pointing at cairn-rof.

Ten mutation verdicts recorded by the auditor before INCONCLUSIVE existed were not re-run
under the new rule. Each reported a real pytest summary line, so each took the red-count
path and is unaffected -- but that is a reading, not a re-execution.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED

Three Opus subagents: an implementer, an auditor sharing none of its context, and a fixer.
The operator re-executed the closing-commit resolution, the correction of the historical
pass, idempotence by sha256 over all eight artifacts, all five verdict cases of the new
INCONCLUSIVE rule, both git-failure denials, four mutations including the repaired
invariance test, and the full gate; and read every diff.

The fixer retracted part of its own report unprompted: it had run the full suite twice, not
once, and read an empty `ps` result as proof its first run had died when that run was in
fact still alive and hung. Its green was therefore taken under contention. The operator's
own run, on a machine with no agent running, returned the same 1835 passed at exit 0 in
268 s -- inside the normal 215-291 s band, where a contended run measured 771 s earlier in
the session. Swap sat at 15.65 of 16 GB, so a further run risked manufacturing a contention
artifact rather than settling anything; CI on this commit is the clean-machine measurement.

That is a separation of hats within one session, not verification by another party.

title: Harness: project_theater_patterns is read by nothing, and its signature matches nothing
description:
audit-policy.yaml carries a project_theater_patterns section declaring
P-platform-skip-hides-a-gate, a MAJOR finding for `skipif\(sys\.platform` in
tests/**/*.py. Two independent reasons it produces nothing.

First, nothing reads the section. scripts/theater-scan.sh builds its findings from
a fixed list of scan_pattern calls written into the script; it sources no policy
file. The only mention of project_theater_patterns anywhere in the skill's scripts
is a comment in _load-policy.sh listing sections that "other consumers" read.

  $ grep -rn "project_theater_patterns" ~/.claude/skills/beads-compliance-and-completion-verification/scripts/
  _load-policy.sh:17:# Other YAML sections (parallelism, weights_by_type, project_theater_patterns,

Second, the signature does not match this repository even if it were read. Four
modules carry a platform skip and every one of them writes it across two lines:

  tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py:15:    sys.platform != "darwin",
  tests/integration/test_grounding_fs.py:12:        sys.platform != "darwin",
  tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py:14:         sys.platform != "darwin",
  tests/conformance/test_skill_contract.py:17:      sys.platform != "darwin",

The signature anchors on `skipif(` immediately followed by `sys.platform`, and
ripgrep is line-oriented, so it matches none of them. Wiring the section without
correcting the signature installs the appearance of a gate that reports zero
findings, which is worse than the section being visibly inert.

Both halves are the work: teach theater-scan.sh to read project_theater_patterns
and run scan_pattern for each entry, and write a signature that matches a skipif
whose arguments sit on the following line.

Consequence to size before starting: all four modules would raise a MAJOR finding,
which lowers anti_theater on every bead whose evidence cites them. Those beads are
closed. Decide whether the pattern applies to new work only or triggers a
re-audit, because a gate that retroactively reopens closed beads is a different
decision from one that catches the next unpaired skip.

The finding itself is real and owned: cairn-hcl exists because the M0 write
boundary is macOS-only and the degraded behavior is asserted nowhere. This bead is
about the gate, not the gap.

Surfaced by cairn-cue, which is about audit-policy.yaml binding what it claims to
bind. threshold, remediation_policy and weights_by_type bind; this section is the
one that does not.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
FROM cairn-cue (commit cac8ab6): an unverified half of the cross-bead attribution fix.

`score-bead.py`'s `score_cross_bead` now owns a synthesis finding by the row's subject
bead rather than by every id the row names:

  owned = [f for f in synthesis_findings if f.get("subject") == bead_id]

That is correct for the "Bead-graph truthfulness" rows, which are the only kind this
repository produces -- each says "bead A references non-closed bead B", and the defect,
if any, belongs to A.

`synthesis.md` has two other section kinds: "Integration gaps" and "Contradictions".
`synthesize.py` auto-detected none of either here, so no row of those kinds exists to
test the change against. The reading that a two-bead integration gap belongs to BOTH
beads is defensible, and under the new attribution only the subject would be charged.

This bead owns the audit's pattern surface, so it is the place to settle it: either
confirm that subject-attribution is right for all three section kinds, or make the
ownership rule per-kind. A fixture producing one Integration-gap row and one
Contradiction row would settle it directly.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
FROM cairn-oij (commit 58a1438): a subject shape the harness has no fixture for.

S2-12 gained an in-range arm that plants the declared seam and requires the reported
cross-check result to move. Three subject shapes are now covered by a real fixture:
a subject that cross-checks (toy_curve, PASS), one that hardcodes its in-range result
(nonconforming, FAIL), and one whose axis is not in the allowed set (witness, FAIL at
the first arm).

A fourth shape is not covered: a subject that DECLARES a seam and never calls it on
the in-range path. The arm would report the constant-result FAIL for it, because a
result that does not move is a result that does not move regardless of why. That is
the intended verdict, but it is inference from reading the code rather than a
measurement, and it is the shape closest to a real mistake -- a skill whose
cross-check is wired to the wrong call site looks conforming everywhere else.

A fixture for it is cheap: take the nonconforming fixture, give it a real comparison
against a seam it declares but does not use on the in-range path, and assert S2-12
FAILs with the constant-result reason rather than the no-seam one. The distinction
between those two reasons is what a reader of the matrix would act on.

This bead owns the harness's pattern surface, which is why it lands here rather than
in a bead of its own.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
CLOSED AT eecc40a. Three commits: bdcb9ad (the gate), 870f67f (a CLAUDE.md note the
implementer added and then judged below that section's bar), eecc40a (the exemption
pinned to a match count after I found it was whole-file).

BOTH HALVES OF THE DEFECT, REPRODUCED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BUILT

  Nothing read the section. `theater-scan.sh` builds findings from a fixed catalog
  written into the script and sources no policy file:

    $ grep -n "policy|yaml|_load-policy" .../scripts/theater-scan.sh
    0 matches   EXIT=1

  The section IS read by `subagents/theater-detector.md`, and neither the pre-commit
  path nor CI runs a subagent.

  The signature matched nothing. All four modules put the arguments on the next line,
  and ripgrep is line-oriented:

    $ /opt/homebrew/bin/rg -nH 'skipif\(sys\.platform' tests/
    EXIT=1

  (Bare `rg` here is rewritten to `grep`, which rejects the pattern outright; the
  absolute path is what settles it.)

NO SIXTH FORK

`scripts/theater_patterns.py` reads `audit-policy.yaml` and scans the tree;
`scripts/theater-patterns.sh` is the entry point; `scripts/check.sh:60` runs it, so the
pre-commit hook and CI both get it from one wire. The vendored skill is untouched, which
is the point of the bead this one came from.

STATED PLAINLY, BECAUSE IT WOULD BE EASY TO IMPLY OTHERWISE: these findings gate the
commit and reach NO dimension of the audit's score. `anti_theater` is computed by the
skill's `score-bead.py` from `theater.json`, which `theater-scan.sh` writes from its own
catalog. Nothing here moves that number. A fork would also have bound the section to one
bead's cited files rather than the tree, and would be reverted by the next upstream
update.

THE DECISION THE BEAD ASKED FOR

The bead asks whether the pattern applies to new work or triggers a re-audit. Decision:
new work. The four modules carrying platform skips represent a gap that is real, already
diagnosed, and already owned by an open bead -- cairn-hcl. Retroactively lowering
anti_theater on closed beads whose evidence cites them would reopen settled work over a
gap that has an owner, which is churn rather than safety. The value is prospective: a new
platform skip with no paired assertion is a claim that a gate ran when it did not, and
nothing caught that.

THE EXEMPTION, AND THE HOLE I FOUND IN MY OWN SPECIFICATION

First shape was whole-file, and I verified it at HEAD rather than reading the report:

  $ (append a second, linux-flavored skipif to tests/integration/test_grounding_fs.py)
  $ ./scripts/theater-patterns.sh
  EXIT=0   pass: 1 pattern(s) over 133 file(s)

So those four modules had become the one place in the repository where a new, unrelated
platform skip was invisible -- and the likeliest place someone would add one, being
already the platform-specific modules. The implementer's
`test_the_exemption_is_by_name_not_by_directory` proves a sibling in the same directory
fires, which is a real property and a different one.

The exemption is now pinned to a measured match count per path
(`audit-policy.yaml:206-214`), so the allowance cannot drift wider than the tree in
either direction. Both directions re-executed by me at eecc40a:

  GROWTH, a second skip in an already-exempt file:
  EXIT=2
    MAJOR P-platform-skip-hides-a-gate  tests/integration/test_grounding_fs.py:238
      the exemption covers 1 match(es) in this file; it carries 2. A skip added to an
      already-exempt file is invisible unless the count moves.

  DROP, the skip removed without lowering the count:
  EXIT=3
    P-platform-skip-hides-a-gate: tests/integration/test_grounding_fs.py is exempt for
    1 match(es) but no longer matches the signature and carries 0; lower matches to the
    real count so the allowance cannot absorb a new skip

  RESTORED:
  EXIT=0   pass: 1 pattern(s) over 133 file(s)

The four counts are measured rather than typed: a test re-measures the tree and compares
it to the file, and mutating one recorded count to 2 kills six tests.

The exemption also names `exempt_until_bead: cairn-hcl` and cannot outlive its owner. The
gate denies on an exemption naming no removing bead, on a removing bead already closed, on
an exempt path no file_glob reaches, and on a duplicate path.

THE GATE FIRED ON ITS OWN TEST FILE, AND WAS NOT EXEMPTED

The fixture text in `tests/unit/test_theater_patterns.py` is a literal platform skip, so
the first suite run went red. Exempting it would have widened the one list whose
narrowness those tests exist to hold, so the fixture is assembled at runtime instead
(`MARK = "skip" + "if"`).

PROVED ABLE TO FAIL

Seventeen mutations, all KILLED, including both sides of the count check off by one, the
growth check removed, the drop check removed, one recorded count wrong (6 tests), a bare
path accepted again, and a duplicate path accepted.

  $ scripts/check.sh          (run alone; load 6.23 before, 8.05 after)
  1698 passed, 8 warnings in 227.71s
  [check] all gates pass                              EXIT=0

1648 at 328e655 -> 1698, +50.

TWO FINDINGS THAT WERE PARKED HERE AND DID NOT BELONG

I described this bead as owning "the harness's pattern surface". That framing is too wide
-- it owns one policy section and one scanner -- and it attracted two findings that would
have been lost at this close. Both are rehomed:

  synthesis-row attribution for the Integration-gap and Contradiction section kinds ->
  cairn-fi7, which owns an attribution defect in the same forked scorer.

  the missing S2-12 conformance fixture, a subject declaring a seam it never calls ->
  cairn-m1-cqt.3, the planted fixture corpus bead, which is the mechanism that settles it.

NO-CLAIM

Nothing here verifies any behavior on Linux. The exempted gap is untouched and unmeasured,
which is the decision, not an oversight.

The gate fires on any non-exempt platform skip. It does not detect whether a skip is
PAIRED with an assertion naming the degraded behavior, which is what the rationale asks
for; pairing is not machine-checkable from the signature alone, and the finding text asks
the author for it.

The count compares totals, not positions, so a skip swapped one-for-one inside an exempt
file is invisible to it. That is a deliberate limit of a count and the reason the count
sits beside `exempt_until_bead` rather than replacing it.

`anti_theater` is claimed unchanged on inference from reading `theater-scan.sh` and
`score-bead.py`'s inputs, not from a before-and-after `single-bead-audit.sh` run.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED

Implemented by one subagent across two rounds, the second because I found the whole-file
hole myself. I reproduced both halves of the original defect, proved both new directions
against the real tree, read the exemption and the scan loop in the source, and took a
clean full suite on a quiet machine. I did not re-run the seventeen mutations. That is a
separation of hats within one session, not independent verification by another party.

title: M1: Mac/Linux parity — CI matrix, gp discovery, the Linux write boundary, and host-bound goldens
description:
WHY: the M0 write boundary is macOS-only, and so is the harness around it. CI made
that concrete rather than theoretical. `cairn.bundle.write_pin` and
`cairn.attest.init` set `stat.UF_APPEND` through `os.chflags`, and both test files
carry `pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform != "darwin")`. On any other platform
`_set_append_only` logs `append_only_unavailable` and returns False, so the pin and
the attestation file carry mode bits only: 0444 and 0644 under an owner who can
chmod them back. The gate still fails closed on a hash mismatch, but the artifacts
are no longer append-only, and nothing in the suite says so out loud on that
platform.

MEASURED on ubuntu-latest, run 32886786555, the first CI run this repo ever had.
The suite does not reach a single assertion:

- `cairn.pari.GP_BIN` is the literal string "/opt/homebrew/bin/gp"
  (src/cairn/pari.py:11). On Linux `apt-get install pari-gp` puts gp at /usr/bin/gp,
  so `env.gp_binary_sha256()` raises GpMissing during collection of
  tests/integration/test_runner.py and pytest stops with 1 error in 1.47s.
- ty reports `Module os has no member chflags` (tests/conftest.py:234) and
  `st_flags` on five more lines; both are macOS and BSD only. The types gate is red
  on Linux for that reason alone.
- tests/goldens/capabilities.golden pins "gp_bin": "/opt/homebrew/bin/gp", so the
  CLI contract golden cannot match anywhere else.

CI therefore runs on macos-latest (.github/workflows/ci.yml), which is the platform
M0 describes. That is a scope decision, not a fix: this bead owns making it a matrix.

ALSO MEASURED on macos-latest, run 32887773951, after the CI-only divergences were
removed: 1351 passed, and one failure that is not about Linux at all.
tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py::test_certificate_golden_recomputes_from_the_golden_transcript
fails on any machine but the one that generated the golden, because the certificate
binds `tool_digests.gp_binary_sha256` and every host has a different gp binary. The
golden is machine-bound by construction. That is content addressing behaving
correctly and a golden test that can never be portable; decide whether the fixture
scrubs the host-bound fields (tests/conftest.py already has `scrub` and SCRUB_RULES),
pins a vendored gp digest, or is marked local-only with the reason stated.

WHAT
- Resolve gp rather than hardcode it: discover the binary (PATH, with an explicit
  env override), keep its sha256 in the identity bundle, and let the identity differ
  per host, which is the intended behavior. Note the cost before starting:
  src/cairn/pari.py is in toy_curve.IDENTITY_SOURCES, so editing it bumps
  implementation_revision and the transcript and certificate goldens must be
  regenerated with their diffs read.
- The non-macOS arm of `_set_append_only`: `chattr +a` / `+i` on Linux, grounded by a
  probe the way the macOS arm was, or an explicit degraded deploy shape that the
  suite asserts out loud rather than skipping quietly.
- Make the host-bound goldens portable or explicitly local, per the finding above.
- Turn the CI job into a matrix over macos-latest and ubuntu-latest, both required.
  A platform that is skipped is a platform nobody is testing.

DONE WHEN
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs a matrix over macos-latest and ubuntu-latest and
  both legs are green on a pushed commit, with the run ids in the close comment.
- `uv run ty check src tests` is clean on both platforms.
- No test is skipped for platform reasons without an assertion elsewhere that names
  the degraded behavior; a skip that hides a missing write boundary is the failure
  this bead exists to remove.
- `scripts/check.sh` passes on a Linux checkout with no local edits.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: the Linux grounding table runs on a real Linux filesystem and every cell records its observed errno; the run and its raw output are pasted in the close comment.
- Positive: `cairn bundle pin` and `cairn attest init` on Linux either set the append-only attribute (asserted by reading it back) or log `append_only_unavailable` and the deploy shape is reported degraded by `cairn doctor`.
- Planted negative: on a platform without the attribute, a test asserts the artifacts ARE writable by their owner, so the weaker boundary is stated by a passing test rather than left to a skip.
- No-Claim: this bead does not add the second OS user; decision 8 defers that to M3 (cairn-m3-u7x). It answers only what the boundary is where `chflags` does not exist.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.7 (toy_curve self-test), a file this bead's work unblocks.

tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py carries
`pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform != "darwin", ...)`, matching
tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py. All 30 of its tests skip off macOS,
because the pinned_bundle fixture pins through the uappnd chflags bit.

That set includes every planted negative of the self-test, so on Linux the
self-test presently has integration coverage only through the unit files. When
the non-macOS arm of _set_append_only lands, this skipif is one of the marks to
revisit.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.16, one more module on the macOS-only list.

tests/conformance/test_skill_contract.py carries

  pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform != "darwin", ...)

for the same reason tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py does: its
module-scoped harness fixture calls bundle.write_pin, which sets the uappnd
chflags bit, and clears it in teardown with os.chflags(pin_path, 0). On Linux
the whole 44-case conformance sweep skips, which means the section 2 contract
is unchecked there.

Splitting the module was deliberate so the parity job has less to fix.
tests/conformance/test_clause_table.py holds the clause-table checks — ids
unique and ordered, no MUST check is a stub, COVERAGE.md matches CLAUSES, the
registry is well formed — carries no platform gate and runs anywhere, because
it reads no bundle, no substrate and no subprocess.

What the Linux arm needs is the pin mechanism, not the harness: every clause
check is platform-neutral once a gate bundle can be opened. The two fixture
subjects launch through cairn.runner as sys.executable subprocesses and read
nothing platform-specific.

One observation for the write boundary, not a claim about Linux. The in-child
environment dump that S2-11 reads shows the child holding exactly:

  CAIRN_HARNESS_MODE, CAIRN_HARNESS_SUBJECT, HOME, LANG, PATH, PYTHONPATH,
  TMPDIR, __CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING

runner.ENV_ALLOWLIST names PATH, HOME, LANG, LC_ALL, LC_CTYPE, TMPDIR and TZ, so
__CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING arrives from the macOS exec layer rather than from
child_env. A Linux child will not carry it, and any test that pins the exact key
set would fail there. The conformance check counts the variables and asserts no
CAIRN_DB prefix and no .sqlite value, so it is not sensitive to this.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
CORRECTION AND A PROBED FACT, 2026-08-27.

An earlier note on cairn-m1-cqt said this bead "cannot be verified on this machine at
all". That is false, and the operator caught it. OrbStack and Docker are running here,
and a Linux container answers the platform questions directly.

  $ docker run --rm --platform linux/arm64 python:3.14-slim python -c "..."
  platform        : linux
  has chflags     : False
  has UF_APPEND   : True

TWO THINGS THAT FALL OUT OF TEN SECONDS OF CONTAINER TIME.

`stat.UF_APPEND` EXISTS ON LINUX while `os.chflags` does not. The constant is defined
even though the syscall behind it is absent, so a platform guard written as
`hasattr(stat, "UF_APPEND")` would conclude Linux supports the append-only flag and
then fail at the call. `os.chflags` is the only honest discriminator.

The shipped code already guards on the right one -- `src/cairn/attest.py:130` and
`src/cairn/bundle.py:147` both test `hasattr(os, "chflags")` before reaching
`os.chflags(path, stat.UF_APPEND)`. Recorded as a confirmed-good property rather than
a defect, because the wrong version of that guard is the obvious way to write it and
a later reader may "simplify" toward the trap.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THIS BEAD. The Linux arm is more tractable than the deferral
implied. A container gives the Linux write boundary, gp discovery and the host-bound
goldens a real environment without a CI matrix, and the same image is what the matrix
would run. The honest reason this bead is deferred is that it is M1-scoped work, not
that the platform is unreachable from here.

Still unprobed, and named so nobody reads more into the above: whether PARI/gp
installs and behaves the same in that image, what the write boundary actually does on
Linux when `chflags` is absent (the degraded behavior this bead exists to assert), and
whether any golden is host-bound in a way a container changes.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
COST EVIDENCE FOR THE MATRIX DECISION, measured 2026-09-01.

This bead records that CI runs on macos-latest as a scope decision. Here is what that scope
decision costs, summing each run's created-to-updated interval from `gh run list`:

  30 runs listed          216 wall minutes    2161 billed at the macOS 10x rate
  3 runs on 2026-09-01     14.6 wall minutes   146 billed

The free tier is 2000 minutes a month. The 2026-08-27 exhaustion was 23 runs spending about
2020, and it cost five days with no CI verification at all: nothing closed on 2026-08-28 or
2026-08-29 was verified, and the backlog only cleared on 2026-09-01.

At the Linux 1x rate the same 216 wall minutes bill 216 and the quota is never approached. So
the Mac/Linux parity work this bead owns is not only a portability question; the runner rate
is the difference between a quota that lasts a month and one that lasts three weeks.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: the three Linux blockers measured on this bead are real and
unresolved -- the hardcoded `GP_BIN`, `ty` on `os.chflags`, and the host-bound goldens. A
runner switch without them does not collect a single test. The cost figure is an argument for
priority, not a shortcut past the work.

A SEPARATE, SMALLER LEVER available before any of that. `.githooks/post-commit` pushes every
bead-closing commit, so three beads closed within ten minutes started three runs; the
workflow's concurrency setting killed one of them, which is the mechanism working, but a batch
would not have started them. Whether a session pushes per close or once at the end is a policy
question independent of the platform, and closing several beads in one commit costs one run.

title: Harness: an unverifiable audit pass is reported as a false close
description:
One scorecard states both of these about cairn-8jm, four lines apart, in pass
2026-08-29T04-42-52Z:

  Denominator: UNVERIFIABLE -- only 425 of 1000 weight was measured, below the 450 this
               project requires. Unmeasured: docs_etc, test_depth, tests. A score over this
               base says nothing about the work.
  TOTAL 0 / 1000 -- UNVERIFIABLE, 425 of 1000 weight measured, below the 450 floor;
               no score is issued
  FALSE-CLOSED (status=closed, score=0 < threshold 700)
  Verdict: THEATER

It declares that no score is issued, then compares the placeholder zero to the threshold and
convicts the bead on the result. `minimum_measured_weight` exists to say "I cannot judge
this"; the false-closed line converts that into "I judged this and it is theater". Those are
different claims and only one of them is supported.

This is the third instance of one defect family in one session, after cairn-8jm (the audit's
silence rendered as a missing-items finding) and cairn-a30 (a doctor WARN rendered as a bead
scoring below threshold). Each time an absence is given the shape of a verdict.
`~/.claude/rules/absence-is-not-evidence.md` is the standing rule.

THE INVERSION THAT PRODUCES IT

Measured weight is the sum of the dimensions the deterministic pass could reach. In
single-bead stub mode Phases 4 and 6 are excluded by design, leaving implementation 200,
anti-theater 200, docs_etc 25 and cross-bead 25 -- 450, exactly the floor.

docs_etc is excluded, not zeroed, when the extractor finds no documentation, migration,
telemetry or feature-flag item in the bead body. That drops the measured base to 425 and puts
the bead under the floor.

So a bead whose body NAMES a doc artifact it never delivered scores 0 out of 25 and stays
verifiable at 450. A bead that names none at all becomes unverifiable and is convicted of
theater. Failing to deliver a named artifact is scored more kindly than not having one to
name. A bead about a shell gate and a Python classifier has no documentation deliverable, and
the audit has no way to say so.

WHAT IS AT STAKE

Any harness bead whose spec carries no non-code artifact cannot be closed through the
pre-commit gate, whatever its quality. cairn-8jm is the first; the shape is generic.

DONE WHEN
- An unverifiable pass is its own verdict, distinct from false-closed, and the scorecard does
  not compare a withheld score to a threshold.
- A decision, recorded, on whether an unverifiable verdict blocks a close. Both answers are
  defensible: blocking is honest about coverage and stops every no-doc bead; allowing lets a
  bead close on 425 of 1000 measured. The decision belongs to whoever owns the threshold, and
  the audit must state which was chosen.
- scripts/scorecard_coherence.py either catches the contradiction between "no score is
  issued" and "score=0 < threshold", or its scope is stated so that this is knowingly outside
  it. It reads the newest pass's scorecards to refuse a table that disagrees with its own
  denominator, and this scorecard disagrees with its own denominator in prose rather than in
  the table.

TEST PLAN

- tests/unit/test_scorecard_coherence.py -- an unverifiable scorecard that also carries a
  false-closed line is refused, and one that carries the unverifiable banner alone is not.
- tests/unit/test_audit_missing_items.py -- an unverifiable bead does not reach the
  debt-from-nothing verdict on the strength of a withheld score.

source: `scripts/scorecard_coherence.py` lines 1-161
source: `scripts/audit_missing_items.py` lines 1-366
test: `tests/unit/test_scorecard_coherence.py` lines 1-210
test: `tests/unit/test_audit_attribution.py` lines 1-328
