comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
OPERATOR DECISION, 2026-08-29: separate "n/a" from "unmeasured".

A dimension the extractor inspected and found empty has been measured. A dimension whose
phase never ran has not. Today both leave the numerator and the denominator, and that is the
conflation to remove.

  docs_etc: EXCLUDED -- n/a -- no non-code artifacts in spec
            the extractor looked and found none. A measurement.

  tests:    EXCLUDED -- Phase 4 ran in stub mode
            nothing looked. Silence.

Counting the first as measured restores the single-bead-stub base to 450 and the floor is
cleared without moving it. The alternatives were rejected: keeping the block would force a
named bypass on every harness bead with no documentation deliverable; letting an unverifiable
pass through would let anything the deterministic path cannot reach close freely; and
lowering minimum_measured_weight to 400 moves the cliff rather than removing it.

NOTED RISK, not dismissed. `unmeasured_dimensions: excluded` was cairn-exi's deliberate
answer to a bead that scored 975 with 775 of it awarded for having nothing to check. This
hands 25 of those points back. It is bounded to one dimension and only where the extractor
ran, which is the distinction cairn-exi was drawing in the first place, but the implementer
must confirm that the "Done." bead cairn-exi used as its subject does not clear the threshold
again under this change. If it does, the decision needs revisiting rather than shipping.

The false-closed line must also stop comparing a withheld score to the threshold, whatever
the denominator works out to. An unverifiable pass is its own verdict.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
CLOSED. The operator's decision shipped, narrowed by a measurement that the decision itself
required, and the narrowing is the substance of this close.

THE CONFIRMATION GATE FIRED, AND IT WAS RIGHT TO

The decision said to treat an "n/a" note as a measurement and a "WAIVED" note as silence, and
required confirming that cairn-6cp, the "Done." fixture cairn-exi used as its negative
control, does not clear the threshold again. Applied at the n/a PREFIX level it scored:

  cairn-6cp   1000 / 1000   GREEN VERIFIED

The first implementer stopped there rather than shipping, which is what the decision asked for.

WHY, AND IT IS NOT THE DIMENSION THE RISK NOTE ANTICIPATED. score-bead.py line 160 writes
"n/a -- no code artifacts in spec" for IMPLEMENTATION, weight 250 on a task bead, to a bead
naming two files that never existed. Line 648 writes the same prefix for docs_etc, weight 25.
The prefix-level reading hands back 275 points, not 25, and it is the 250 that carries the
negative control over the line: without it the measured base is 250 and 6cp stays under the
450 floor.

THE NARROWING, WHICH IS THE DECISION READ PROPERLY

The decision's own text bounds it: "It is bounded to one dimension" and "hands 25 of those
points back". 25 is exactly docs_etc's weight. NA_MEASURED_DIMENSIONS is frozenset({"docs_etc"}).
Measured under it, and re-derived by the session rather than taken from a report:

  cairn-6cp   0      UNVERIFIABLE, 250 of 1000 measured, unmeasured implementation/test_depth/tests
  cairn-8jm   867
  cairn-x72   833

The single-bead-stub base for a real code bead is restored to 450, the floor is not moved, and
the negative control stays convicted. cairn-6cp's card carries no FALSE-CLOSED line and its
verdict reads "No score was computed and no threshold was compared."

THE HALF THAT WAS NOT INDEPENDENT, AND WOULD HAVE DELETED A GATE

The bead calls the false-closed change unconditional. It is not, because
scripts/audit_attribution.py line 241 is the only thing that becomes the hook's exit code:

  failed = status == "closed" and bool(summary.get("false_closed"))

It blocks on that flag and nothing else. Stopping false_closed from firing on an unverifiable
pass, with no replacement, does not rename the block, it removes it -- and lets any bead the
deterministic path cannot reach close freely, which is verbatim the alternative the decision
rejected. So an unverifiable pass blocks under its own name: the scorer emits an
`unverifiable` flag and the attribution gate fails a closed bead carrying one, with a message
that names the unmeasured dimensions and does not claim a score was computed.

THE BLOCK WAS RENAMED, NOT WIDENED. Four historic beads come back UNVERIFIABLE under the new
rule; each was scored against the saved original scorer and all four were already blocked as
FALSE-CLOSED.

VERIFICATION, RE-EXECUTED BY THE SESSION

Four tests observed failing against the unfixed code before the fix. The end-to-end gate,
which is the acceptance criterion this bead exists for: single-bead-audit.sh on cairn-x72
exits 0 at 833 with no bypass, and the three cairn-owned gates each exit 0 --
audit_attribution OK, scorecard_coherence COHERENT, audit_missing_items 0 measured gaps.
scripts/check.sh 1958 passed, exit 0.
Each of the four parts reverted separately turns a test red.

A GAP THE IMPLEMENTER NAMED, CLOSED BY THE SESSION. Parts 1 and 2 live in the vendored fork
and no repo test covers them, so an upstream skill update would revert them silently.
.githooks/pre-commit greps for NA_MEASURED_DIMENSIONS and denies without it; the tripwire was
proven by mutating the marker and observing the denial, and the file restored byte-identical.
CLAUDE.md's fork bullet carries the change.

NO-CLAIM

scripts/audit_missing_items.py was made unverifiable-aware, which is a fifth change beyond
the four the bead names; the bead's own TEST PLAN would otherwise have passed against a
fixture while the script stayed broken. cairn-6cp's recorded status is tombstone rather than
closed, so audit_attribution's status guard never reaches it in a real pass; the probe used a
synthetic copy with the status rewritten. Whether a tombstoned bead should block is a
pre-existing question this change does not touch. The Part 1 and Part 2 probes share one JSON
line, so their isolations are not fully independent. cairn-x72's 833 came from the live audit
run rather than an independently scored copy. This close is CI-unverified at the time of
writing.

title: Harness: decide whether the pre-claim spec-quality gate runs, and at what threshold
description:
The vendored compliance skill ships `scripts/spec-quality-gate.sh`, a pre-claim gate
that scores a bead's spec out of 1000 before any work starts. Cairn does not run it.
It is fully deterministic, needs no subagent and no network, and is therefore
hook-eligible in the same way `scripts/bead-artifact-block.sh` is.

MEASURED 2026-08-26, running the unmodified script against this repo:

  cairn-m0-e0s.12    920      cairn-hcl      670
  cairn-m0-e0s.17    880      cairn-m1-cqt.6 610
  cairn-qn9          480      cairn-m1-cqt.1 540
  cairn-exi          460      cairn-fur      380
  cairn-cue          430      cairn-o0l      380

The split is not quality, it is shape. M0 implementation beads carry bulleted
acceptance criteria, named test types and a Done-when line, and land at 880 to 920.
Harness beads are written as prose and land at 380 to 480, which is the same failure
`cairn-exi` fixed on the completion side: a regex scorer cannot read prose.

THE ONE DIMENSION THAT PENALIZES DOING IT RIGHT

cairn-m0-e0s.12 scores 920 and loses exactly 80 of the missing 100 on
`Dependencies explicit`, 20/100, for '3 implicit dep phrase(s) with no explicit
Dependencies section'. That bead has real `br dep` edges. The scorer greps the body
for a `## Dependencies` heading or the literal string `br dep` and says so itself:
'heuristic; verify with `br dep list`'. Scoring the graph would need the graph; the
script reads a string instead.

So the gap from 920 to 1000 is a heading duplicating what the dependency graph
already holds authoritatively, and prose that duplicates a graph is prose that
drifts from it. A hard gate at 950 buys that duplication on every bead.

DONE WHEN

- A decision recorded on this bead, with its cost, on whether the gate runs at all,
  and if so whether at `--policy block` or `--policy advise`.
- If it runs: a cairn-owned wrapper beside `scripts/bead-artifact-block.sh`, never a
  sixth fork. `_load-policy.sh` reads only `threshold` and `remediation_policy`, so
  `spec-quality-gate.sh` inherits the completion audit's 700 unless the wrapper
  passes `--threshold` explicitly. One number cannot serve two different scales.
- The `Dependencies explicit` dimension either satisfied from the graph rather than
  the body, or its cost accepted in writing.
- Every currently-open bead re-scored, and the ones the chosen threshold would block
  listed by name, so the cost of adopting it is a number and not a guess.

NOT IN SCOPE: raising the completion-audit threshold. That is a different gate on a
different scale, and its ceiling is 850 for reasons recorded in `audit-policy.yaml`.

title: M0 — the real slice: substrate + exemplar skill + Tier-0 verifier + tier gate (40-bit toy curve end to end)
description:
WHY THIS MILESTONE EXISTS
Cairn is a research harness whose epistemics are immutable and whose strategy is mutable (PLAN §0; CLAUDE.md). M0 builds the one vertical slice everything else plugs into: a content-addressed substrate (SQLite + BLAKE3), one exemplar skill built end to end (content-addressed I/O, captured seed, known-answer self-test, declared cost profile), the Tier-0 verifier (`xP == Q` in a subprocess), and the tier gate with its gate bundle + pin. "Everything else plugs into this shape — get it right once, the verifier included." Build M0 before adding another design layer: a running 40-bit slice reveals more than more architecture.

OPERATOR DECISIONS THAT BIND M0 (confirmed 2026-08-21; recorded in PLAN §16)
(1) PARI-only arithmetic at M0 with the BSGS-vs-SEA *algorithm* cross-check through 50 bits; the gmpy2 Hasse-interval BSGS enters as the *implementation* axis at M1.
(2) One 60-bit rho measured with cypari2 at M0 (bead m0-rho60-measure = cairn-m0-e0s.15); a compiled baseline is funded at M1 only if the interpreted rung cannot finish inside the Tier-1 budget.
(5) Skill yanks and `salt` issuance are human-only, like waivers — at M0 the `yank_records`/`salts` rows therefore carry the human-path digest+offset columns (schema only; behavior M1).
(8) No separate OS user for the orchestrator before M3; at M0 the gate-bundle pin and the attestation file are protected by file mode/flags only, and the grounding brief records exactly what that does and does not refuse (probed 2026-08-21 on macOS 26.6/APFS: mode 0644 + `uappnd` lets the owner append and refuses overwrite, `r+`, truncate AND `chmod` while the flag stands; 0444 + `uappnd` refuses append too, so the attestation file is 0644+uappnd and the pin is 0444+uappnd; the owner can still `chflags nouappnd` — the one-user gap).
(9) A ticket carries its gate-bundle hash; a mismatch re-mints the ticket.

STACK FACTS M0 STANDS ON (probed on this Mac 2026-08-21; research/grounding/pari-sage-toy-curve-backend.md)
PARI/GP 2.17.4 at /opt/homebrew/bin/gp (the shell has `alias gp='git push'` — always use the full path); cypari2 2.2.4 bundles libpari 2.17.2 and produced bit-identical p,a,b,n,tries to gp for the toy-curve search; `ellcard` is milliseconds through 50 bits, ≈75 ms/curve at 60 bits and overflows the default 8 MB PARI stack (use `pari.allocatemem(64_000_000)` / `gp -s 64M`); gp exits 0 on fatal errors (1/0, stack overflow) with the message on stderr, zero-fills missing arguments, and writes nothing to stderr on a successful quiet run (so the verifier's empty-stderr accept predicate is satisfiable); the PARI PRNG state is advanced by `ellsea(E)` and by 60-bit `ellcard`/`ellsea(E,1)` but not by ≤ 50-bit `ellcard`, so `toy_curve` pins its call sequence (cairn-m0-e0s.6); under SQLite's rollback journal only `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` blocks a reader (the WAL probe's control arm, cairn-m0-e0s.2); Sage absent; elan/lean absent; gp's own startup needs more than 2 MB of PARI stack (`gp -q -f -s 2M` exits 1 at startup with `### Errors on startup, exiting...` on stdout and the overflow message on stderr) while `verify.gp` on the 60-bit instance prints OK at every ceiling ≥ 3M including the 8 MB default because `verify()` never calls `ellcard` — so the verifier's forced-crash fixture is the bundle script's `crash_selftest(p,a,b)` entry (a 60-bit `ellcard` under `8M`: rc 0, empty stdout, overflow on stderr; cairn-m0-e0s.8/.11), never `verify()` at 8M; a file carrying `uappnd` cannot be unlinked or renamed by its owner while the flag stands (EPERM), so every test that flags a file under tmp_path clears the flag in teardown; CPython's `Popen.communicate()` reaps the child through `wait()`, so the runner captures stdout/stderr to files and reaps with `os.wait4` alone (cairn-m0-e0s.9). M0 re-executes the facts it relies on as tests and records the rest (WAL, busy timeout, append-only flag, write boundary) — bead m0-grounding-probes (cairn-m0-e0s.2).

DONE WHEN (PLAN §13 M0):
- the exemplar skill `toy_curve(bits, seed)` runs on a 40-bit toy curve; a deterministic M0 fixture (an integration fixture, not a second research skill) derives `x` and `Q = xP` from that output; the subprocess verifier accepts that pair, rejects a one-coordinate and a one-scalar negative fixture, classifies a forced backend crash as FAIL, and refuses — before the subprocess spawns — a submission that names its own `(P, Q)` rather than the statement node's;
- the generator output, derivation receipt, verifier result and gate-run record are hashed, self-tested, cost-tagged substrate nodes;
- the tier gate refuses a fixture launch declaring a tier two above its ticket and records `TierRefused`; a gate run against a bundle whose hash differs from the pin fails closed;
- a write to the pin and a write to the attestation file, each attempted as the orchestrator's process user, are refused by the operating system, and a `review_verdict` row whose digest matches no attestation record is absent to `justify`;
- `justify` returns STRONG-EMPIRICAL from a synthetic `ladder_table` evidence node with verdict KEEP whose attempt carries a passed reproducibility record, returns the CONJECTURE ceiling for the same table with that record absent or its grade `AuditOnly`, returns a coverage violation when the table's population does not cover the statement's scope, and returns a lattice violation when a synthetic `statistical` node is offered for PROVEN, against a synthetic statement hash;
- a blob unreachable from the roots table is collectable while a rooted one is not;
- the first gate self-tests run before the gates: the verifier's planted `xP ≠ Q` and forced-crash fixtures and the canonicalizer's known-answer vectors for both keys.

SCHEMA-ONLY AT M0 (behavior exercised at M1): escrow reserve/spend/release, yank reach and `disowned` propagation, and the process-tree form of the budget ceiling — M0's runner already enforces the ceiling on the direct child's wall clock (4× the declared expectation, status `BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, cairn-m0-e0s.9). M0 has a fixture writing and reading each such column. A behavior no M0 test exercises is architecture, not a slice.

ENGINEERING RULES FOR EVERY CHILD BEAD
- Integration test first (real PARI via cypari2, real gp subprocess, real SQLite file), unit tests second: unit tests cover the pure predicates (canonical encoding, the verifier's pre-spawn validator and accept predicate, the tier-gate predicate, `justify`'s coverage comparator and kind→class map, the runner's status mapping); e2e is `tests/e2e/test_m0_slice.py`. No mock may stand in for the gate under test; a planted fault (a monkeypatched backend answer, a killed child) is not a mock of the gate.
- Logging: one logger (`src/cairn/log.py`, bead cairn-m0-e0s.1) used by every CLI and every gate decision; each record names the step, the input hashes, the `gate_runs` row id where one exists, the verdict with its reasons and the timing; `--log DEBUG` (or `CAIRN_LOG=DEBUG`) adds subprocess argv and stdin/stdout/stderr digests; tests assert on the log records wherever a verdict is involved (pytest caplog), so a silent gate is a failing test.
- Python via `uv` only (`uv run pytest`, `uv add`); never bare pip/python; subprocesses use `sys.executable`.
- CLI convention (defined once in cairn-m0-e0s.1): every `cairn` subcommand takes the global options `--db` (default `var/substrate.sqlite`), `--bundle` (`deploy/gate-bundle.sqlite`), `--pin` (`deploy/gate-bundle.pin`), `--attest` (`deploy/attestations.log`) and `--log LEVEL`; no subcommand spells its own variant of these paths.
- Zero explanatory comments in code; names carry meaning.
- Every child carries a positive observable, a planted negative (a fixture that must FAIL), and a No-Claim line (what green does not prove).
- Closure of a child is a claim until its commands are re-executed at close; paste command + output in the close comment. The epic closes only when `uv run pytest` is green on a fresh clone and `uv run cairn m0-run --bits 40 --seed 1` (bead m0-e2e-slice = cairn-m0-e0s.14) produces the four nodes.

SHARED FIXTURES (named once, used by several beads): `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` — the 60-bit (p,a,b,n,P) that the grounding brief's bench.gp yields at bits=60 seed=1, generated once with gp and committed by cairn-m0-e0s.1; the stack-fact test (.1), the verifier's 60-bit and forced-crash tests (.8), the gate plan's crash fixture (.11) read it, and cairn-m0-e0s.6 asserts `toy_curve(60, 1)` reproduces it. `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` — one brief with sections written by .2 (stack facts), .6 (tries table), .15 (rho at 60 bits); .8 adds the `verify()`-OK-at-3M/8M/64M row to .2's gp-facts section, since `verify.gp` is .8's file.

CLI CONTRACT (binding on every subcommand bead; defined in cairn-m0-e0s.17, derived from /agent-ergonomics-and-intuitiveness-maximization-for-cli-tools): subcommands register through `cli.register(name, configure, run, *, summary, read_only, json, dangerous, gating, aliases, dry_run_default)` so `cairn capabilities --json` is generated from the registry (`dangerous=True` names its `gating` flag, which the registry adds to the parser and `main` refuses pre-run when absent — unless `dry_run_default=True`, which leaves `run` to perform the dry run itself and gate only its irreversible branch: the `gc`, `bundle` and `doctor` shapes); stdout is data and stderr is diagnostics; `--json` on every read-side command emits exactly one JSON document with `schema_version`; exit codes come from `cairn/exits.py` (0 OK, 1 USER_INPUT, 2 GATE_REFUSED, 3 ENVIRONMENT, 4 BACKEND, 5 CONFLICT; the doctor's own dictionary in cairn-m0-e0s.18); every refusal raises `CliError` with a copy-pasteable `next_command`; argparse `suggest_on_error=True`; dangerous operations (gc, bundle pin/build over an existing artifact, attest init over an existing file) are gated behind `--yes`/`--force` and name the safe alternative; no ANSI, no prompts, no TUI; `--help` everywhere exits 0 and names `--json`, `capabilities`, `robot-docs`; `cairn robot-docs` is the in-tool agent handbook; `cairn doctor` (cairn-m0-e0s.18, /world-class-doctor-mode-for-cli-tools) is the read-only-by-default self-diagnosis with detect-then-fix, a single `mutate()` chokepoint, verbatim backups and `undo <run-id>` — an agent runs it first when any command refuses. Registering a subcommand moves the contract goldens: the registering bead regenerates `tests/goldens/capabilities.golden` and `help_top.golden` and adds `help_<name>.golden` (`UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest tests/unit/test_cli_contract.py -k 'golden or help'`) in its own commit; `tests/unit/test_cli_contract.py::test_json_commands_emit_exactly_one_document_on_stdout` is parametrized over every `json=True` command while cairn-m0-e0s.17's text scopes that assertion to `env`, `kat`, `capabilities` — the first bead registering a `json=True` command whose bare `<cmd> --json` cannot exit 0 (`measure`, `selftest`, `justify`, …) narrows that parametrize to those three names in its commit and asserts its own one-document output in its owning integration test. Subcommand inventory at M0 close, each registered by its owning bead: `env` (.1), `kat` (.3), `capabilities`/`robot-docs` (.17), `measure toy-curve-tries|rho60` (.6/.15), `selftest` (.7), `startup-scan` (.9), `bundle build|pin|show` and `attest init|append` (.10), `gate selftest` (.11), `justify` (.12), `gc` (.13), `m0-run` (.14), `doctor` (.18).

NOT IN M0: the ladder, baseline skills, Lean gate, workers, orchestrator, parallel tracks (M1–M4 epics). The research tree is never pre-decomposed into beads (CLAUDE.md).

TEST PLAN (shapes) — ENGINEERING RULES ADDED FOR EVERY CHILD BEAD
- Layer discipline: pure functions are unit tests in `tests/unit/` (the canon encoder/decoder, the coverage comparator, the accept-predicate truth table, the tier-gate predicate, the runner's status mapping, gate-plan validation, GC reachability); anything touching gp, SQLite, PARI, file modes/flags or a subprocess is integration in `tests/integration/`; `cairn m0-run` is e2e in `tests/e2e/`. Pure modules are pyramid-shaped (unit-dominant); gate/CLI modules are trophy-shaped (integration-dominant).
- No fake-unit tests: a unit test that monkeypatches three or more boundaries is an integration test in disguise — promote it to `tests/integration/` against the real components or delete it.
- Parametrize failure paths instead of duplicating tests: every refusal/violation/trigger table is one `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over (input, expected reason) with `match=` on every raise; two tests differing only in data are merged.
- No cross-layer redundancy: each known-answer vector is asserted exactly once, in unit (`tests/unit/test_canon.py`, `tests/unit/test_claims_kat.py`); integration and e2e tests assert behavior, never re-assert KAT values.
- Before closing a child, run `/optimal-tests --audit <its test files>` and act on every finding; the audit's triage table is pasted in the close comment beside the test output.
- Structured test logging: `tests/conftest.py` (cairn-m0-e0s.1) installs an autouse `json_test_log` fixture that routes `src/cairn/log.py` records to `tmp_path/test.log.jsonl` as JSON lines — every `cairn.log` record as `{ts, level, step, event, …fields}` (ids/hashes, verdict, reasons, wall_ms are fields) plus `phase: start|end` marker records carrying the test nodeid and `wall_ms` — plus a `db_snapshot(conn_or_path, label)` helper (a `sqlite3.Connection` or a DB path, so a `Substrate` passes its path or connection) writing `{event:'db_snapshot', label, counts:{table: n}}`; the file is attached to the pytest report on failure; every integration test that touches the substrate calls `db_snapshot` at least once after its act phase.
- Factories: `tests/factories.py` (cairn-m0-e0s.5) holds realistic synthetic builders — `claim_statement(family, size, assumptions, cost_model, seed)`, `hypothesis_object(...)`, `evidence_node(kind, target_statement_hash, population, assumptions, verdict=None, repro=None, producer=...)`, `ladder_table_keep(statement, population, repro_passed=True)`, `repro_record(attempt_id, passed=True)`, `review_verdict(statement_hash, verdict='approve', ...)`, `gate_run(...)`, `ticket(...)`, `selftest_summary(origins, randomized_arm, cross_check)`, `instance_from_vector('curve60_seed1')` (the signatures cairn-m0-e0s.5 defines) — producing canon-valid objects with a per-test seed; used by cairn-m0-e0s.5, .10, .12 (and the synthetic statement node of .14); tests never hand-roll these dicts.
- Isolation: every test runs under tmp_path only; `tests/conftest.py` autouse `isolation_guard` fixture snapshots the repo's `deploy/` and `var/` trees — and `.doctor/` once cairn-m0-e0s.18 lands — (paths, sizes, mtimes) before and after each test and fails the test on any delta; it wraps `subprocess.Popen` with a spy (not a mock — the real Popen is called) that fails the test if `argv[0]` is anything but `sys.executable` or `cairn.pari.GP_BIN`; it scrubs `CAIRN_DB*` from `os.environ` for the test's duration.
- Mock policy: `monkeypatch` is allowed only as declared fault injection inside a skill's own seam — the `cairn.pari.ellsea` wrapper returning n+2 (cairn-m0-e0s.6), a fixture skill that exits 3 or sleeps (cairn-m0-e0s.9), a missing `GP_BIN` path (cairn-m0-e0s.1) — never as a stand-in for gp, SQLite, PARI, the bundle, the pin, the attestation file or any gate under test; a spy that calls through and records is not a mock; `tests/unit/test_no_mocks_in_integration.py` greps `tests/integration/` and `tests/e2e/` for `unittest.mock`/`MagicMock`/`mocker.patch` and fails on any hit.
- Property-based and fuzz tests use Hypothesis only (dev dependency, profiles pinned in `tests/conftest.py`, cairn-m0-e0s.1; atheris does not build on this Mac — probed 2026-08-21, its wheel needs a custom libFuzzer clang — so it is omitted); every metamorphic relation names the planted mutant it kills in `tests/mutants/<module>_mutants.py`, and a relation that kills no mutant is deleted; every fuzz target has a seed corpus under `tests/fuzz_corpus/<target>/` holding the bead's planted negatives, replayed as `@example`s before random generation, with ≥ 500 examples per target under the `ci` profile.
- Goldens: known-answer vectors and committed curve rows live under `tests/vectors/`; frozen transcripts, certificate values and the bundle hash under `tests/goldens/`; `tests/goldens/PROVENANCE.md` records, per golden, the generator command, tool versions and a volatility note (canon/claims KATs and the bundle hash are deterministic and platform-independent; the CURVE60 vector, the toy-curve rows and the environment manifest depend on libpari/platform); `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest` regenerates, anything else fails on a difference with a unified diff, `*.actual` is gitignored, and a regenerated golden lands only in an attributed commit naming the reason — for the self-test floor and certificate (cairn-m0-e0s.7) this is PLAN §2's rule that only an attributed update may raise the floor or re-mint the certificate.

title: M0: uv project scaffold + real-PARI smoke test (cypari2 in-process + gp subprocess + 60-bit stack fact)
description:
WHY: every later bead runs real PARI through two builds — cypari2 in-process for skills, /opt/homebrew/bin/gp as the verifier subprocess — and real SQLite. Nothing downstream is testable until the toolchain is pinned and a real call succeeds under `uv run`.

WHAT
- `uv init --package` layout: `pyproject.toml` (name `cairn`, Python ≥3.14 — cypari2 2.2.4 ships a 3.14 wheel per the grounding brief), `src/cairn/`, console script `cairn` (argparse is enough).
- Deps: `cypari2` (bundles libpari 2.17.2), `blake3`; dev: `pytest`. `gmpy2` is added at M1 only (operator decision 1).
- Dirs: `tests/integration/` (real PARI/gp/SQLite; the default suite), `tests/unit/`, `tests/e2e/`, `tests/vectors/`, `bundle/` (gate-bundle source), `deploy/` (built bundle + pin + attestation file; gitignored except a README), `var/` (runtime DBs; gitignored). `.gitignore`: `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, `var/`, `deploy/*.sqlite`, `deploy/*.pin`, `deploy/*.log`.
- `src/cairn/pari.py`: one shared cypari2 handle; `pari.allocatemem(64_000_000, silent=True)` exactly once at import (the 60-bit `ellcard` overflows the 8 MB default — PROVEN by probe; `silent=True` keeps PARI's stack-size notice off the harness's stderr, as the grounding brief's `bench_cypari2.py` does); `GP_BIN = "/opt/homebrew/bin/gp"` with an existence check raising a typed error; `pari_versions()` returning `pari.version()` and the cypari2 version (they feed the environment-manifest digest in bead m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3); thin wrappers `ellcard(E)` / `ellsea(E, early_abort)` so a later test can plant a disagreement at one seam (cairn-m0-e0s.6), and `ellorder(E, P)` — the point-order call the self-test's postconditions and its zero-call spy go through (cairn-m0-e0s.7). Never call gp through a shell.
- `src/cairn/cli.py`: argparse entry for the `cairn` console script; the global options `--db` (default `var/substrate.sqlite`), `--bundle` (`deploy/gate-bundle.sqlite`), `--pin` (`deploy/gate-bundle.pin`), `--attest` (`deploy/attestations.log`) and `--log LEVEL` are defined once in a shared parent parser attached to the top-level parser and, through `parents=`, to every subparser — so `cairn --db X m0-run …` and `cairn m0-run … --db X` both parse to one resolved namespace — and every subcommand (`--version`, `kat`, `selftest`, `measure`, `bundle`, `attest`, `gate`, `justify`, `gc`, `m0-run`, registered by their own beads) reads them from there; no subcommand defines its own spelling of these paths (a built bundle is written to `--bundle`, its pin to `--pin`, `attest init` creates `--attest` — cairn-m0-e0s.10).
- `src/cairn/log.py`: the one logger every CLI and gate decision uses — structured records on stderr `{ts, step, ids/hashes, verdict, reasons, wall_ms}`; level from `--log LEVEL` or `CAIRN_LOG` (default INFO); DEBUG adds subprocess argv and stdin/stdout/stderr BLAKE3 digests; never logs substrate paths into a skill's environment. Tests assert on records via pytest caplog.
- Shared fixture: `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` = `{bits:60, seed:1, p, a, b, n, P:[x,y]}` as decimal strings, generated ONCE in gp with EXACTLY the call sequence cairn-m0-e0s.6 pins for bits > 50 (the PARI PRNG state is advanced by `ellsea(E,1)` and by 60-bit `ellcard`, so any other call order yields a different curve — probed 2026-08-21): `setrand(1); p = randomprime([2^59, 2^60]); tries = 0; while(1, a = random(p); b = random(p); if((4*a^3 + 27*b^2) % p == 0, next); tries++; E = ellinit([a,b], p); n = ellsea(E, 1); if(n && isprime(n), break)); if(ellcard(E) != n, error("confirm")); P = random(E)` run as `/opt/homebrew/bin/gp -q -f -s 64M gen60.gp`; the grounding brief's mode-1 row predicts `tries = 45` at seed 1 and the file records it; committed with `origin: author_supplied`, the gp script (`tests/vectors/gen60.gp`) and the tries count in the file; the stack-fact smoke test (c) below, the verifier's 60-bit and forced-crash tests (cairn-m0-e0s.8) and the gate plan's crash fixture (cairn-m0-e0s.11) read it; cairn-m0-e0s.6 asserts `toy_curve(60,1)` reproduces it bit-for-bit.
- Smoke tests (integration, `tests/integration/test_smoke.py`):
  (a) cypari2: `ellinit([-3,1],5)` → `ellcard` = 7 (PARI user manual usersch3.tex:29031-29032, upstream_vendored);
  (b) gp subprocess: `subprocess.run([GP_BIN,"-q","-f","-s","64M"], input="print(ellcard(ellinit([-3,1],5)))")` → stdout `7`, rc 0;
  (c) stack fact: `ellcard` on the committed 60-bit curve (`tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json`) succeeds under allocatemem (cypari2) and under `gp -s 64M` and equals the vector's `n`; control: the same under `gp -s 8M` fails with a stack-overflow message on stderr and rc 0 (the gp exit-0-on-fatal fact).
- Unit tests (`tests/unit/test_pari_module.py`): `run_gp` builds argv `[GP_BIN,"-q","-f","-s",<stack>]` and passes `shell=False`; `run_gp(..., timeout_s=0.001)` on a good input raises `GpTimeout` and leaves no zombie (`os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)` raises `ChildProcessError` afterwards); the global CLI options parse with their defaults for every registered subcommand and parse to the same values whether placed before or after the subcommand token; a missing `GP_BIN` (monkeypatched path) raises the typed error before any spawn; `log.py` emits a parseable record at INFO and adds digests only at DEBUG.
- `uv run cairn --version` prints the version; `uv run cairn --version --log DEBUG` emits at least one structured record on stderr.

DESIGN: the PARI handle lives in one module so allocatemem runs once; all gp invocations go through `cairn.pari.run_gp(args, stdin, *, timeout_s)` returning (rc, stdout, stderr) — on timeout it kills the child, reaps it and raises `GpTimeout` (the verifier maps that to `FAIL timeout`, cairn-m0-e0s.8) — so later beads share one spawn path; all logging goes through `cairn.log.get(step)` so every bead's records have one shape.

TEST PLAN (shapes)
- Dev dependencies: `uv add --dev pytest hypothesis` (Hypothesis 6.165.x installs cleanly under Python 3.14 on this Mac — probed 2026-08-21; atheris does not: its build needs a custom libFuzzer clang, so Hypothesis is the only fuzz/property engine at M0 and no atheris target exists anywhere in M0).
- `tests/conftest.py` (created here, shared by every bead): Hypothesis profiles `settings.register_profile('ci', max_examples=500, deadline=None, print_blob=True)` and `settings.register_profile('dev', max_examples=50, deadline=None)`, loaded from `HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE` (default `ci`); `.hypothesis/` gitignored; the autouse `isolation_guard` fixture (snapshot of `deploy/` and `var/` before/after each test — any delta fails; a call-through spy on `subprocess.Popen` failing the test when `argv[0]` is neither `sys.executable` nor `cairn.pari.GP_BIN`; `CAIRN_DB*` scrubbed from the environment); the autouse `json_test_log` fixture routing `cairn.log` records to `tmp_path/test.log.jsonl` with phase/step/wall_ms and the `db_snapshot(substrate, label)` helper; the golden harness `assert_golden(name, text)` reading `tests/goldens/<name>.golden` — or `tests/vectors/<name>` when `name` ends in `.json`, since the KAT and row vectors (`canon_kat.json`, `claims_kat.json`, `toy_curve_rows.json`, `curve60_seed1.json`; cairn-m0-e0s.3/.5/.6 and this bead) live under `tests/vectors/` and compare through the same harness — rewriting it when `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` is set, otherwise failing with a unified diff and writing `<name>.actual` beside it (gitignored); and `load_vector(name)` for `tests/vectors/*.json`.
- Golden: `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` is a golden of volatility 3 — deterministic under pinned PARI 2.17.4 / libpari 2.17.2 and the pinned call sequence, platform-dependent only through libpari's PRNG, so a libpari bump may legitimately move it; `tests/goldens/PROVENANCE.md` (created here) records its generator command (`/opt/homebrew/bin/gp -q -f -s 64M tests/vectors/gen60.gp`), gp/libpari versions, date and that note; regeneration is `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest tests/integration/test_smoke.py -k curve60` followed by an attributed commit naming the libpari version; without the env var the smoke test (c) fails when gp's live output differs from the file.
- Harness self-test `tests/unit/test_golden_harness.py`: `assert_golden` on a temp golden differing from its actual fails without `UPDATE_GOLDENS` (the failure message carries a unified diff) and rewrites the file with `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1`; `isolation_guard` fails a test body that creates a file under `deploy/` and one that spawns `/bin/echo` (both exercised through `pytester` so the guard's own failure is observed, not inferred).
- `tests/unit/test_no_mocks_in_integration.py` (created here; the epic's mock policy): greps `tests/integration/` and `tests/e2e/` for `unittest.mock`, `MagicMock` and `mocker.patch` and fails on any hit; its own planted negative, through `pytester`, is a temp integration file holding `from unittest.mock import MagicMock` that the check must flag.
- Layer: everything here is integration except `test_pari_module.py`, `test_golden_harness.py` and `test_no_mocks_in_integration.py` (unit).
- The conformance harness (cairn-m0-e0s.16) is a consumer of this conftest (same profiles, same guard, same log fixture).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_smoke.py tests/unit/test_pari_module.py -q` green; three smoke tests visible: cypari2 ellcard=7, gp subprocess prints 7, 60-bit ellcard on the committed vector succeeds under the 64 MB stack and matches the vector's `n`; `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` committed with its generating gp script (`tests/vectors/gen60.gp`) and `tries: 45` (the grounding brief's mode-1 row; a different count means the call sequence drifted from the one cairn-m0-e0s.6 pins, and the smoke test asserts the count); `uv run cairn --version --log DEBUG` prints the version and one structured log record.
- Planted negative: 60-bit `ellcard` under `gp -s 8M` must fail with a stack-overflow message on stderr and rc 0, asserted as the expected failure shape; if it unexpectedly succeeds the test fails (the stack fact changed and the verifier's stack ceiling needs re-grounding); a monkeypatched missing `GP_BIN` must raise the typed error with zero spawns; `run_gp(..., timeout_s=0.001)` must raise `GpTimeout` (a returned (rc, stdout, stderr) there fails the test).
- `grep -r "which gp\|'gp'" src/` finds nothing; the only gp path is `cairn.pari.GP_BIN`.
- No-Claim: green proves the toolchain loads and one known curve order computes; it proves nothing about any skill, gate or timing profile; the 60-bit vector is author-generated (its order is re-checked by the test, not vendored).
- `tests/conftest.py` registers the Hypothesis `ci` (500 examples, no deadline) and `dev` profiles and loads `ci` by default (`uv run python -c "import tests.conftest; from hypothesis import settings; print(settings.default.max_examples)"` prints 500 — importing the conftest loads the `ci` profile; without that import Hypothesis's own default prints 100, probed 2026-08-21 on 6.165.10); `uv run pytest --fixtures -q` lists `isolation_guard`, `json_test_log`, `assert_golden` and `load_vector`; `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_no_mocks_in_integration.py -q` green, and its `pytester` negative flags the planted `MagicMock` import.
- `tests/unit/test_golden_harness.py` green: a differing golden fails `assert_golden` without `UPDATE_GOLDENS` and is rewritten with it; `*.actual` and `.hypothesis/` are gitignored; `tests/goldens/PROVENANCE.md` holds the `curve60_seed1.json` row (command, gp/libpari versions, volatility 3 note).
- Planted negative (harness): through `pytester`, a test writing under `deploy/` and a test spawning `/bin/echo` are each failed by `isolation_guard` (a green result there fails this bead).
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment, so the compliance audit can re-run it without reading the session.
notes:
BEAD ALIASES → IDS (the descriptions name beads by alias; these are the br ids): m0-scaffold-smoke = cairn-m0-e0s.1; m0-grounding-probes = cairn-m0-e0s.2; m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3; m0-substrate-core = cairn-m0-e0s.4; m0-claims-schema = cairn-m0-e0s.5; m0-toy-curve-skill = cairn-m0-e0s.6; m0-skill-selftest-cert = cairn-m0-e0s.7; m0-tier0-verifier = cairn-m0-e0s.8; m0-skill-runner-receipt = cairn-m0-e0s.9; m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate = cairn-m0-e0s.10; m0-gate-plan-selftests = cairn-m0-e0s.11; m0-justify = cairn-m0-e0s.12; m0-gc-roots = cairn-m0-e0s.13; m0-e2e-slice = cairn-m0-e0s.14; m0-rho60-measure = cairn-m0-e0s.15; m1-ladder = cairn-m1-cqt.1; m1-baseline-skills = cairn-m1-cqt.2; m1-planted-corpus = cairn-m1-cqt.3; m1-budget-escrow-yank = cairn-m1-cqt.4; m1-formalization-gate = cairn-m1-cqt.5; m1-worker-dispatch-canary = cairn-m1-cqt.6; m1-human-queue-review = cairn-m1-cqt.7; m1-router-ledger-hunt-repro = cairn-m1-cqt.8.

TOOLCHAIN FACT (probed 2026-08-21 in a scratch uv project): ~/.config/uv/uv.toml sets a corporate Artifactory index as default and it times out off-network; the cairn pyproject.toml must pin PyPI itself:
[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "pypi"
url = "https://pypi.org/simple"
default = true
With that, `uv add cypari2 blake3` and `uv add --dev pytest` resolve (Python 3.14.0 arm64, cypari2 2.2.4 / libpari 2.17.2, blake3 1.0.9); cypari2 has no `__version__` — read versions via importlib.metadata; `pari.allocatemem(64_000_000)` prints a line unless silent=True.

CURVE60 KNOWN ANSWER (probed 2026-08-21 with exactly the gen60.gp sequence above under `/opt/homebrew/bin/gp -q -f -s 64M`, 0.3 s wall): p=866004983247663323, a=218370429096749092, b=332004879195750802, n=866004985024698433, tries=45, P=(649465449118648377, 257340576278519516); the committed vector must equal these values. On that curve `crash_selftest(p,a,b)` at `-s 8M` → rc 0, empty stdout, `*** ellcard: the PARI stack overflows !` (current stack size 8000000) on stderr, and OK at `-s 64M`; `verify(p,a,b,n,P,3P,3)` → OK at `-s 3M`, `8M` and `64M`, `FAIL ["xP-ne-Q"]` with x=4, and `-s 2M` exits 1 at startup with `### Errors on startup, exiting...` on stdout.

CURVE60 UNDER CYPARI2 (probed 2026-08-21 in the grounding brief's scratch venv, cypari2 2.2.4 / libpari 2.17.2, Python 3.14.0): the same call sequence in-process — `pari.setrand(1); p = pari.randomprime([2**59, 2**60])`; loop `a = pari.random(p); b = pari.random(p)`, singular skip, `tries += 1`, `E = pari.ellinit([a,b], p)`, `n = pari.ellsea(E, 1)`, accept iff `n and pari.isprime(n)`; then `pari.ellcard(E) == n`; then `P = pari.random(E)` — reproduces p, a, b, n, tries = 45 and P = (649465449118648377, 257340576278519516) exactly (0.29 s wall under `allocatemem(64_000_000)`), so the field-for-field assertion `toy_curve(60, 1) == tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` in cairn-m0-e0s.6 is grounded for both builds, P included; `pari.random(E)` is the cypari2 spelling of gp's `random(E)`. Subprocess start cost, same venv: `python -c "import cypari2; p = cypari2.Pari(); p.allocatemem(64_000_000, silent=True); p.ellcard(p.ellinit([-3,1],5))"` → 0.03–0.08 s wall over three runs, so the 40-bit `mean_wall_s` the tier gate judges against the 1 core-s Tier-0 edge (cairn-m0-e0s.10/.14) has ample margin.

title: M0: gate bundle (separate read-only SQLite, content-addressed) + deployment pin (0444+append-only) + attestation file (0644+append-only) + attestation digest/offset check + tier gate predicate (TierRefused; bundle≠pin fails closed; uncertified/yanked refused; ticket bundle-hash mismatch re-mints) + OS write-boundary tests + waiver-cannot-advance fixture
description:
WHY (PLAN §4, §5): a gate that silently fails open manufactures the appearance of enforcement. The gate bundle is content-addressed, opened read-only by the orchestrator process, its hash pinned at deployment in an operator-owned file the process user cannot write, and recorded in every gate-run record; a bundle whose hash differs from the pin fails closed whoever rewrote it. The tier gate reads only launch-supplied inputs (cost profile at inputs, budget, hypothesis key/method identity) plus substrate-resolved ones (self-test standing, ticket) and judges against gate-owned objects; a refusal is a `TierRefused` record, not an exception to retry around. Operator decisions 8 (one OS user at M0 → mode/flags only; what that refuses is recorded by bead m0-grounding-probes = cairn-m0-e0s.2) and 9 (ticket carries bundle hash; mismatch ⇒ re-mint) bind.

WHAT (`src/cairn/bundle.py`: build, pin, `GateBundle`; `src/cairn/attest.py`: `attest init/append`, `attestation_record_matches`, `visible_review_verdicts`; `src/cairn/tiergate.py`: `TierGate`)
- `bundle/*.json` source: `verifier {backend_path:"/opt/homebrew/bin/gp", stack_ceiling:"64M", timeout_s:30, accept:{rc:0, stdout:"OK", stderr_empty:true}}` (a structured object the driver evaluates field by field, cairn-m0-e0s.8 — never a string it would have to evaluate) plus the `verifier_script` object (the bytes of `src/cairn/gp/verify.gp` — the file cairn-m0-e0s.8 owns, so the build depends on that bead — kind `verifier_script`, so the verifier's script is pinned and hash-recorded in every gate run; the driver materializes it from the bundle, cairn-m0-e0s.8); `tiers {boundary_table:[{tier:0,max_core_s:1},{tier:1,max_core_s:3600},{tier:2,max_core_s:3600000},{tier:3,max_core_s:null}] (one unit, core-seconds, throughout; M0 defaults, CONJECTURE; 3 600 000 core-s is the ≈10³ core-hour Tier-2/3 edge of PLAN §5; a launch's tier is the first row whose max its production cost does not exceed), ceiling_multiplier:4, tier1_cumulative_edge:null}` (edge set at M1, decision 10); `gate_plan` (ordered steps with expected results — bead m0-gate-plan-selftests = cairn-m0-e0s.11; its crash fixture embeds the committed 60-bit curve `(p,a,b)` from `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` as decimal strings for the `crash_selftest(p,a,b)` entry at `8M` and its `64M` control); `waivable_checks: []` (no admission gate is waivable; the waiver fixture consults this set); `auditor {f:0.01,bits:20}`; `lean {permitted_axioms:["propext","Classical.choice","Quot.sound"]}` (stored, unused until M1); `role_templates:{}`, `allow_lists:{}` (M1).
- `uv run cairn bundle build --src bundle/` (writes the global `--bundle` path, default `deploy/gate-bundle.sqlite`; no `--out`): one row per object (kind, canonical bytes, hash); bundle hash = H('cairn/gate-bundle/v1' ‖ sorted (kind,hash) pairs); deterministic (build twice → same hash). `uv run cairn bundle show [--json]` (read-only; `bundle` is one registered name — `cli.register('bundle', …, read_only=False, json=True, dangerous=True, gating='--force', dry_run_default=True)` through cairn-m0-e0s.17, its `configure` adding the `build|pin|show` sub-subparsers — so the capabilities row is `bundle`'s, not `show`'s; the registry adds `--force` at the `bundle` level and `configure` attaches a `default=argparse.SUPPRESS` `--force` parent to `build` and `pin` (the `globals_parent(suppress=True)` pattern; probed 2026-08-21: `bundle build --force` and `bundle --force build` both parse to `force=True`, `bundle build` to `False`) so `cairn bundle build … --force` parses; `dry_run_default=True` keeps `main`'s pre-run refusal off so `show` and a first `build`/`pin` run flagless, and `build`/`pin` call `cli.refuse_overwrite(path, flag='--force', command='cairn bundle <sub>', force=ns.force)` before writing; `attest` is likewise one registered name (`read_only=False`, `init|append` sub-subparsers, no gating flag — its refusal over an existing file is a plain `CliError(GATE_REFUSED)`)) prints the bundle's hash, the pin's recorded hash, `pin_match` and the (kind, hash) rows: exit 0 when they match, 2 GATE_REFUSED when they differ with `next_command` = the re-pin sequence below, 3 ENVIRONMENT when either file is missing. `uv run cairn bundle pin` (reads the global `--bundle`, writes the global `--pin`, default `deploy/gate-bundle.pin`) writes the hash, chmods pin and bundle 0444 and sets `uappnd` on the pin (macOS; probed 2026-08-21: with the flag standing the owner's `chmod` is refused too; re-pinning is the operator's act and needs `chflags nouappnd` first). Dangerous-op gating (cairn-m0-e0s.17): `bundle build` over an existing bundle and `bundle pin` over an existing pin are refused without `--force` (exit 2, `next_command` naming `--force`; `bundle show` is the safe read); with `--force`, `build` chmods the 0444 bundle writable and rewrites it, while `pin` over a pin still carrying `uappnd` meets the OS refusal (EPERM, cairn-m0-e0s.2) and exits 3 ENVIRONMENT with `next_command` = `chflags nouappnd <pin>` followed by the same command — so the copy-pasteable re-pin sequence every refusal in the codebase names is `chflags nouappnd Y && cairn bundle build --src bundle/ --bundle X --force && cairn bundle pin --bundle X --pin Y --force`. `uv run cairn attest init` (creates the global `--attest` path, default `deploy/attestations.log`; no positional path; it reads the global `--bundle`/`--pin` through `GateBundle.open` to take `W` from `gate_plan.fixtures`, so it runs after `bundle pin` and fails closed on a pin mismatch — exit 2 with the re-pin sequence as `next_command`; over an existing attestation file it is refused, exit 2, `next_command` = `cairn attest append …`, since the harness never re-creates that file and moving it aside is the operator's act; exit 3 when the bundle or pin file is missing) creates the file mode 0644 and sets `uappnd` (appendable by the owner, not overwritable, not truncatable, not re-modable while flagged; 0444 would refuse the append — cairn-m0-e0s.2 probe 3), and appends as record 0 the gate plan's fixture waiver `{kind:'waiver', target_kind:'hypothesis_key', target: H(W), check:'tier_gate', reason:'gate-plan fixture', issued_by:'attest init', expires_at:'9999-12-31T23:59:59Z'}` — `W` is the fixture hypothesis object the bundle's `gate_plan.fixtures` carries (cairn-m0-e0s.11) — so the `waiver_cannot_advance` step reads an operator-written record at a known offset instead of appending one per run, a shape that survives the second OS user of M3; elsewhere than macOS it logs loudly and skips the flag.
- `GateBundle.open(path, pin_path)`: opens `file:...?mode=ro`; recomputes the hash from rows; compares to the pin; mismatch → `BundlePinMismatch`, and every gate run refuses with a `gate_runs` row `gate='bundle_open', result='refused', reasons=['bundle-hash-ne-pin']`.
- `attestation_record_matches(file, offset, digest) -> bool`: reads the length-prefixed canonical record at `offset`, compares BLAKE3; `visible_review_verdicts(statement_hash)` filters rows through it (used by bead m0-justify = cairn-m0-e0s.12; the same function serves `yank_records`/`salts` at M1). Operator append path: `uv run cairn attest append --kind review_verdict ...` appends the canonical record and mirrors the substrate row with digest+offset (at M0 the same OS user runs both; the boundary is the file mode/flag + the digest rule); `--kind waiver` appends the file record and mirrors no row at M0 (no M0 reader consumes waivers — `waivable_checks` is empty; the waiver table arrives with the human queue, cairn-m1-cqt.7), the form cairn-m0-e0s.12's waiver-moves-no-tag test uses.
- `TierGate.admit(launch) -> Admitted | TierRefused`; launch = `{cost_profile, inputs, budget_remaining, hypothesis_key, method_identity, statement_hash?, skill_identity_hash, declared_tier}`; the production cost at inputs is `cost_profile.evaluate(inputs).expected_core_s` (a `cairn.profile.CostProfile`, the module cairn-m0-e0s.6 creates — this bead depends on it for the type alone; a profile whose `evaluate` raises `ProfileUndeclared` at the launch's inputs is a refusal, `profile-undeclared`; the tier-gate tests use synthetic `CostProfile` instances, never the toy-curve one); resolves `certified(skill_identity)` and `not yanked(skill_identity)` (predicates in cairn-m0-e0s.4); selects the ticket (Tier 0: none; Tier 1: a hypothesis object, plus the claim statement node where a claim exists, recorded in the substrate — the §8 presence check and the §7 statement pre-filters that also condition the Tier-1 ticket arrive at M1; Tier 2/3 kinds are M1 — absent ⇒ refuse); refuses when `declared_tier > ticket_tier + 1` (`tier_refusals` row), when declared tier < the tier the boundary table assigns the production cost at the launch's inputs, when uncertified or yanked, when `evaluate(inputs).expected_core_s + expected_verification_core_s` (cairn-m0-e0s.6's `Evaluation`) > remaining budget; the predicates do not short-circuit — `reasons` lists every one that holds, in the fixed order `profile-undeclared` (which leaves the cost-dependent predicates unevaluated), `ticket-absent`, `tier-two-above`, `boundary-table`, `uncertified`, `yanked`, `budget`, `ticket-bundle-mismatch` — and the launch is admitted iff `reasons` is empty, so a gate-plan self-test step asserts the reason it plants whatever else its fixture launch lacks (cairn-m0-e0s.11); every decision is a `gate_runs` row (gate='tier_gate', result admitted|refused) with bundle hash + pin hash; a ticket whose recorded bundle hash ≠ current bundle hash → refused `ticket-bundle-mismatch`, and that refusing decision is also the re-mint of decision 9 at M0: because the Tier-1 ticket here is a substrate node no gate run produced (the hypothesis object), the gate re-selects it under the current bundle and writes the fresh `tickets` row in the same decision, so the next launch on that key reads the fresh row and is admitted — a stale row blocks a key for exactly one refusal, never permanently (from M1 a ticket a gate run produced, a ladder table, is re-minted only by re-running that gate under the current bundle, tier-below work the refusal leaves to the next launch). The gate is the only writer of `tickets` rows (table in cairn-m0-e0s.5): on admission it mints the row for the ticket it selected — at M0 `{hypothesis_key, method_identity, statement_hash?, tier: 0, kind: 'hypothesis_object', node_hash: the hypothesis object's hash, bundle_hash: the current bundle hash}` — when no row under the current bundle exists, and a later launch reads the most recent row for that hypothesis key and method identity; the stale-bundle test pre-writes a row under another bundle hash for a key whose hypothesis object is recorded, asserts the refusal (`ticket-bundle-mismatch` in `reasons`) and that a fresh row under the current bundle now exists beside the stale one (rows are append-only, cairn-m0-e0s.5), then asserts that the same launch re-issued is admitted reading the fresh row. Every decision logs (hypothesis key, declared tier, ticket tier, reasons) through `cairn.log`.
- Waiver fixture: a waiver record appended through the attestation path does NOT produce a ticket or admit a tier (admission gates are non-waivable, §4; `waivable_checks` is empty). The claim half of the same §4 fixture — a waiver moves no tag — is `justify`'s own planted test (cairn-m0-e0s.12).
TESTS (integration, real files under tmp_path; `tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py`, `tests/integration/test_tier_gate.py`): build+pin; open OK; `bundle show --json` reports `pin_match: true` with exit 0 on the pinned pair and exit 2 after the bundle edit below; `bundle build` over the built bundle and `bundle pin` over the pin → refused without `--force` (exit 2, `--force` named, files unchanged); `attest init` over the existing file → refused (exit 2, file unchanged); edit one row in a writable copy of the bundle → open refuses, gate_runs row says why; `open(pin,'w')`, `open(pin,'a')`, `os.chmod(pin,0o644)`, `os.unlink(pin)` and `os.rename(pin, …)` → PermissionError (`uappnd` refuses unlink and rename while it stands — probed 2026-08-21; the pin cannot be replaced by rename); `open(attestations,'w')`, `os.truncate`, `os.unlink` and `os.rename` → PermissionError; every test that flags a file under tmp_path clears the flag in teardown (`chflags nouappnd`), since pytest's basetemp cleanup cannot remove a flagged file; the built bundle's `verifier.accept` equals `{rc:0, stdout:'OK', stderr_empty:true}` and its `verifier_script` row hash equals BLAKE3 of `src/cairn/gp/verify.gp`; `open(attestations,'a')` succeeds and the mirrored review_verdict row is visible only when digest/offset match (forge a row with a wrong digest → absent); launch declaring tier 2 with a Tier-0 ticket → TierRefused row; tier 1 with hypothesis object recorded → Admitted; uncertified skill → refused; yanked skill (a yank_records row) → refused; production cost above the Tier-1 boundary declared as tier 1 → refused; declared cost above the remaining budget → refused; ticket with stale bundle hash → refused; waiver → no ticket.
UNIT (`tests/unit/test_tier_gate_predicate.py`, pure): the predicate's truth table over (declared tier, ticket tier, boundary-table tier at cost, certified, yanked, budget ok, ticket bundle matches) — each refusal reason reached by exactly the rows that should reach it; the boundary-table lookup at its edges (1, 3600, 3 600 000 core-s: a cost exactly at an edge stays in the lower tier, one unit above it moves up).

TEST PLAN (shapes)
- Golden: `tests/goldens/gate_bundle_hash.golden` = the bundle hash of `bundle/` built from the committed sources (`bundle/*.json` + `src/cairn/gp/verify.gp`) — an exact golden of volatility 2 (deterministic and platform-independent: the bundle holds strings, bytes and hashes only, `backend_path` included as a string; it moves only when a bundle source changes, an operator act); `tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py::test_bundle_hash_golden` builds twice under tmp_path, asserts both equal and equal the golden through `assert_golden`; a bundle-source edit therefore lands only with `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` and an attributed commit naming the change (the pin is the deploy-time copy of this rule, the golden the repo-time one); PROVENANCE.md row lists the source files hashed.
- Fuzzing (`tests/unit/test_attest_fuzz.py`, Hypothesis ≥ 500, real temp files, no flags): `attestation_record_matches(file, offset, digest)` over `offset ∈ st.integers(-(2**63), 2**63)`, `digest ∈ st.binary(max_size=64)` and file contents from `st.binary()` plus structured mutations of a real record (truncated length prefix, a length prefix larger than the file, zero length, two records back to back, a record whose digest matches at offset+1) — returns `False` or raises the typed `AttestationError`, never an unhandled exception, and returns `True` only when the length-prefixed record at exactly `offset` hashes to exactly `digest`; `visible_review_verdicts` never yields a row whose `(file_offset, record_digest)` is not an exact match; planted mutants in `tests/mutants/attest_mutants.py`: `matches_any_record_with_digest` (scans the file ignoring `offset`), `matches_digest_prefix`, `matches_on_length_only` — each killed; seed corpus `tests/fuzz_corpus/attest/` holds the forged-digest row, the off-by-one offset and the truncated prefix as `@example`s.
- Property over the tier-gate predicate (`tests/unit/test_tier_gate_properties.py`, Hypothesis ≥ 500, synthetic `CostProfile`s and launches from `tests/factories.py`): `reasons` is always a subsequence of the fixed order `[profile-undeclared, ticket-absent, tier-two-above, boundary-table, uncertified, yanked, budget, ticket-bundle-mismatch]`; admitted iff `reasons == []`; monotone — for any launch `L`, `reasons(L with certified=False) ⊇ reasons(L)`, `reasons(L with yanked=True) ⊇ reasons(L)` and `reasons(L with budget_remaining=0) ⊇ reasons(L)` (adding a failing predicate never removes a reason; a perturbation of `declared_tier` is not monotone — raising it can clear `boundary-table` while adding `tier-two-above` — so the property perturbs only the standing, yank and budget inputs) — kills `short_circuit_gate` in `tests/mutants/tiergate_mutants.py` (returns on the first reason) and `reasons_unordered`; the boundary edges `{1, 3600, 3_600_000}` stay as `@example`s.
- Failure-path convergence: the OS write-boundary table is one `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over `(file ∈ {pin, attestations}, op ∈ {open-w, open-a, truncate, chmod, unlink, rename}, expected)` with `pytest.raises(PermissionError)` per refused row and the one permitted row (`attestations`, `open-a`) asserting success; the tier-gate refusal cases one parametrize over `(launch_delta, expected_reasons)`; each test flags and un-flags its own files.
- Layer: bundle/pin/attest/tier-gate decisions are integration (real files, real flags, real substrate, `db_snapshot` of `gate_runs`/`tickets`/`tier_refusals` after each decision); the predicate and the record matcher are unit.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py tests/integration/test_tier_gate.py tests/unit/test_tier_gate_predicate.py -q` green; `uv run cairn bundle build` twice (the second with `--force`) → identical bundle hash; `uv run cairn bundle show --json` on the pinned pair exits 0 with `pin_match: true`; deploy/ artifacts created with modes 0444 (bundle), 0444+uappnd (pin) and 0644+uappnd (attestations), asserted by `os.stat` and `ls -lO`; `cairn attest init` leaves the fixture waiver at record 0 (`attestation_record_matches(file, 0, BLAKE3 of it)` true); a refused launch's `reasons` lists every failed predicate (the uncertified, tier-two-above launch names both).
- Planted negative: modified bundle → fail closed with a gate_runs row and `bundle show` exit 2; `bundle build`/`bundle pin` over an existing artifact and `attest init` over an existing file must be refused without `--force` with nothing written; tier-two-above → TierRefused recorded; pin write, chmod, unlink and rename → PermissionError; attestation overwrite/truncate/unlink/rename → PermissionError; forged review_verdict digest → absent; waiver → no ticket; stale-bundle ticket → refused; yanked/uncertified → refused. Any of these passing silently fails the bead.
- No-Claim: file mode/flags under ONE OS user — the owning process could `chflags nouappnd` and chmod them back; M0 records this gap (bead m0-grounding-probes = cairn-m0-e0s.2) and decision 8 defers the second OS user to M3; Tier-2/3 ticket kinds, the cumulative edge, the §8 presence check and the §7 pre-filters are M1.
- `tests/goldens/gate_bundle_hash.golden` compares exactly to a double build; a bundle-source change fails without `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1`; its PROVENANCE.md row lists the hashed sources; `tests/unit/test_attest_fuzz.py` green at ≥ 500 examples with `attestation_record_matches` never `True` off an exact (offset, digest) match and never raising unhandled, and `matches_any_record_with_digest`, `matches_digest_prefix`, `matches_on_length_only` killed; `tests/fuzz_corpus/attest/` replayed.
- `tests/unit/test_tier_gate_properties.py` green at ≥ 500 examples (reasons ordered, admitted iff empty, monotone under added failures) with `short_circuit_gate` and `reasons_unordered` killed; the write-boundary table and the refusal cases are each one parametrized test.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment, so the compliance audit can re-run it without reading the session.
notes:
BEAD ALIASES → IDS (the descriptions name beads by alias; these are the br ids): m0-scaffold-smoke = cairn-m0-e0s.1; m0-grounding-probes = cairn-m0-e0s.2; m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3; m0-substrate-core = cairn-m0-e0s.4; m0-claims-schema = cairn-m0-e0s.5; m0-toy-curve-skill = cairn-m0-e0s.6; m0-skill-selftest-cert = cairn-m0-e0s.7; m0-tier0-verifier = cairn-m0-e0s.8; m0-skill-runner-receipt = cairn-m0-e0s.9; m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate = cairn-m0-e0s.10; m0-gate-plan-selftests = cairn-m0-e0s.11; m0-justify = cairn-m0-e0s.12; m0-gc-roots = cairn-m0-e0s.13; m0-e2e-slice = cairn-m0-e0s.14; m0-rho60-measure = cairn-m0-e0s.15; m1-ladder = cairn-m1-cqt.1; m1-baseline-skills = cairn-m1-cqt.2; m1-planted-corpus = cairn-m1-cqt.3; m1-budget-escrow-yank = cairn-m1-cqt.4; m1-formalization-gate = cairn-m1-cqt.5; m1-worker-dispatch-canary = cairn-m1-cqt.6; m1-human-queue-review = cairn-m1-cqt.7; m1-router-ledger-hunt-repro = cairn-m1-cqt.8.

MEASURED COST vs THE TIER-0 EDGE (from cairn-m0-e0s.6 as built, commit 9c07701; brief §6a): `toy_curve`'s declared `CostProfile.evaluate(bits)` returns the measured mean SUBPROCESS wall (interpreter start + cypari2 import + allocatemem included): 0.137 s at 30 bits, 0.134 s at 40, 0.251 s at 50, 0.878 s at 60. The bundle's Tier-0/Tier-1 edge is 1 core-s, so a 60-bit `toy_curve` launch is admitted Tier 0 with only ~12% headroom, and the measured tries distribution is geometric (sd/mean ~0.9; the worst of 50 seeds drew 340 tries against a mean of 88), so a slower machine or an unlucky seed crosses the edge and the gate assigns Tier 1 — a correct refusal of a Tier-0 declaration, not a bug, but it means the M0 fixture that asserts "the 40-bit slice launch is admitted Tier 0" must use 40 bits (0.134 s, ~7x headroom) and never 60. The boundary table stays CONJECTURE at M0 per this bead; M1 re-sets it from the baseline skills' measured distributions.
