comments.text:
Built at commit 2531d3f7365140c6d4a1603b741a21e37faa34e1 (three commits: b0e9759 bundle+attest, 34c37e6 tier gate, 2531d3f audit findings). Working tree clean at close.

Baseline before any work: `git status --short` empty, `uv run pytest -q` -> 741 passed. At close: 896 passed. Branch coverage over the three modules: bundle 98%, attest 97%, tiergate 100%; every uncovered line is a declined finding named below.

## Acceptance bullet 1 (positives) -- all re-executed at this SHA

`uv run pytest tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py tests/integration/test_tier_gate.py tests/unit/test_tier_gate_predicate.py -q`

    85 passed in 0.62s

`uv run cairn bundle build --src bundle/ ...` twice, the second with `--force`:

    c86c39f6b6f67007c3130dc4bac7faf6c4675a80658312da16646612bdd71e4b
    c86c39f6b6f67007c3130dc4bac7faf6c4675a80658312da16646612bdd71e4b

`uv run cairn bundle pin` then `uv run cairn bundle show --json` on the pinned pair, exit 0:

    {"bundle_hash": "c86c39f6...bdd71e4b", "pin_hash": "c86c39f6...bdd71e4b", "pin_match": true,
     "objects": [allow_lists, auditor, gate_plan, lean, role_templates, tiers, verifier, verifier_script, waivable_checks]}
    show rc=0

The `verifier_script` row hash is `b27697bd9e713a40021a1603a2fc33a501dd92bf2a29d1358d0e2dac04147f06`, equal to BLAKE3 of `src/cairn/gp/verify.gp`, and `verifier.accept` equals `{rc: 0, stdout: "OK", stderr_empty: true}` (asserted in `tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py:61`).

Modes and flags, `os.stat` then `ls -lO`:

      g.sqlite     mode=0444  uappnd=False
      g.pin        mode=0444  uappnd=True
      att.log      mode=0644  uappnd=True
    -rw-r--r--@ 1 jr843u  wheel  uappnd   228 att.log
    -r--r--r--@ 1 jr843u  wheel  uappnd    65 g.pin
    -r--r--r--@ 1 jr843u  wheel  -      12288 g.sqlite

`cairn attest init` leaves the gate plan's fixture waiver at record 0:

      waiver target (H(W))     : 7535d7bbd876e5955df63ad81986e78cc1f98f98252966195b8d2b3eb75136c9
      record 0 digest          : 76a04b779af9cd77a2f22c9e37e01ee5970280b2242b2d63b199b6e196cb8143
      matches at offset 0      : True
      matches at offset 1      : False
      forged digest at offset 0: False
      waivable_checks          : []

A refused launch names every failed predicate: the uncertified, tier-two-above launch returns `('tier-two-above', 'uncertified')` (`tests/integration/test_tier_gate.py:164`), and the boundary-and-budget launch returns `('boundary-table', 'budget')` (`tests/integration/test_tier_gate.py:129`).

## Acceptance bullet 2 (planted negatives) -- each observed failing, not assumed

Modified bundle, one object's canonical bytes replaced in a writable copy:

    bundle_hash 7bafce326af159cb1a950e9f9198438b1d51e7d819b175d1cc3af79f7c4224ea, pin_hash c86c39f6...bdd71e4b, pin_match false
    tampered show rc=2
    error: gate bundle hash 7bafce32... differs from the pin c86c39f6...; every gate fails closed until they agree
      (.../g.pin); run: chflags nouappnd .../g.pin && cairn bundle build --src bundle/ --bundle .../tampered.sqlite --force
      && cairn bundle pin --bundle .../tampered.sqlite --pin .../g.pin --force

and through `open_for_gate` the refusal is a substrate row: `gate='bundle_open', result='refused', reasons=['bundle-hash-ne-pin']` (`tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py:97`).

Refusals with nothing written:

    error: .../g.sqlite exists and would be overwritten; nothing was changed; run: cairn bundle build --force
    error: .../g.pin exists and would be overwritten; nothing was changed; run: cairn bundle pin --force
    error: the attestation file .../att.log exists; the harness never re-creates it and moving it aside is the
      operator's act; run: cairn attest append --kind review_verdict --record REC.json --attest .../att.log
    error: the pin .../g.pin refused the write (Operation not permitted); clearing its append-only flag is the
      operator's act; run: chflags nouappnd .../g.pin && cairn bundle build ... --force && cairn bundle pin ... --force

OS write boundary, observed by running each operation:

      g.pin      open-w    PermissionError [1] Operation not permitted
      g.pin      open-a    PermissionError [13] Permission denied
      g.pin      truncate  PermissionError [1] Operation not permitted
      g.pin      chmod     PermissionError [1] Operation not permitted
      g.pin      unlink    PermissionError [1] Operation not permitted
      g.pin      rename    PermissionError [1] Operation not permitted
      att.log    open-w    PermissionError [1] Operation not permitted
      att.log    open-a    SUCCEEDED
      att.log    truncate  PermissionError [1] Operation not permitted
      att.log    chmod     PermissionError [1] Operation not permitted
      att.log    unlink    PermissionError [1] Operation not permitted
      att.log    rename    PermissionError [1] Operation not permitted

Forged review_verdict digest absent (`test_gate_bundle.py:214`), waiver mints no ticket (`test_tier_gate.py:214`), stale-bundle ticket refused and re-minted then admitted on the next launch (`test_tier_gate.py:182`), yanked and uncertified refused (`test_tier_gate.py:148,155`).

## Acceptance bullets 4 and 5

`uv run pytest tests/unit/test_attest_fuzz.py tests/unit/test_tier_gate_properties.py tests/unit/test_bundle_canon.py -q` at HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=ci (500 examples):

    62 passed in 4.54s

`tests/goldens/gate_bundle_hash.golden` = `c86c39f6b6f67007c3130dc4bac7faf6c4675a80658312da16646612bdd71e4b`, compared to a double build under tmp_path, with its PROVENANCE.md row naming the nine hashed sources. `matches_any_record_with_digest`, `matches_digest_prefix` and `matches_on_length_only` each killed by the seed corpus; `short_circuit_gate` and `reasons_unordered` each killed. Seed corpus replayed: `tests/fuzz_corpus/attest/` (7 cases). The write-boundary table and the tier-gate refusal cases are each one parametrized test.

## /optimal-tests --audit

Ran in `--audit` mode over the five test files. Findings applied: `cairn bundle pin` had never run through the CLI at all (the pin was written only by the fixture calling `bundle.write_pin`); `bundle build` at an unusable `--src`, `bundle pin` without a bundle, `attest append` before `attest init`, `attest init` without the gate artifacts, and the human (non-`--json`) stdout of build/pin/show were all uncovered; the bundle canonicalizer's rejection paths had no test at all (`tests/unit/test_bundle_canon.py`); one bare `pytest.raises` per typed error got a `match=`; `test_a_non_hex_digest_never_matches` asserted an identity on a private helper and was replaced by a claim about matching.

Declined, with reasons: the non-`chflags` platform fallbacks (`bundle.py:141-146`, `attest.py:125-130`) -- both test files are `skipif(sys.platform != "darwin")` and the Linux `chattr +a` boundary is the M1 container bead; two defensive raises in the bundle decoder (`bundle.py:218,254`) -- the encoder and decoder are inverse over the admitted types, so no bundle this code builds reaches them; one `print` line whose `--json` twin is asserted (`attest.py:186`).

## Mutation proof of the "untested protection" findings

Each protection deleted in place, the named tests run, then the file restored and verified byte-identical by `shasum -a 256 -c` (both files OK).

    write_pin drops _set_append_only(pin)              -> 6 failed, 30 passed
    GateBundle.open drops the pin comparison           -> 2 failed, 34 passed
    attest.init drops _set_append_only(file)           -> 5 failed, 31 passed
    canonical_bytes drops canon.encode's float check   -> 27 passed  (SURVIVED)

The fourth survived, and chasing it was worth it. `_Json` rejects a float by type fallthrough anyway, so both layers refuse and the assertion could not tell which fired. They do differ: `canon.encode` names the path to the float (`$.a.b[1]`), which is what an operator editing `bundle/*.json` needs, while `_Json` only says "bundle objects admit no float". Asserting the path discriminates them; re-run after the fix: 5 failed, 23 passed. Mutant killed.

## Disagreements with the bead text, asserting the observed truth

1. `ls -lO` in tests. The bead asks for the modes to be "asserted by `os.stat` and `ls -lO`". `tests/conftest.py`'s `isolation_guard` refuses any subprocess outside `{python, gp}`, so a test cannot spawn `ls`. The tests assert via `os.stat` plus `st_flags & UF_APPEND`, which reads the same fact from the same syscall and compares a value rather than parsing a string; `ls -lO` is run by hand at close and its output is pasted above.
2. `auditor {f: 0.01}`. `cairn.canon.reject_floats` refuses floats outright, because a float has no canonical encoding, so `bundle/auditor.json` carries `{"f": "0.01", "bits": 20}` with `f` as a string.
3. `gate_runs` names no launch. The row's canonical form carries gate, bundle hash, pin hash, plan step, instance hash, statement hash, result, reasons and `at`; it does not carry the hypothesis key, and `at` is second-resolution. Two tier-gate decisions with identical content in one second therefore collapse into one content-addressed row. The launch identity survives in `tier_refusals` (refusals only) and in the JSON log. Pinned by `test_two_indistinguishable_decisions_in_one_second_are_one_content_addressed_row` (`tests/integration/test_tier_gate.py:249`) so the gate plan runner (cairn-m0-e0s.11) and the e2e slice (cairn-m0-e0s.14) meet it as a stated property rather than a surprise.
4. The bundle SQLite carries no `hash` column. The first draft stored one and folded it into the bundle hash, so editing an object's canonical bytes in place left the bundle hash unchanged and the pin check passed -- a silent fail-open that the planted tamper test caught on its first run. The row hash is recomputed from the bytes on every read and the column is gone, so nothing can disagree with the bytes.

## Files touched

    src/cairn/bundle.py     :40  class _Json          :92  bundle_hash       :97  build
                            :126 write_pin            :163 GateBundle.open   :257 record_open_refusal
                            :271 open_for_gate        :279 repin_sequence
    src/cairn/attest.py     :39  fixture_waiver       :55  append_record     :64  read_record
                            :86  attestation_record_matches                  :106 visible_review_verdicts
                            :112 init
    src/cairn/tiergate.py   :63  tier_for_cost        :75  predicate_reasons :107 _selected_ticket
                            :115 _recorded_ticket     :122 admit             :172 _mint
    src/cairn/cli.py        :31  COMMAND_MODULES gains cairn.bundle and cairn.attest
    src/cairn/claims.py     :604 read_record and verdict_matches_file delegate to cairn.attest
    bundle/                 allow_lists, auditor, gate_plan, lean, role_templates, tiers, verifier, waivable_checks (.json)
    tests/conftest.py       :180 clear_flags   :190 pinned_bundle
    tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py    36 tests
    tests/integration/test_tier_gate.py      17 tests
    tests/unit/test_tier_gate_predicate.py   32 tests
    tests/unit/test_tier_gate_properties.py  11 tests
    tests/unit/test_attest_fuzz.py           23 tests
    tests/unit/test_bundle_canon.py          28 tests
    tests/mutants/attest_mutants.py, tests/mutants/tiergate_mutants.py
    tests/fuzz_corpus/attest/                7 seed cases
    tests/goldens/gate_bundle_hash.golden, tests/goldens/PROVENANCE.md
    tests/goldens/capabilities.golden, help_top.golden, help_bundle.golden, help_attest.golden
    tests/unit/test_cli_contract.py, tests/unit/test_pari_module.py  (nested-subcommand parametrization)

## No-Claim

Green here does not prove any of the following.

The file mode and flag boundary holds under ONE OS user. The owning process can `chflags nouappnd` and `chmod` these artifacts back; the harness declines to, which is a discipline, not an enforcement. Operator decision 8 defers the second OS user to M3, and the gap is recorded by cairn-m0-e0s.2.

The boundary table (1, 3600, 3 600 000 core-s) is CONJECTURE at M0 and M1 re-sets it from the baseline skills' measured distributions. The M0 fixture that asserts a Tier-0 admission must use 40 bits, not 60: per the bead's own note, a 60-bit `toy_curve` launch sits at 0.878 s against a 1 core-s edge with a geometric tries distribution, so a slow machine or an unlucky seed crosses it. No test here uses the toy-curve profile at all; the tier gate's tests build synthetic `CostProfile`s, so a re-measurement of `toy_curve` cannot move them.

Tier-2/3 ticket kinds, the Tier-1 cumulative edge, the PLAN section 8 presence check and the section 7 statement pre-filters are M1. A tier-2 launch is refused two-above here by construction, not by judging a tier-2 ticket.

Waivers move nothing at M0 because `waivable_checks` is empty and no M0 reader consumes them. The claim half of the section 4 fixture -- a waiver moves no tag -- is cairn-m0-e0s.12's planted test, not this one.

The verifier is pinned but not exercised. This bead asserts that the bundle carries `verify.gp`'s bytes and that `VerifierConfig.from_bundle` builds from them; it never spawns gp. The verifier's own behavior is cairn-m0-e0s.8's, already closed.

`_decode` is the bundle's own inverse and is exercised only over values this code encodes. A bundle SQLite whose canonical bytes were crafted by something else is refused by the pin, not by the decoder.

Not independently verified: this is a single-agent build. No second agent re-ran these commands. The mutation proof is the closest thing to independent verification here -- each protection was deleted and the failure observed rather than reasoned about -- but the tests, the code and the audit were all written in one session by one agent, and the audit was self-applied. Treat the disagreements section as the place a reviewer should look first.

title: M0: declarative gate plan runner with planted-failure self-tests run before the gates (verifier xP≠Q + forced crash; canonicalizer KATs; waiver-cannot-advance); ordered scopes where an earlier failure blocks later steps; fail closed on invalid/missing config
description:
WHY (PLAN §4 gate discipline; §13 M0): every gate ships a planted-failure self-test (a fixture that must FAIL and one that must PASS) run before the gate itself; gates run from a declarative plan with expected results and ordered scopes — an earlier failure blocks later steps and records why; invalid or missing gate config fails closed; a green result whose provenance is weaker than required cannot strengthen a claim. The first gate self-tests at M0 are the verifier's planted `xP ≠ Q` and forced-crash fixtures and the canonicalizer's known-answer vectors for both keys.

WHAT (`src/cairn/gateplan.py`)
- Plan = ordered steps from the gate bundle, e.g. `[{step:'canon_kat', cmd:'kat canon', expect:'pass'}, {step:'verifier_selftest_pass', fixture:'corpus-1 x=3', expect:'OK'}, {step:'verifier_selftest_fail_xP_ne_Q', fixture:'corpus-1 x=4', expect:'FAIL xP-ne-Q'} (`corpus-1` = the F_5 instance `(p=5, a=2, b=1, n=7, P=(0,1), Q=(3,3))` embedded in the bundle as decimal strings — `a` already reduced from the corpus file's `-3`, cairn-m0-e0s.7/.8 — never read from `src/cairn/skills/toy_curve_corpus.json` at gate time), {step:'verifier_selftest_crash', entry:'crash_selftest', fixture:'curve60_seed1 (p,a,b) as decimal strings embedded in the bundle; the committed vector of cairn-m0-e0s.1', stack:'8M', expect:'FAIL backend-crash'} (the real backend really overflowing: rc 0, empty stdout, `*** ellcard: the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr — `verify()` itself prints OK at 8M because it never calls `ellcard`, probed 2026-08-21, which is why the crash step calls the script's `crash_selftest` entry, cairn-m0-e0s.8), {step:'verifier_selftest_crash_control', entry:'crash_selftest', same curve, stack:'64M', expect:'OK'} (the must-PASS half: the crash entry is a live computation, not a stub), {step:'waiver_cannot_advance', expect:'no-ticket'}, {step:'tier_gate_selftest_two_above', expect:'TierRefused(tier-two-above)'}]`. The two tier-gate steps run against the real `TierGate` (cairn-m0-e0s.10) from `gate_plan.fixtures`, carried in the bundle so they are pinned and hash-recorded: two synthetic hypothesis objects `A` and `W` (canonical per cairn-m0-e0s.3, `target_family:'gate_plan_fixture'`, `method_identity:{interface_version:'gate_plan_fixture/1', params:{}}`, differing in `declared_parameter_ranges` — `A` `{bits:[1,1]}`, `W` `{bits:[2,2]}` — so `H(A) ≠ H(W)` and recording `A` never hands `W` a ticket when the plan re-runs against the same substrate), a fixture `CostProfile` with one declared size at 0.01 core-s, and a fixture `skill_identity_hash`; the launch shape is `{declared_tier, hypothesis_key, method_identity: the object's, cost_profile: the fixture profile, inputs: its one size, budget_remaining: 1e6, skill_identity_hash: the fixture identity}`. `waiver_cannot_advance`: asserts `attestation_record_matches(attest, 0, BLAKE3 of the fixture waiver)` — the record `cairn attest init` appended naming `H(W)` (cairn-m0-e0s.10); a missing or altered record 0 fails the step — then admits the launch with `declared_tier:1, hypothesis_key:H(W)` (no hypothesis object recorded for `W`) and observes `TierRefused` with `ticket-absent` among its reasons and no `tickets` row for `H(W)` (= `no-ticket`), and asserts the bundle's `waivable_checks == []`. `tier_gate_selftest_two_above`: records `A` in `hypothesis_objects` if absent (the harness writer; a same-hash insert is a no-op, cairn-m0-e0s.4) so `H(A)` holds a Tier-0 ticket, then admits the launch with `declared_tier:2, hypothesis_key:H(A)` and observes `TierRefused` whose reasons include `tier-two-above` and a `tier_refusals` row — the gate collects every applicable reason (cairn-m0-e0s.10), so the uncertified fixture identity does not mask the planted one; each step writes a `gate_runs` row (gate='gate_plan', plan_step, result pass|fail|blocked, reasons, bundle+pin hash); the first failing step blocks all later steps (`result='blocked', reasons=['blocked-by:<step>']`).
- `GatePlan.run(bundle, substrate, attest_path) -> PlanResult` (`attest_path` is the global `--attest` the `waiver_cannot_advance` step reads record 0 from); non-zero exit on any failure; a missing plan, an unknown step kind, or a plan lacking any of the required self-test steps (`verifier_selftest_pass`, `verifier_selftest_fail_xP_ne_Q`, `verifier_selftest_crash`, `verifier_selftest_crash_control`, `canon_kat` — the must-PASS and must-FAIL halves of the verifier's pair, the crash pair, and the canonicalizer's vectors; §4's discipline is a pair per gate, so a plan holding only the FAIL half is refused) → fail closed before any step runs (`missing-required-selftest`).
- `uv run cairn gate selftest [--json]` (registered through cairn-m0-e0s.17, `read_only=False` — it writes `gate_runs` rows — `json=True`): exit 0 iff every step passes, 2 GATE_REFUSED on a failing or blocked step, `PlanInvalid` or `BundlePinMismatch` (`next_command`: the re-pin sequence of cairn-m0-e0s.10 for the mismatch, `cairn gate selftest --json --log DEBUG` for a failing step), 3 ENVIRONMENT when gp, the bundle, the pin or the attestation file is missing (the `--bundle`-absent case is the real producer of 3 that cairn-m0-e0s.17 names); bead m0-e2e-slice (cairn-m0-e0s.14) calls it first. Logging: one record per step (step, expected, observed, gate_runs row id, wall_ms) at INFO; fixture stdin/stdout/stderr digests at DEBUG; `--json` emits one document with `schema_version` and the same per-step fields.
TESTS (integration, `tests/integration/test_gateplan.py`): full plan green against the built bundle; temp bundle without the `xP≠Q` step → plan refuses to run; a weakened accept predicate (`{rc:0, stdout:null, stderr_empty:false}` in a writable bundle copy re-pinned for the test, so the gate under test is the real driver + the real gp with a weakened predicate, not a mock) → plan fails at `verifier_selftest_crash` (the rc-0 overflow is now read as OK) and later steps are `blocked` — the `xP≠Q` step still fails correctly under that predicate because gp quits 1 there, which is exactly why the rc-0 crash step exists; a bundle copy whose `verifier_script` has the `ellmul(E,P,x)==Q` check removed (re-pinned) → plan fails at `verifier_selftest_fail_xP_ne_Q` and later steps are `blocked`; malformed plan row → fail closed; expected-result mismatch recorded with stdout/stderr digests; caplog holds one record per step.
UNIT (`tests/unit/test_gateplan_validation.py`, no gp): plan validation — a missing required step, an unknown step kind, a duplicate step name and an expected-result value outside the vocabulary are each refused before any step runs with the named reason; the blocking logic over a synthetic step sequence — the first failure blocks every later step and each blocked row names the blocker (`blocked-by:<step>`); a plan with zero steps is refused.

TEST PLAN (shapes)
- Fuzzing (`tests/unit/test_gateplan_fuzz.py`, Hypothesis ≥ 500, no gp, no substrate writes): the loader `GatePlan.load(plan_rows)` over arbitrary plan documents — `st.lists(st.dictionaries(st.text(), st.recursive(st.none() | st.booleans() | st.integers() | st.text(), lambda c: st.lists(c) | st.dictionaries(st.text(), c))))`, `None`, a scalar, an empty list, a 10 000-step plan — and over mutations of the committed plan (drop one required step, duplicate a step name, rename `expect`, unknown `step` kind, `expect` outside the vocabulary, a fixture field of the wrong type) — every malformed plan is refused with `PlanInvalid(reason)` naming the first offending path before any step runs, with zero `gate_runs` rows written (a reader connection counts them) and zero subprocess spawns (the `isolation_guard` spy); the committed plan itself loads unchanged; planted mutants in `tests/mutants/gateplan_mutants.py`: `loader_skips_unknown_steps` (ignores instead of refusing) and `loader_runs_valid_prefix` (runs steps up to the first bad one) — each killed; seed corpus `tests/fuzz_corpus/gateplan/` holds the planted negatives (missing `verifier_selftest_fail_xP_ne_Q`, FAIL-half-only plan, duplicate step, vocabulary miss, empty plan, `expect: null`) replayed as `@example`s.
- Property over the blocking logic (`tests/unit/test_gateplan_validation.py`, Hypothesis ≥ 500): for any outcome sequence from `st.lists(st.sampled_from(['pass', 'fail']), min_size=1, max_size=20)` applied to synthetic steps, with `i` the first `fail` index, rows `< i` are `pass`, row `i` is `fail`, every row `> i` is `blocked` with `reasons == ['blocked-by:<step_i>']`, and with no `fail` every row is `pass` — kills `continue_after_failure` and `blocks_name_wrong_step`.
- Failure-path convergence: the plan-validation refusals (missing required step × 5, unknown kind, duplicate name, vocabulary miss, zero steps) are one `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over `(plan_delta, expected_reason)` with `match=`; the two weakened-bundle integration cases (weakened accept predicate, weakened `verify.gp`) stay separate since each re-pins a different bundle and observes a different failing step.
- Every integration plan run calls `db_snapshot` (`gate_runs` per result) after the run, so a step that wrote two rows or none is visible in `test.log.jsonl`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run cairn gate selftest --json` exits 0 listing every step `pass` with its gate_runs row id (the crash step's observed `FAIL backend-crash` and its control's `OK` both count as `pass` against their expectations); `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_gateplan.py tests/unit/test_gateplan_validation.py -q` green.
- Planted negative: a weakened-accept-predicate bundle copy must make the plan FAIL at the crash step and block the rest; a bundle copy whose `verify.gp` lacks the `xP == Q` check must make it FAIL at the `xP≠Q` step; a plan missing a required self-test step must be refused before any step runs (exit 2); `--bundle` naming a missing file exits 3 with a `next_command`; an attestation file lacking the fixture waiver at record 0 must fail the waiver step; the two-above step must observe `tier-two-above` in the refusal's reasons (a `TierRefused` for another reason alone fails the step); the crash fixture returning anything but `FAIL backend-crash`, or its control returning anything but `OK`, fails the plan. Asserted.
- No-Claim: a green plan proves the fixtures behave as planted on this machine at this bundle hash; it is not evidence about any claim.
- `tests/unit/test_gateplan_fuzz.py` green at ≥ 500 examples: every malformed plan is refused with `PlanInvalid` naming its path, zero `gate_runs` rows and zero spawns; `loader_skips_unknown_steps` and `loader_runs_valid_prefix` killed; `tests/fuzz_corpus/gateplan/` replayed; the blocking property holds over random outcome sequences with `continue_after_failure` and `blocks_name_wrong_step` killed; the validation refusals are one parametrized test.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.

comments.text:
Carried forward from cairn-m0-e0s.10 (commit 2531d3f), because this bead reads gate_runs.

A gate_runs row is content-addressed: run_id is the node hash of the canonical gate run, whose fields are gate, bundle_hash, pin_hash, plan_step, instance_hash, statement_hash, result, reasons and `at`. Two facts follow.

The canonical form names no launch. It carries no hypothesis key and no skill identity, so a row says which verdict was reached under which bundle, never by whom. For the tier gate the launch identity survives in tier_refusals (which carries hypothesis_key, but only for refusals) and in the JSON log record `tiergate.admit`.

`at` is second-resolution (cli.now_iso). Two decisions identical in every canonical field within one second collapse to a single row through claims._insert_once, which is the substrate's designed append-only-and-content-addressed behavior, not a write that failed.

For a gate plan runner this matters where a step is expected to run more than once, or where "the step ran" is read off a row count. Distinguish steps by plan_step, which is exactly the free field for it, rather than by counting rows.

Pinned by tests/integration/test_tier_gate.py::test_two_indistinguishable_decisions_in_one_second_are_one_content_addressed_row so the behavior is a stated property rather than a surprise.

title: M0: justify(evidence, statement_hash): kind→max-class map, producer-standing ceiling, coverage check (interval containment / categorical equality / assumption ⊆), lattice violations, review_verdict digest rule, refuted-version rule, append-only attributed tag history
description:
WHY (PLAN §7): the tag is derived, never set. Each evidence kind has a maximum class; `justify` checks the evidence's declared target names the exact statement hash, its declared population is a superset of the statement's scope and its assumptions a subset of the statement's, and returns a typed justification or a lattice/coverage violation — never a boolean. A weaker class may inform, never justify. Every tag transition is an append-only attributed tag_history row with an evidence pointer. PROVEN needs a `lean_artifact` AND an `approve` `review_verdict` on the same statement hash whose digest matches the attestation file (else the row is absent).

WHAT (`src/cairn/justify.py`; tables from bead m0-claims-schema = cairn-m0-e0s.5)
- `justify(evidence, statement, ctx) -> Justification | CoverageViolation | LatticeViolation | Absent | Pending`. Classes are totally ordered SPECULATION < CONJECTURE < STRONG-EMPIRICAL < PROVEN.
- Kind → max class: `lean_artifact` + visible `approve` verdict on the same statement hash → PROVEN (without it → `Pending(human_review)`, claim stays at its pre-review tag); `ladder_table` verdict KEEP — or KEEP_IN_SAMPLE when the statement's `scope.size_interval ⊆ evidence.in_sample_sizes` — whose own attempt carries a passed reproducibility record (`repro_records.passed = 1` reached through `evidence.repro_record_hash`) → STRONG-EMPIRICAL; same table with the record absent or grade `AuditOnly` → CONJECTURE ceiling; any other table verdict → justifies nothing; `statistical` / `repro_node` → ≤ STRONG-EMPIRICAL on the declared population, EXCEPT for a statement whose typed fields carry a cost model (`claim_statements.quantities.cost_model IS NOT NULL`) → CONJECTURE ceiling; `model_proof` → ≤ CONJECTURE; `counterexample_hunt_record` SURVIVED → CONJECTURE (a ticket, not a promotion), KILLED → the statement moves to terminal `refuted` with the evidence pointer.
- Producer-standing ceiling: producer is a certified skill revision (its `skill_certificates.selftest_summary`, cairn-m0-e0s.4/.7) with no STRONG-EMPIRICAL basis covering the attempt's inputs — every `corpus_origins` entry `author_supplied`, `randomized_arm` false, and no `cross_check` whose `independent_range` (an axis-aligned interval record over the input fields, `{bits:[lo,hi]}`, read with the same containment comparator the coverage check uses) contains the attempt's inputs → cap at CONJECTURE; a gate-bundle producer or a gate run is not capped by this rule.
- Coverage: `population.target_family == scope.target_family`; numeric intervals of the population contain the statement's (size and every parameter range); `population.assumptions ⊆ statement.assumptions`; otherwise CoverageViolation (typed: which field).
- Disowned evidence (attempt `disowned_at` not null) → Absent; an `AuditOnly` node (by `effective_grade`, cairn-m0-e0s.4) → the CONJECTURE ceiling, never Absent and never higher (inadmissible above it, §3 — the done-when's AuditOnly case). Refuted statement + any positive class → LatticeViolation. A class offered above the kind's maximum (e.g. `statistical` for PROVEN) → LatticeViolation.
- `derive_tag(statement_hash)` = strongest class justified by any evidence node targeting it; writes a tag_history row (actor 'gate:justify', evidence pointer, typed justification); a downgrade requires an evidence pointer; nothing edited in place.
- `review_verdicts` visible only through `attestation_record_matches` (`src/cairn/attest.py`, bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate = cairn-m0-e0s.10). A waiver is not evidence: `evidence_nodes.kind` admits no waiver kind, `justify` reads the attestation file for `review_verdict` records and nothing else, and `derive_tag` is unchanged by a waiver record naming the statement hash — the claim half of §4's waiver-cannot-advance fixture (the tier half is cairn-m0-e0s.10's).
- CLI: `uv run cairn justify --statement <hash> [--json]` (registered through cairn-m0-e0s.17, `read_only=False` — `derive_tag` appends `tag_history` — `json=True`) prints the derived tag and the justifying evidence hash; `--json` → `{schema_version, statement_hash, tag, justified_by, evidence: [{hash, kind, result}]}` listing every evidence node targeting the statement with its typed result; exit 0 whenever a tag is derived (SPECULATION with no evidence included — never 1 for an empty result), 1 USER_INPUT for a hash that names no `claim_statements` row, 3 ENVIRONMENT when `--db` cannot be opened. Logging: every `justify` call logs (statement hash, evidence hash, kind, result type, class or violation field) and every `derive_tag` logs the transition through `cairn.log`.
TESTS (integration, real substrate + attestation file; `tests/integration/test_justify.py`) — the §13 done-when set, named test ids: synthetic statement S (family 'toy_curve', size [30,50], assumptions {A1}); ladder_table KEEP on [30,60] ⊇ scope with passed repro record → STRONG-EMPIRICAL; repro absent → CONJECTURE; repro record with `passed = 0` → CONJECTURE; grade AuditOnly → CONJECTURE; population [40,50] → CoverageViolation(size_interval); assumptions {A1,A2} → CoverageViolation(assumptions); family mismatch → CoverageViolation(target_family); statistical offered for PROVEN → LatticeViolation; statistical for a cost-model statement → CONJECTURE ceiling; KEEP_IN_SAMPLE with scope ⊆ in_sample_sizes → STRONG-EMPIRICAL and with scope ⊄ → nothing; lean_artifact + approve verdict with matching digest → PROVEN; same with a forged digest → verdict absent → not PROVEN (Pending); disowned ladder_table → Absent; a producer with an all-`author_supplied` synthetic selftest_summary → CONJECTURE ceiling while the same node from a producer with a covering arm is not capped; statement moved to refuted then a KEEP table offered → LatticeViolation; a waiver record appended through `cairn attest append --kind waiver` naming S → `derive_tag(S)` unchanged and `tag_history` gains no row; tag_history holds one row per transition and refuses UPDATE; caplog holds one record per call.
UNIT (`tests/unit/test_justify_rules.py`, pure): the coverage comparator (interval containment incl. equal endpoints, categorical equality, assumption subset incl. empty set); the kind→max-class table; the class order; the producer-standing rule over synthetic summaries, including a summary whose only covering basis is a cross-check whose `independent_range` contains the attempt's inputs (not capped) and the same summary with the inputs outside that range (capped).

TEST PLAN (shapes)
- Metamorphic relations (`tests/unit/test_justify_properties.py` over the pure rules, Hypothesis ≥ 500 per relation; generators from `tests/factories.py`: scopes with `size_interval = [lo, hi]`, `lo ≤ hi` from `st.integers(20, 80)`, `param_ranges` as 0–3 axis-aligned intervals, `assumption_set` from `st.frozensets(st.sampled_from(['A1'..'A6']))`, `target_family` from a three-word vocabulary, evidence kinds from the CHECK vocabulary, `repro ∈ {absent, passed, failed}`, grade ∈ {Replayable, Verifiable, AuditOnly}, producer summaries over origins/arm/cross_check; planted mutants in `tests/mutants/justify_mutants.py`, each relation's `test_mutant_<name>_is_killed` asserting the relation fails on it): MR-W widening and narrowing — for any `e` the generator builds with a population containing `S`'s scope (every interval `[lo, hi]` with `lo ≤ S.lo` and `hi ≥ S.hi`, equal endpoints drawn often, the family equal, the assumptions `⊆`), `justify(e, S)` is a `Justification` — the precondition is structural, never computed by the function under test, so a comparator that rejects equal endpoints is seen — and for any `e'` equal to `e` with every population interval widened (`[lo − d1, hi + d2]`, `d ≥ 0`) `justify(e', S)` is a `Justification` of the same class, while for any `e''` equal to `e` with one population endpoint moved strictly inside `S`'s scope (`lo'' > S.lo` or `hi'' < S.hi` on any one interval) `justify(e'', S)` is `CoverageViolation` naming that field — kills `comparator_strict_containment` (requires strict `⊂`, failing on equal endpoints) by the equal-endpoint cases and `comparator_checks_lo_only` by the `hi'' < S.hi` cases; MR-A assumption — for any `e` with `justify(e, S)` a `Justification`, adding any assumption `a ∉ S.assumption_set` to `e.population.assumptions` always yields `CoverageViolation(assumptions)` — kills `comparator_assumptions_superset` (tests `⊇` instead of `⊆`); MR-M monotone in evidence strength — for any statement and any list of evidence nodes, `class(derive_tag)` is non-decreasing as nodes are appended (the terminal `refuted` path excluded from the generator) and never exceeds `max_class(kind)` of the strongest node — kills `derive_takes_last_node` (uses the most recent node) and `kind_table_off_by_one` (`statistical → PROVEN`); MR-C ceiling — for any evidence node and any producer summary, `class ≤ kind_ceiling`, and a summary that is all-`author_supplied` with `randomized_arm = False` and no `cross_check` whose `independent_range` contains the attempt's inputs caps at CONJECTURE — kills `producer_rule_ignores_range` (treats any cross_check as covering); composite MR-W ∘ MR-A (widen, then add an assumption ⇒ still `CoverageViolation(assumptions)`).
- Fuzz-shaped robustness (same file, ≥ 500): the coverage comparator over arbitrary interval records (`lo > hi`, missing axes, extra axes, negative sizes, huge ints, `None` endpoints) returns a typed violation naming the field or a `Justification`, never an unhandled exception.
- Failure-path convergence: the kind → max-class table is one `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over `(kind, verdict, repro, grade, expected_class_or_violation)`; the §13 done-when cases stay one parametrized integration test in `tests/integration/test_justify.py` whose `ids=` are the bead's named case ids, since their setups differ only in data from `tests/factories.py`; every justify integration case calls `db_snapshot` (`tag_history` row count) after `derive_tag`.
- Layer: relations and tables unit (pure comparator, kind table, producer rule); `derive_tag`, the attestation-file visibility rule and the waiver-moves-no-tag case integration (real substrate, real attestation file).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_justify.py tests/unit/test_justify_rules.py -q` green with every done-when case named in the test ids; `uv run cairn justify --statement <hash>` prints the derived tag and justifying evidence hash, `--json` one document with `schema_version`, and an unknown hash exits 1.
- Planted negative: statistical→PROVEN must be a LatticeViolation; missing or failed repro must cap at CONJECTURE; forged verdict digest must not yield PROVEN; a coverage gap must be a CoverageViolation; an all-`author_supplied` producer must be capped; a waiver record must move no tag. Any of these returning a positive class fails the bead.
- No-Claim: all evidence is synthetic; no ladder, Lean artifact or real verdict exists at M0; the Tier-2/3 branches (KEEP_IN_SAMPLE scope, hunt records) are exercised by construction only.
- MR-W, MR-A, MR-M, MR-C and MR-W∘MR-A in `tests/unit/test_justify_properties.py` green at ≥ 500 examples; every mutant in `tests/mutants/justify_mutants.py` (`comparator_strict_containment`, `comparator_checks_lo_only`, `comparator_assumptions_superset`, `derive_takes_last_node`, `kind_table_off_by_one`, `producer_rule_ignores_range`) killed — a survivor fails the bead; the comparator never raises unhandled on 500 arbitrary interval records.
- The kind → max-class table and the §13 done-when cases are each one parametrized test (the done-when case ids are the `ids=`), all built from `tests/factories.py`; `tag_history` counts land in `test.log.jsonl` via `db_snapshot`.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment, so the compliance audit can re-run it without reading the session.

## Bullet 2 — planted negatives, each observed failing

Each guard was removed with scripts/mutation-check.sh, which exits 0 only when the
mutation went red and the file came back byte-identical. Not one was assumed.

an endpoint moved inside the scope names the field), MR-A, MR-W composed with MR-A,

## Bullet 4 — one parametrized table each, and db_snapshot

The kind -> max-class table is one parametrize over (kind, verdict, repro, grade,
cost_model, expected). The done-when set is one parametrize whose ids= are the bead's

## Two disagreements with the bead text

1. The declared signature returns Justification | CoverageViolation | LatticeViolation |
   Absent | Pending. A counterexample_hunt_record with verdict KILLED returns a sixth
   type, Refutation(evidence_hash). The bead's own kind map requires a KILLED hunt to
   move the statement to terminal refuted carrying the evidence pointer, which none of
   the five expresses; the alternative was keying the refutation path on an Absent
   reason string. Recorded for the downstream callers on cairn-m1-cqt.1.

2. The bead maps the mutant kind_table_off_by_one to MR-M. Measured, MR-M does not kill
   it: KIND_MAX_CLASS is applied through weakest() as a cap, so raising statistical to
   PROVEN never raises a derived class and the ceiling relation stays green under the
   mutant. The relation that sees it is the offered-class lattice check, so MR-L was
   written and the mutant maps to it. The assertion is the observed truth.

## The test audit

A fresh subagent ran /optimal-tests --audit over these files against the bead. It
returned 13 findings and proved every "untested" claim with mutation-check.sh rather
than inferring it from coverage. All 13 were applied, none declined. Nine mutations that
survived at audit time are now killed, each re-executed in the main context at 8836bb1.

It found one source defect: derive_tag wrote the refuting evidence hash into tag_history
but returned the ladder's hash in Derivation.justified_by, so a refuted claim's history
and the CLI output named different nodes. Fixed; the Derivation now carries the pointer
the row carries.

It also found the property suite was red in five of ten runs at HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=dev,
because MR-C discarded 57% of draws at an assume() and two mutant kills depended on a
rare draw. The filters are early returns and the killing cases are pinned with @example.
Ten dev runs after the fix: 20 passed, ten times.

## No-Claim

All evidence in these tests is synthetic. No ladder, no Lean artifact and no real
reviewer verdict exists at M0, so the PROVEN path, the KEEP_IN_SAMPLE branch and the
counterexample_hunt_record branches are exercised by construction only. The producer-
standing ceiling reads the attempt's inputs from the evidence node's own
population.param_ranges rather than from the attempt's recipe; at M0 the two agree by
construction and a real ladder_table may not. Both gaps are recorded on cairn-m1-cqt.1;
the real-verdict half is recorded on cairn-m1-cqt.5.

Nothing here says a claim IS true. justify derives what a body of evidence licenses under
the §7 rules; whether the evidence is any good is the ladder's, the gate's and the
reviewer's question, none of which exist yet.

## Not independently verified

Only one agent audited these tests, and I wrote both the code and the tests it audited.
Re-executing its cited commands in the main context is not independent verification, and
neither is a second pass by me. The strongest thing a skeptic can re-run without trusting
me: uv run pytest tests/unit/test_justify_properties.py -q, where each of the six named
mutants must make its own relation fail, so the suite cannot pass by the mutants being
toothless.

The baseline was red before this bead started. tests/integration/test_runner.py's rusage
test borrowed the 40-bit toy_curve budget for a CPU-burner fixture that needs 72% of it
on an idle machine; under the full suite it crossed and returned BUDGET_EXCEEDED. Fixed
first, in its own commit 6249447 ahead of any bead work, with the repro and its inversion
in the message and the assertion left byte-identical. Its oracle was re-proved live by
mutation (FIXTURE_GRANDCHILD 1 -> 0, KILLED).

title: M0: GC roots table + reachability over lineage; only blobs collectable; cache completeness on missing blob; dry-run CLI
description:
WHY (PLAN §3 retention): keep lineage + certificates forever, GC the giant intermediate blobs once their derivation is recorded and the result verified. Roots = recipes, ledger rows, certificates, recorded divergences; liveness = reachability from roots over lineage edges; only blobs are collectable; a cached result is served only if every blob it references is present, otherwise recomputed.

WHAT (`src/cairn/gc.py`; the `roots(root_kind, node_hash)` table is defined in bead m0-substrate-core = cairn-m0-e0s.4, which also inserts the recipe, certificate and divergence roots as it writes them): `add_root(root_kind, node_hash)` for the ledger-row kind that M1 writes; `reachable()` = BFS from every roots row over `lineage` treated as undirected — the conservative reading of 'reachability from roots over lineage edges': a blob is live while any path of `lineage` rows joins it to a root, so a rooted recipe's input blobs (`'input'` edges) and its attempts' output blobs (`'output_of'`/`'member'` edges, the set cairn-m0-e0s.9 writes) are both kept, and a blob with no path to any root is the only collectable thing; `collect(dry_run)` deletes blob rows not reachable and writes a `gc_runs` record (count, bytes, at); nodes/edges/attempts/receipts/roots are never deleted (append-only triggers from cairn-m0-e0s.4 refuse). `uv run cairn gc [--dry-run] [--yes] [--json]` — dry-run by default (the dangerous-op gating of cairn-m0-e0s.17; registered `dangerous=True, gating='--yes', dry_run_default=True` — without `dry_run_default` the registry's `main` exits 2 before `run` whenever `--yes` is absent (`cli._refuse_ungated`) and the flagless listing below could never happen; with it `run` branches on `ns.yes` itself: absent → list and exit 0, present → collect): without `--yes` it lists the candidates and deletes nothing, `--dry-run` being the explicit spelling of that default, and only `--yes` collects; `--json` → `{schema_version, dry_run, roots, reachable, candidates: [{hash, size}], bytes, deleted}`; exit 0 in both modes (an empty candidate list is 0, never 1), 3 ENVIRONMENT when `--db` cannot be opened, 5 CONFLICT when a second connection holds a write transaction past the busy timeout (the real producer of 5 that cairn-m0-e0s.17 names); each run logs (roots counted, reachable count, candidate count, bytes, dry_run) through `cairn.log` and at DEBUG the candidate hashes.
TESTS (integration, `tests/integration/test_gc.py`): recipe R (root) → attempt → manifest → blob B1; orphan blob B2; `collect` removes B2, keeps B1; delete B1's row manually (simulated loss) → `serve(R)` returns None (recompute path; links to the substrate serve test); collect on an empty DB is a no-op; a certificate node is a root and its blob survives; a non-reproducible recipe's two attempts are both rooted as divergences (cairn-m0-e0s.4) and survive; `gc` without `--yes` (and with `--dry-run`) deletes nothing and lists exactly the orphan; `gc --yes` removes it; `gc --yes` while a second connection holds `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` exits 5 after the busy timeout.
UNIT (`tests/unit/test_gc_reachability.py`, pure): `reachable()` over synthetic root sets and edge lists — a chain, a diamond, a cycle (terminates; every member reachable once), a disconnected component (unreachable), a root with no edges (reachable alone), and an empty root set (nothing reachable); the collectable set equals blobs minus reachable in each case.

TEST PLAN (shapes)
- Metamorphic relations (`tests/unit/test_gc_properties.py`, Hypothesis ≥ 500, synthetic graphs: a node pool of 1–30 hashes, `edges ∈ st.lists(st.tuples(node, node, st.sampled_from(['output_of', 'input', 'member', 'certifies'])))`, `roots ∈ st.frozensets(node)`, `blobs ⊆ nodes`; planted mutants in `tests/mutants/gc_mutants.py`, each relation's `test_mutant_<name>_is_killed`): MR-R adding a root never shrinks — `reachable(roots ∪ {r}, E) ⊇ reachable(roots, E)` for any `r` — kills `reachable_from_last_root_only`; MR-E removing an edge never grows, and removing a node's only edge drops it — `reachable(roots, E \ {e}) ⊆ reachable(roots, E)` for any `e ∈ E`, and when `e` is the only edge touching a reachable non-root node `v`, `v ∉ reachable(roots, E \ {e})` — the second clause is what kills `reachable_cached_by_roots_only` (a memo keyed on roots alone returns the stale larger set, which the bare `⊆` cannot tell from the correct one); MR-Sym reachability is symmetric in edge direction — `reachable(roots, E) == reachable(roots, reversed(E))` — kills `reachable_directed_child_to_parent` (the walk that would collect every output blob of a rooted recipe); MR-Comp complement — `collectable(roots, E, blobs) == blobs − reachable(roots, E)` and `collectable ∩ reachable == ∅` — kills `collectable_includes_rooted_blob`; idempotence (integration) — with 150 orphan blobs planted (more than one page, so a one-page collector leaves survivors) `collect(); collect()` removes 150 on the first run and zero on the second — kills `collect_one_page_only` (deletes only the first 100 candidates; against a single orphan it would survive).
- Failure-path convergence: the reachability shapes (chain, diamond, cycle, disconnected component, root without edges, empty root set) are one `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over `(roots, edges, expected_reachable)`; the integration cases stay separate (each builds a different real lineage through the substrate).
- Every GC integration test calls `db_snapshot` (`blobs`, `nodes`, `lineage`, `roots`, `gc_runs` counts) before and after `collect`, so a deleted node or a surviving orphan is visible in `test.log.jsonl`.
- Layer: relations and shapes unit (pure `reachable` over synthetic edges); `collect`, the append-only refusal and the serve-on-missing-blob path integration.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_gc.py tests/unit/test_gc_reachability.py -q` green; `uv run cairn gc` (and `gc --dry-run`) lists exactly the orphan and deletes nothing; a following `uv run cairn gc --yes` removes it and the `gc_runs` record names count and bytes; `gc --yes` under a held write transaction exits 5.
- Planted negative: the rooted blob must survive (collecting it fails the test); gc attempting to delete a node must be refused by the append-only trigger; a run without `--yes` that deletes fails the test.
- No-Claim: GC over the M0 edge kinds only; the hash-chained log and checkpoint (M2) are not roots yet.
- MR-R, MR-E, MR-Sym, MR-Comp in `tests/unit/test_gc_properties.py` green at ≥ 500 examples and the idempotence case green in integration; every mutant in `tests/mutants/gc_mutants.py` (`reachable_from_last_root_only`, `reachable_cached_by_roots_only`, `reachable_directed_child_to_parent`, `collectable_includes_rooted_blob`, `collect_one_page_only`) killed — a survivor fails the bead; the six reachability shapes are one parametrized test; `db_snapshot` before/after `collect` appears in `test.log.jsonl`.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
Carried forward from cairn-m0-e0s.10 (commit 2531d3f), because this bead reads gate_runs.

A gate_runs row is content-addressed: run_id is the node hash of the canonical gate run, whose fields are gate, bundle_hash, pin_hash, plan_step, instance_hash, statement_hash, result, reasons and `at`. Two facts follow.

The canonical form names no launch. It carries no hypothesis key and no skill identity, so a row says which verdict was reached under which bundle, never by whom. For the tier gate the launch identity survives in tier_refusals (which carries hypothesis_key, but only for refusals) and in the JSON log record `tiergate.admit`.

`at` is second-resolution (cli.now_iso). Two decisions identical in every canonical field within one second collapse to a single row through claims._insert_once, which is the substrate's designed append-only-and-content-addressed behavior, not a write that failed.

For a gate plan runner this matters where a step is expected to run more than once, or where "the step ran" is read off a row count. Distinguish steps by plan_step, which is exactly the free field for it, rather than by counting rows.

Pinned by tests/integration/test_tier_gate.py::test_two_indistinguishable_decisions_in_one_second_are_one_content_addressed_row so the behavior is a stated property rather than a surprise.

comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.7 (toy_curve self-test), a property to know before touching the
goldens.

tests/goldens/toy_curve_selftest_transcript.golden and
tests/goldens/toy_curve_certificate.golden are coupled to
toy_curve.IDENTITY_SOURCES, which is src/cairn/pari.py,
src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py and src/cairn/skills/toy_curve_corpus.json.

The self-test's randomized arm seeds from
`first 8 bytes of H(implementation_revision || 'selftest-seed')`, so editing any
of those three files moves the seed, the arm's 30-bit curve, the transcript and
the certificate. Within a fixed revision the transcript is exactly byte-equal
across the double run, which is why the golden compares exactly.

Consequence: an edit to src/cairn/pari.py that has nothing to do with the
self-test still requires
`UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py`
plus an attributed commit. That is the same rule as re-minting the certificate,
so the regeneration and the re-mint belong in one commit. tests/goldens/PROVENANCE.md
grades the transcript golden volatility 3 for this reason, not the 2 the
cairn-m0-e0s.7 spec predicted.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
Carried forward from cairn-m0-e0s.11 (commit 4a4bb69), because this bead calls
cairn gate selftest first.

The gate plan's two tier-gate steps use a fixture skill_identity_hash that no
substrate certifies. tiergate.predicate_reasons adds UNCERTIFIED whenever
sub.certified(identity) is false, so both fixture launches always collect at
least one reason and the gate never admits them.

Two consequences for anyone reading gateplan.py or extending the plan.

The tier gate collects every applicable reason rather than short-circuiting, so
the planted reason is present alongside UNCERTIFIED. The step checks membership
(tier-two-above in reasons, ticket-absent in reasons), never equality. A step
written against the whole reason tuple would break the first time an unrelated
predicate fires.

_run_waiver's ticket-present branch is defensive and unreachable today: it fires
only if the gate mints a ticket for the waiver hypothesis, which requires an
admission, which UNCERTIFIED prevents. It is asserted by no test, and that is
stated rather than papered over. If a later milestone certifies a fixture
identity, that branch becomes live and needs a test before it is trusted.

Pinned by tests/integration/test_gateplan.py::test_a_recorded_waiver_hypothesis_removes_ticket_absent_and_fails_the_waiver_step,
which reaches the neighbouring branch by pre-recording the hypothesis object.

tests/goldens/m0_run_transcript.golden holds 20 lines: seven gate-plan steps with
expected and observed verdicts, nine slice steps, three verifier arms with reason
codes, and the refusal. scrub() performs 14 hash substitutions and 7 timing ones,
and the test asserts a node hash is present before scrubbing and absent after, so
a scrub that stops matching fails loudly rather than baking in a local hash.

tests/_checks.py:4 scans tests/e2e; test_no_mocks_in_integration: 2 passed.

## Defects this bead fixed outside its own files

bundle.waiver_hypothesis raised a bare KeyError on a plan with no fixtures block,
which reaches an operator as BACKEND when malformed gate config is a refusal.
cli.py gained json_parent so --json binds after a nested subcommand.

## Disagreements with the bead text, resolved by observation

recipe.inputs is Map(STR, BLOBREF), so the input document is a content-addressed
blob rather than a string map; this is what makes the recipe key depend on bits.
claim_statement.scope is a declared struct, and quantities.units is Map(STR, STR),
so the instance travels as decimal strings.

Node A carries the output manifest and not the receipt: a receipt records wall
time and rss, so a node containing one cannot have the same hash on a cache hit,
and the same seed replaying to the same node A is an acceptance criterion.

The uncertified refusal does create the substrate and does run the whole gate plan
first, because the plan is step 1 and the certified check is step 2. The bead's
requirement is no attempt row, which holds.

## No-Claim

A 40-bit toy instance on one Mac. Nothing about ECDLP or any research claim; the
honest baseline is an invariant this slice does not touch.

Specifically not established: any platform other than macOS (the pin and
attestation file use chflags; cairn-hcl owns the Linux arm); that the verifier is
correct beyond these instances; that the cost profile's numbers are accurate.

Not covered by any test, and stated rather than papered over: the BACKEND path for
an attempt closing FAIL is unreachable without a genuinely broken skill;
_served_document's malformed-manifest guards are fail-closed defense with no
reachable trigger; the submitter-named guard in run_slice cannot be killed by a
test without breaking the verifier itself; --log DEBUG is not exercised against
m0-run, though the gate-plan tests cover the DEBUG digest records.

Not independently verified: the test audit was a subagent whose findings were
re-executed here before being acted on, but no second party reviewed this close.
The mutation evidence is self-run.

title: M0: measure one 60-bit Pollard rho with cypari2 (operator decision 2): ops/s, extrapolated wall, a completed 40-bit rho verified by the Tier-0 verifier; record for the M1 compiled-baseline decision
description:

PARI-only (gmpy2 comparison is M1, decision 1). Logs progress (ops, elapsed, rate) every 10⁶ ops through `cairn.log`. Run in the background; not on the M0 done-when path.

- Layer: the command is a measurement, not a gate; its one pure function `rate_report(ops, elapsed_s) -> RateRow | RefusedTooFewOps` is unit-tested in `tests/unit/test_measure_rho_rate.py` as one `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over `ops ∈ {0, 10**6 - 1, 10**6, 10**7}` (the first two refused with `match='fewer than 1e6 ops'`, the last two reported with ops/s and the extrapolated 60-bit wall tagged CONJECTURE); the planted off-by-one negative is an integration test through the real Tier-0 verifier (cairn-m0-e0s.8) in `tests/integration/test_measure_rho40.py`, which also runs the 40-bit walk to completion and asserts its `x` verifies; the 60-bit capped run itself is not a test (it lives in the brief).

1416 at 6c98471 -> 1452 after .13 -> 1472, +20 for this bead.

WHAT THE AUDIT PASS CHANGED, AND THE DEFECT IT CAUGHT

A fresh Opus /optimal-tests --audit returned nine findings, three able to ship a
defect. All nine were applied, none declined. The first is the one worth reading:

  A NUMBER NO RUN PRODUCED. §9 recorded the 40-bit expected op count as 1218031 in
  both rows and in prose. The true birthday bound for that instance's order
  (n = 945003441719) is 1218362, which I recomputed independently:
  int(sqrt(pi*945003441719/2)) = 1218362. Back-solving 1218031 gives
  n = 944488786772, which is no instance in this repository, and measure.py was
  unchanged between the commit that wrote the brief and the one before it, so no run
  at any commit emitted 1218031. It was invented. Corrected in all three places, and
  every other number in §9 was then re-derived from a command; no second mismatch.

  THE GUARD THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT WAS A TAUTOLOGY. The test pinning the
  birthday bound asserted expected_rho_ops(RHO60_ORDER) == RHO60_EXPECTED_OPS, and
  RHO60_EXPECTED_OPS is that call, so it read f(x) == f(x). Mutating the formula to
  sqrt(2*order/2) survived all 13 tests. Now pinned to literals. Re-run by me:
  $ bash scripts/mutation-check.sh src/cairn/measure.py \
      'return int(math.sqrt(math.pi * order / 2))' 'return int(math.sqrt(2 * order / 2))' \
      tests/integration/test_measure_rho40.py tests/unit/test_measure_rho_rate.py
  KILLED  by 2 test(s): 2 failed, 18 passed          EXIT=0

  A REAL CORRECTNESS GAP IN THE DISTINGUISHED-POINT KEY. The implementer reported
  this mutant surviving rather than hiding it. The key must carry the y-coordinate,
  because R and -R share an x and only the full point separates a real collision
  from a negation coincidence. At the shipped theta = 2^-10 that coincidence is
  recorded about once in 1024 walks, so the 40-bit seed solves either way and 50
  instrumented walks found zero negations - a second seed would not have exposed it.
  Measured at theta = 2^0 over bits {24,28,32} x seeds 1..20: the full key is 60/60
  correct, the x-only key 39/60 wrong. The suite now runs a real 24-bit walk at
  theta_bits=0 on the seed whose first key collision is a negation; theta_bits was
  made a keyword parameter of rho() rather than monkeypatched, so nothing patches
  module state. Re-run by me:
  $ bash scripts/mutation-check.sh src/cairn/measure.py \
      'key = (xi, int(cur[1])) if len(cur) == 2 else (xi,)' 'key = (xi,)' \
      tests/integration/test_measure_rho40.py tests/unit/test_measure_rho_rate.py
  KILLED  by 1 test(s): 1 failed, 19 passed          EXIT=0

Also unpinned and now pinned, each SURVIVED before and KILLED after: RHO_R 20 -> 7
(3 tests), RHO_THETA_BITS 10 -> 8 (2 tests), the elapsed_s <= 0 guard (1 test). The
successful --json path had no test at all and now asserts the full document with
extrapolated_wall_s recomputed in the test rather than read back.

TWO PLACES THE IMPLEMENTATION DISAGREED WITH A FINDING, BOTH TOWARD MORE RIGOR

  The audit judged all three of rho60_report's BACKEND raises unreachable without a
  mock. One is reachable with none: a tiny --cap-minutes stops the 40-bit walk before
  it solves, and `cairn measure rho60 --cap-ops 100000000 --cap-minutes 0.0001` exits
  4 naming the op count. It now has a real test.

  Moving the --cap-minutes check out of the 10^6-op log block was measured before it
  was chosen. A per-op clock read costs about 8% of the headline rate (means 1357354
  vs 1247270 ops/s over three alternating pairs, non-overlapping). A 1000-op stride
  is inside noise (1357146 vs 1346347, ranges overlap) and takes the cap's
  granularity from ~0.74 s to ~0.74 ms. A test pins RHO_LOG_EVERY % RHO_CLOCK_EVERY.

DISAGREEMENTS WITH THE BEAD TEXT

  The bead estimates ~1.3x10^9 group ops at 60 bits. The birthday bound for the
  actual vector order is 1166326476, about 1.17x10^9. The computed value is used.

  The bead implies 10^8 ops is the smaller of the two budgets. On this machine 10^8
  ops takes 77 to 145 s, so the op cap always binds first and the minute cap is never
  exercised by a default run.

  The bead names --json fields but not where the 40-bit evidence goes. verified_x is
  at top level as the bead requires; a rho40 sub-object, expected_ops, stop,
  instance_hash and versions were added beside it.

  The bead names no seed for the 40-bit instance. Seed 1, matching the 60-bit one.

NO-CLAIM

One seed, one machine, one core, interpreted PARI arithmetic through cypari2, a rate
sampled over the first 10^8 ops of a single walk. The three 60-bit walls are
extrapolations, not completed runs, and carry CONJECTURE. The 1.88x rate spread is
attributed to machine load as an inference from the declared conditions, not an
isolated measurement of scheduler effects. Nothing here claims anything about any
method's asymptotics, about other hardware, or about a compiled implementation's
rate.

Two gaps, each owned by a named open bead:

  The funding call this measurement feeds. PLAN §5's Tier-1 budget is one core,
  minutes; 15 to 28 minutes is not that on any of the three runs, which is the
  condition operator decision 2 named. That is an input, not the decision, and the
  gmpy2 comparison (decision 1) remains unmeasured, so how much of the gap is
  interpreter overhead is unknown. Recorded on cairn-m1-cqt.2, which owns the call.

  Two of rho60_report's three BACKEND refusals - a Tier-0 verifier that refuses the
  recovered x, and a 60-bit order differing from the recorded one - have no
  user-reachable trigger at fixed bits and carry no test. Reaching them needs a
  planted subject rather than a mock. Recorded on cairn-m1-cqt.3, the planted fixture
  corpus bead, which builds exactly that mechanism. §9 states plainly that they are
  untested so a green suite is not mistaken for coverage of them.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED

Written by one subagent, audited by a second, findings applied by a third. I
re-executed both planted negatives directly against the real verifier, ran the rho60
measurement myself as a third data point, recomputed the birthday bound and every
extrapolation, re-ran the two most consequential mutation transitions, and ran the
full suite at HEAD. I read the whole diff a7f5afb..5766d60: zero lines were removed
from any test file, no golden was regenerated in this pass, and neither test file
imports mock or uses monkeypatch. That is a separation of hats within one session,
not independent verification by another party. Run A's and run B's verifier wall
times (0.061 s, 0.057 s) are prior-session observations left as recorded; a fresh run
yields a new value rather than reproducing an old one.

title: M0: conformance harness for the §2 skill contract (MUST clauses, table-driven; toy_curve first conforming skill; planted non-conforming fixture must fail)
description:
WHY (PLAN §2): the §2 skill contract is a specification, and every baseline skill from M1 (`rho_dp`, `bsgs`, the gate-owned instance-maker — cairn-m1-cqt.2) must satisfy its MUST clauses mechanically, not by review. "Specifications aren't suggestions, they're contracts": a clause with no check is an unverified clause. This harness turns "is this a §2 skill" into a table-driven check with a printed compliance matrix, a planted non-conforming fixture that must fail, and `toy_curve` (cairn-m0-e0s.6/.7) as the first conforming subject.

WHAT (`tests/conformance/skill_contract.py`, `tests/conformance/test_skill_contract.py`, `tests/conformance/COVERAGE.md`, `tests/fixtures/skills/nonconforming.py` + `nonconforming_corpus.json`)
- Clause table `CLAUSES: list[Clause(id, level: MUST | SHOULD, text (quoted from PLAN §2), check: Callable[[SkillSubject, Context], Verdict])]`, one row per extracted clause: S2-01 MUST typed interface + fixed version — `interface_version` matches `<name>/<int>`, `run` is typed, `identity_bundle()` returns all five §2 fields with a content-derived `implementation_revision`; S2-02 MUST content-addressed I/O — `python -m <module>` reads canonical JSON on stdin, writes canonical JSON on stdout, and the recomputed output-manifest hash equals the declared one; S2-03 MUST captured seed — `seed` is an input field, two runs under one seed are byte-equal, two seeds differ; S2-04 MUST self-test with a vendored corpus and a per-field `origin ∈ {upstream_vendored, independent_oracle, randomized_postcondition, author_supplied}` on every field; S2-05 MUST per-case ledger `pass | intentional_non_goal | known_gap` and a committed `pass_floor`; S2-06 MUST the committed floor is raised only by an attributed update — checked as `pass_floor ≤ measured pass`, `pass_floor == skill_certificates.selftest_summary.floor`, and `pass_floor ==` the committed golden `tests/goldens/<skill>_floor.golden` (the golden moves only through `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` in an attributed commit, cairn-m0-e0s.7); S2-07 MUST golden certificate — a `skill_certificates` row exists for the identity bundle hash, `certified()` is true, `cert_hash` recomputes from the row's own fields; S2-08 MUST byte-equal double run of the self-test transcript; S2-09 MUST declared cost profile — a `cairn.profile.CostProfile` with `tier`, a `production` component and a `verification` component, `evaluate(inputs)` returning `expected_wall_s`, `expected_core_s`, `expected_verification_core_s`, and `ProfileUndeclared` at an undeclared input; S2-10 MUST DISAGREE semantics — where the skill declares a cross-check it also declares its seam (`SEAM = 'cairn.pari.ellsea'` for toy_curve), and a planted disagreement at that seam yields `status = 'DISAGREE'`, both transcripts present, never `OK`, and `serve()` never returns it (never cached); S2-11 MUST no substrate handle — the child environment holds no `CAIRN_DB*`, argv carries no `.sqlite` path, and an env dump from inside the child (through the real runner, cairn-m0-e0s.9) shows none; S2-12 MUST axis declaration — `cross_check.axis ∈ {implementation, algorithm}`, `independent_range` an axis-aligned interval record over the input fields, `result == 'untested'` outside that range, and a cross-check that has never disagreed reported in the ledger as untested-for-disagreement, never as passing; S2-13 SHOULD numeric profile or tolerance declared when the skill emits floats (toy_curve: `null`, integer-only → `NA`); S2-14 SHOULD Tier-0 arithmetic skills verify their own answer before returning (postcondition arm present).
- Runner `run_conformance(subject, ctx) -> list[Verdict(clause_id, level, status: PASS | FAIL | XFAIL | NA, reason)]`; `test_skill_contract.py` parametrizes `subject × clause` over the registered subjects (`cairn.skills.toy_curve`, `tests.fixtures.skills.nonconforming`; M1 adds `rho_dp`, `bsgs`, the instance-maker) with `ids='<subject>-<clause_id>'`; every MUST FAIL is a test failure for a subject registered as conforming; the fixture subject is registered with its expected FAIL set; a `pytest_terminal_summary` hook prints the compliance matrix (clause × subject × status) and the per-subject MUST score `pass/(MUST total)`; no file is generated (the matrix is the terminal summary).
- Real services: the harness runs each subject's real self-test through the real runner (cairn-m0-e0s.9), the real gp verifier arm (cairn-m0-e0s.8), a real substrate under tmp_path and a bundle built and pinned under tmp_path (cairn-m0-e0s.10); it mocks nothing; the only monkeypatch is S2-10's declared seam, the sanctioned fault injection of the epic's mock policy — applied inside the child: the runner spawns the subject as a subprocess (cairn-m0-e0s.9), which a parent-process `monkeypatch` or `os.environ` read cannot reach, so S2-10 and S2-11's in-child observations launch the subject through the real runner under the harness entry module `tests/fixtures/skills/harness_child.py` (on the child's `PYTHONPATH`, launched under the subject's own `skill_identity`), which patches the subject's declared `SEAM` to return n+2 (S2-10) or writes its own `os.environ` and `sys.argv` to stderr (S2-11) in its own process and then calls the subject's module entry; `json_test_log` records one line per (subject, clause) verdict and `db_snapshot` after each subject's self-test.
- Planted non-conforming fixture `tests/fixtures/skills/nonconforming.py` (+ its corpus): declares `interface_version = 'bad'` (S2-01), omits `origin` on one corpus field (S2-04), returns `{status: 'OK'}` when its declared seam is made to disagree (S2-10) and reads `CAIRN_DB` from its environment (S2-11); it must FAIL exactly those four MUST clauses (asserted by id) and may pass the rest; a harness self-check runs every clause's `check` against this fixture and fails if fewer than two named MUST clauses FAIL — a stubbed check (`lambda *_: PASS`) is caught there.
- `tests/conformance/COVERAGE.md`: the clause table (id, level, PLAN §2 sentence, check function name) committed once; a clause id present in `CLAUSES` but absent from COVERAGE.md, or vice versa, fails `test_coverage_table_matches_clauses`; DISCREPANCIES.md is created only when an XFAIL exists (none at M0).

comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.7 (toy_curve self-test), a property to know before touching the
goldens.

tests/goldens/toy_curve_selftest_transcript.golden and
tests/goldens/toy_curve_certificate.golden are coupled to
toy_curve.IDENTITY_SOURCES, which is src/cairn/pari.py,
src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py and src/cairn/skills/toy_curve_corpus.json.

The self-test's randomized arm seeds from
`first 8 bytes of H(implementation_revision || 'selftest-seed')`, so editing any
of those three files moves the seed, the arm's 30-bit curve, the transcript and
the certificate. Within a fixed revision the transcript is exactly byte-equal
across the double run, which is why the golden compares exactly.

Consequence: an edit to src/cairn/pari.py that has nothing to do with the
self-test still requires
`UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py`
plus an attributed commit. That is the same rule as re-minting the certificate,
so the regeneration and the re-mint belong in one commit. tests/goldens/PROVENANCE.md
grades the transcript golden volatility 3 for this reason, not the 2 the
cairn-m0-e0s.7 spec predicted.

comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.9 (skill runner), a spec attribution to check before conformance
clauses are written against it.

cairn-m0-e0s.9 says the launch contract this runner enforces (canonical JSON on
stdin and stdout, no substrate handle, scrubbed environment, module entry point) is
"checked per skill by the section 2 harness". PLAN section 2 states none of it.
Grepping section 2 for stdin, stdout, "python -m", entry point or canonical JSON
returns nothing; the only stdout clauses in PLAN are section 3's receipt digests and
section 13's Tier-0 verifier acceptance rule.

What section 2 does give: the identity bundle (lines 52-56), pinned nondeterminism
and a byte-equal double run (63-64), the DISAGREE rule (81-84), SKILL_YANKED
(84-86), and launchability only once certified (95-98).

The wire contract is a real design decision made in the beads and in CLAUDE.md, not
a PLAN clause. As implemented by cairn-m0-e0s.9 it is:

  argv     [sys.executable, "-m", "<module>", "<scratch_dir>"]
  stdin    one canonical JSON object, then EOF
  stdout   exactly one JSON object with a status in OK | FAIL | DISAGREE
  stderr   diagnostics only, captured to a file, never a pipe
  env      an allowlist (PATH, HOME, LANG, LC_ALL, LC_CTYPE, TMPDIR, TZ) plus
           whatever the caller names explicitly; no CAIRN_DB* may be named
  scratch  argv[1], the only directory whose byte delta is measured

Conformance clauses should cite that contract as an M0 operator decision rather
than as section 2, so this bead is not testing against an unwritten spec.
