title: M0: CLI agent-ergonomics contract: stdout=data/stderr=diagnostics, exit-code dictionary, --json on every read-side command, capabilities --json, robot-docs, errors that name the exact next command, typo hints, dangerous-op gating, deterministic output, golden-pinned help/capabilities
description:
WHY: the cairn CLI's primary caller is an agent (the orchestrator's workers, the operator's agents, this repo's e2e tests), with no TTY and no human nearby. The first command an agent guesses must work or be redirected with a useful hint (/agent-ergonomics-and-intuitiveness-maximization-for-cli-tools, kernel axioms 0, 4–15, 17). Stdout is data and stderr is diagnostics; exit codes are a documented dictionary, not vibes; every error names the exact command to run instead; the tool describes its own contract in-tool. This bead fixes those conventions once so every later subcommand bead (.6 measure, .7 selftest, .10 bundle/attest, .11 gate selftest, .12 justify, .13 gc, .14 m0-run, .18 doctor) registers through them instead of inventing its own.

WHAT (`src/cairn/cli.py` extended; new `src/cairn/exits.py`, `src/cairn/capabilities.py`, `src/cairn/robot_docs.py`, `src/cairn/errors.py`)
- Exit-code dictionary (`exits.py`, the ONLY place numbers live): 0 OK; 1 USER_INPUT (bad args, malformed file, unknown id — argparse errors are mapped to 1 by overriding `ArgumentParser.error`); 2 GATE_REFUSED (a gate or a safety gate refused, or a self-test failed — fail-closed results: KAT mismatch, bundle≠pin, TierRefused, a verifier FAIL — backend-crash and timeout included — inside a gate run, a self-test arm failure, and a dangerous operation invoked without its `--yes`/`--force`; the state is untouched); 3 ENVIRONMENT (gp missing at GP_BIN, PARI stack unavailable, DB unopenable, bundle/pin/attest file missing or wrong mode, an OS refusal such as EPERM on a flagged file); 4 BACKEND (a subprocess the command itself needed died or returned malformed output outside any gate's classification — an attempt the runner closed FAIL in `m0-run`, `PariError` or `GpTimeout` in `measure` — and the unexpected-exception path of `main`); 5 CONFLICT (a second writer holds `--db`: `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` after the writer's 5 s busy timeout, cairn-m0-e0s.4 — there is no lock file at M0; the doctor's own `.doctor/lock` is cairn-m0-e0s.18's). The doctor subparser maps usage errors to 64 per its own dictionary; every other parser maps them to 1. `cairn doctor` (bead .18) publishes its own dictionary (0 healthy, 1 findings, 2 partial fix, 3 fix failed and rolled back, 4 refused unsafe, 5 concurrency lost, 64 usage) — both dictionaries appear in `capabilities --json`. Never exit 1 for 'ran fine, nothing found' (that is 0 with empty data). `cairn kat canon` moves from exit 1 to 2 (GATE_REFUSED), this bead updating `tests/unit/test_canon.py::test_kat_cli_exit_codes` (cairn-m0-e0s.3 closes asserting 1).
- Errors (`errors.py`): `CliError(code, what, where=None, next_command=None)`; the top-level `main` renders it on stderr as one JSON record through `cairn.log` AND a one-line human form `error: <what> (<where>); run: <next_command>` and exits with `code`; every refusal in the codebase carries a copy-pasteable `next_command` (pin mismatch → the re-pin sequence `chflags nouappnd Y && cairn bundle build --src bundle/ --bundle X --force && cairn bundle pin --bundle X --pin Y --force` — the bare build+pin pair would be refused by this bead's own `--force` gating and by the flag, cairn-m0-e0s.10; uncertified skill → `cairn selftest toy-curve --db D --bundle X --pin Y`; missing gp → the brew install line and `cairn doctor`). No bare 'see --help'. Never silent-fail: every failure has stderr output and a non-zero exit.
- Intent inference: `argparse.ArgumentParser(suggest_on_error=True)` (Python 3.14) covers subcommand names and choices only — probed 2026-08-21 on CPython 3.14.0: `selftst` → "invalid choice: 'selftst', maybe you meant 'selftest'?" while `--jsno` → "unrecognized arguments: --jsno" with no suggestion — so the overridden `ArgumentParser.error` adds the option-flag hint itself (a Levenshtein-≤2 match of each unrecognized token against the parser's option strings, `did you mean --json`), both with exit 1; an alias table for the spellings agents try first (`self-test`→`selftest`, `run`→`m0-run`, `--robot`≡`--json`, `doctor health` kept as-is) implemented as argparse aliases, never silently ignored input.
- `--json` on every read-side command (env, kat, measure, selftest, gate selftest, justify, gc --dry-run, bundle show, doctor, m0-run summary; the write-side `gc --yes` and `startup-scan` emit one document too): stdout holds exactly one JSON document with `schema_version` and sorted keys; nothing else is ever printed to stdout by a `--json` run; all logs stay on stderr. Human output is the default; `--json` is a flag away.
- `cairn capabilities --json`: {tool, version, contract_version, python, commands: [{name, summary, read_only, json, dangerous, gating}], exit_codes: {cli: {...}, doctor: {...}}, env_vars: {CAIRN_LOG, HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE, UPDATE_GOLDENS, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, NO_COLOR}, global_options, default_paths, schema_version} — deterministic (sorted keys, no timestamps); `cairn robot-docs` (alias `--robot-help`) prints the paste-ready agent handbook: the canonical operator sequence (`bundle build` → `bundle pin` → `attest init` → `selftest toy-curve` → `gate selftest` → `m0-run`), one line per command with its read/write nature and exit codes, where artifacts land (deploy/, var/, .doctor/), and the never-do list (never hand-edit deploy/ files, never run gp through a shell, never bypass the pin).
- Dangerous-op gating (axiom 11): `gc` is dry-run by default and deletes only with `--yes`; `bundle pin` refuses to overwrite an existing pin and `bundle build` an existing 0444 bundle without `--force`, and `attest init` refuses when the file exists — each refusal names the safe alternative (`--dry-run`, or the explicit flag) in its `next_command`.
- Determinism and env: stdout JSON byte-identical across re-runs of the same state (two `capabilities --json` runs diff-equal); any emitted time honors `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`; no ANSI escapes are ever emitted (`NO_COLOR`, non-TTY and `CI` need no special casing because there is no styling — a test asserts zero ESC bytes on both streams); no interactive prompt anywhere; bare `cairn` prints usage + the three discovery hints (`--json`, `capabilities`, `robot-docs`) and exits 1 — never a TUI.
- `--help` on the top level and on every registered subcommand exits 0 and mentions `--json`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs`.

TESTS (`tests/unit/test_cli_contract.py`, unit — the CLI is a pure function of argv here; the subprocess-level split test is integration in `tests/integration/test_cli_streams.py`)
- Golden: `tests/goldens/capabilities.golden` (volatility 1 after scrubbing `version`/`python` to `[VERSION]`/`[PYTHON]`); `tests/goldens/help_top.golden` and one `help_<sub>.golden` per registered subcommand — drift fails without `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` (pins the agent-facing contract; /testing-golden-artifacts).
- Parametrized over `cli.registered()`: `--help` exits 0 and names the three discovery surfaces; the command appears in capabilities with the same read_only/json/dangerous flags its registration declares; the one-JSON-document-on-stdout assertion runs here on `env`, `kat`, `capabilities` and the fixture commands (capsys) — a command that needs gp, a bundle or a substrate asserts it in its owning bead's integration test, against its real run.
- Exit dictionary: one parametrized row per code 1–5 through the mapping in `main` — a bad arg → 1; `kat canon --vectors <drifted copy>` → 2; a test-registered fixture command raising `GpMissing` → 3, raising `RuntimeError` (the unexpected-exception path) → 4, raising `sqlite3.OperationalError('database is locked')` → 5 — asserting the exact code and a `next_command` in the stderr record; the real producers are asserted by their owning beads (`gate selftest` with `--bundle` absent → 3, cairn-m0-e0s.11; a second connection holding `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on `--db` while `gc --yes` runs → 5 after the busy timeout, cairn-m0-e0s.13).
- Typo hints: `cairn --jsno capabilities`, `cairn selftst` → exit 1 and stderr naming `--json` / `selftest`.
- Dangerous ops: a test-registered fixture command declared `dangerous=True, gating='--yes'` is refused without `--yes` (exit 2, the safe alternative named in `next_command`, its `run` never called) and runs with it; the concrete gates — `gc` without `--yes` deletes nothing, `bundle pin`/`bundle build` over an existing artifact and `attest init` over an existing file refused — are asserted by cairn-m0-e0s.13 and cairn-m0-e0s.10 through this registry.
- Determinism: `capabilities --json` twice → identical bytes; `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 cairn env --json` carries no wall-clock field.
- Integration (`tests/integration/test_cli_streams.py`): `[sys.executable, '-m', 'cairn.cli', 'env', '--json']` → stdout parses as JSON, stderr holds only JSON log records, rc 0; the same with `--log DEBUG`; `cairn` bare → rc 1, usage on stderr, empty stdout.
- Planted negatives: a registered fixture command that prints a non-JSON line to stdout under `--json` is caught by the contract test (registered only inside the test via `cli.register` and unregistered after); an `ESC[` sequence written to stdout by a fixture command is caught; a subcommand whose `--help` omits `robot-docs` is caught.

DESIGN: `cli.register(name, configure, run, *, summary, read_only, json, dangerous=False, gating=None, aliases=(), dry_run_default=False)` — the registration IS the capabilities row, so capabilities cannot drift from the parser; a `dangerous=True` command must name its `gating` flag, the registry adds that flag to its parser, and `main` refuses with exit 2 before calling `run` when the flag is absent (run never called) unless the command declares `dry_run_default=True` (the gc shape: run performs the dry run and calls `cli.require_yes` before the irreversible step); `main` wraps `run` in the `CliError` handler and maps unexpected exceptions to code 4 with the traceback on stderr at DEBUG and a one-line record at INFO (never silent).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_cli_contract.py tests/integration/test_cli_streams.py -q` green; `uv run cairn capabilities --json | uv run python -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(sorted(d))'` lists commands, exit_codes (cli + doctor), env_vars, default_paths, schema_version; `uv run cairn robot-docs` prints the handbook with the canonical operator sequence; `uv run cairn --jsno capabilities` exits 1 with 'did you mean --json' on stderr.
- Every registered subcommand: `--help` exit 0 naming `--json`, `capabilities`, `robot-docs`; `env`, `kat` and `capabilities` emit exactly one JSON document on stdout under `--json` here and every later read-side command does so in its owning bead (golden-pinned help and capabilities under tests/goldens/ with scrubbed version/python).
- Exit dictionary observed: codes 1–5 each produced through `main`'s mapping by the named rows with a `next_command` in the stderr record; `cairn kat canon` drift → exit 2 and `tests/unit/test_canon.py::test_kat_cli_exit_codes` updated from 1 to 2 in this bead's commit.
- Planted negative: a test-registered fixture command printing a non-JSON stdout line under `--json` is caught; an ESC sequence on stdout is caught; a fixture command registered `dangerous=True` must be refused without its gating flag (exit 2, safe alternative named) with its `run` never called; `kat canon` on a drifted vector copy must exit 2. Any of these passing silently fails the bead (the concrete `gc`/`bundle`/`attest` gates are cairn-m0-e0s.13's and .10's acceptance, inherited through this registry).
- Determinism: two `capabilities --json` runs byte-identical; `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0` leaves no wall-clock field in any `--json` stdout.
- No-Claim: the contract is proven for the subcommands registered at close; later subcommand beads inherit the contract tests by registering (the parametrize is over `cli.registered()`), so a later bead that breaks it fails this bead's tests, not its own.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment, so the compliance audit can re-run it without reading the session.

title: M0: cairn doctor (world-class doctor mode, M0 scope): pure detectors for stack facts, deploy shape, substrate health, KAT and certificate; --fix only through a mutate() chokepoint with verbatim backups and undo <run-id>; doctor exit dictionary; --json/--robot-triage; capabilities; robot-docs; fixture per failure mode; idempotent; offline; no deletes
description:
WHY: a doctor is a contract with a future agent who has no context, no human nearby, and one shot to make the tool work again (/world-class-doctor-mode-for-cli-tools, the One Rule: detect-then-fix, never fix-then-detect). Cairn's deploy shape is unusually easy to break by hand — a pin or attestation file with the wrong mode or a missing uappnd flag, a bundle rebuilt without re-pinning, a substrate left with RUNNING attempts after a crash, a gp binary moved by a brew upgrade — and every one of those is a gate that silently stops working. The stack facts bead .2 grounds are exactly the detectors this doctor ships. Not on the M0 done-when path; it gates nothing in §13 but it is what an agent runs first when any M0 command refuses.

SURFACE (exact spelling, from the skill's CLI-SURFACE): `cairn doctor` (read-only; exit 0 healthy / 1 findings / 4 refused-unsafe); `cairn doctor --fix` (exit 0 / 2 partial / 3 failed-and-rolled-back / 4 refused / 5 concurrency lost); `cairn doctor --dry-run --fix` (prints the plan, writes nothing but the run artifact); `cairn doctor --explain <finding-id>`; `cairn doctor undo <run-id>|latest`; `cairn doctor capabilities --json`; `cairn doctor health` (one line + exit code); `cairn doctor robot-docs`; `cairn doctor ls`; `cairn doctor --robot-triage` ({summary, findings, actions_planned, recommended_command, capabilities_command} — the last is the literal `cairn doctor capabilities --json`, a command and not a URL); `cairn doctor --quick` (cheap detectors only — no gp spawn, no KAT); `cairn doctor --only=<subsystem,...>`; `--json|--robot` with `schema_version`; `--online` exists and is refused at M0 (nothing needs network; exit 6 online-required is never emitted). Global `--db/--bundle/--pin/--attest` select what is examined. Exit dictionary lives in `cairn/exits.py` (bead .17) and in `doctor capabilities --json`. Registration: `cli.register('doctor', …, read_only=False, json=True, dangerous=True, gating='--fix', dry_run_default=True)` — the registry adds `--fix` and reports the doctor as dangerous with that gating flag, `dry_run_default=True` keeps `main`'s pre-run refusal off so the flagless detect pass runs, `configure` adds the `undo|capabilities|health|robot-docs|ls` sub-subparsers and the doctor-only options, the doctor's parser class overrides `error` to raise `CliError(exits.DOCTOR_USAGE, …)` (64) — the one parser whose usage errors are not 1 (cairn-m0-e0s.17) — and `run` returns only `exits.DOCTOR_*` codes.

DETECTORS (pure functions returning findings `{id, subsystem, severity, evidence (file:line / path / mode / hash / row), fixable, recommended_command}`; never call mutate; never spawn anything but gp through `cairn.pari.run_gp`): D-gp-binary (GP_BIN exists; `run_gp(['--version-short'], '')` prints `2.17.4` at rc 0 under the `-q -f -s 64M` prefix — probed 2026-08-21 — and major.minor == 2.17; recommended: the brew line); D-gp-facts (the one stdin line `print("OK")` through `run_gp` with no script file — the doctor reads no test asset — → rc 0, stdout OK, empty stderr; D-pin-mode (0444 + uappnd; fixable); D-attest-mode (0644 + uappnd, every record parses, record 0 is the fixture waiver W; fixable for mode/flag only); D-substrate (opens; `journal_mode=wal`; `PRAGMA integrity_check` ok; append-only triggers present; count of RUNNING attempts with NULL ended_at — recommended `cairn startup-scan --db D` (the subcommand cairn-m0-e0s.9 registers over its `startup_scan()`); a DB file the process user cannot open read-only is a finding of severity `error` naming the path and mode (the doctor exits by its own dictionary only, never the CLI's 3), and an absent DB file is an `info` finding recommending `cairn selftest toy-curve --db D --bundle X --pin Y`, the command that creates it); D-kat (canon KAT passes; skipped under `--quick`); D-certificate (toy_curve identity certified; recommended `cairn selftest toy-curve --db D --bundle X --pin Y`); D-dirs (deploy/, var/ exist and are writable; `.doctor/` and `var/` gitignored; fixable); D-uv-index (pyproject pins the PyPI index; fixable: no — informational with the exact TOML lines).
FIXERS (only two at M0, both byte-for-byte reversible): F-modes (chmod/chflags repair of pin → 0444+uappnd and attestation → 0644+uappnd, sequenced `chflags nouappnd` → `chmod` → `chflags uappnd` because a flagged file refuses `chmod` — cairn-m0-e0s.2 probe 3 — and recorded as one action carrying the prior mode and flags; undo replays the inverse in the same order; refuses with exit 4 if the file is missing — creating a pin is an operator act); F-dirs (create missing deploy/ and var/ — undo is `os.rmdir` of the still-empty directory, the one removal the doctor performs, inside `mutate`, refusing a non-empty one — and append `.doctor/` and `var/` to .gitignore through mutate with a verbatim backup of .gitignore; undo restores the file, or quarantines-by-rename a .gitignore this run created). This bead commits `.doctor/` to the repo's `.gitignore` (the scaffold's list, cairn-m0-e0s.1, already carries `var/` and `deploy/*`); F-dirs is the repair for a missing entry, not its first writer. Everything else is a finding with `recommended_command` — rebuilding a bundle, re-pinning, certifying, scanning RUNNING rows are operator/harness acts the doctor names but never performs.
MUTATE CHOKEPOINT (`src/cairn/doctor/mutate.py`): `mutate(run, path, op)` is the only code allowed to write under `--fix`: takes the lock — `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)` on `.doctor/lock`, released by the kernel when the holder dies so a SIGKILLed fix leaves no stale lock and nothing is ever unlinked; exit 5 if held, naming the holder pid written into the file (never under `var/`, which F-dirs may be about to create) — copies the target verbatim into `.doctor/runs/<run-id>/backups/<relpath>` preserving mode/flags/mtime, computes before/after BLAKE3, applies the op atomically (write-tmp-then-rename for file content; chmod/chflags for modes), appends one line to `actions.jsonl` {path, op, before_hash, after_hash, before_mode, before_flags, ts}; `undo` replays `actions.jsonl` in reverse and verifies the restored hash == before_hash, failing closed if any backup is missing. A code-search test asserts no module under `cairn/doctor/` other than `mutate.py` and `artifacts.py` (the run-artifact writer, whose own test asserts every path it writes lies under `--root/.doctor/`) calls open(...,'w'), os.chmod, os.chflags, os.replace, os.rmdir or shutil. No deletion anywhere (no os.remove/unlink/rmtree; `os.rmdir` only in `mutate`'s undo of its own mkdir; quarantine by rename if ever needed). Atomic writes only.
RUN ARTIFACTS: `<root>/.doctor/runs/<ISO8601Z>__<sha256(git_head + iso_seconds)[:6]>/{report.json, report.md, actions.jsonl, backups/, stderr.log, undo.sh}` — `--root PATH` is the doctor's one extra option (default the checkout root, the `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]` that `cairn.kat.REPO_ROOT` already uses; it locates `.doctor/`, `.gitignore`, `pyproject.toml` and `.git/HEAD`); `git_head` is read textually from `.git/HEAD` and its ref file, never by spawning git (the test guard admits only `sys.executable` and `GP_BIN`), and is `nogit` when absent; the run-id's timestamp is the wall clock even under `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` (it keys a directory that must be unique per run — `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` governs the `ts` fields inside the report); `undo.sh` is the one-line pointer `cairn doctor undo <run-id>`, never raw file operations; `.doctor/latest` symlink updated atomically; `.doctor/scorecard_history.jsonl` is the run index `doctor ls` prints, one line per run `{run_id, mode, exit_code, findings, actions, ts}` — no rubric score is computed or stored; `.doctor/` gitignored (D-dirs/F-dirs). Read-only `cairn doctor` writes nothing but its run directory, `latest` and that index line. Offline by default; no network code exists at M0.

TESTS (`tests/doctor_fixtures/<fm>/` one per detector that is fixable + the unfixable ones for detection only; integration — real files, real SQLite, real gp; every test passes `--root tmp_path` so the run artifacts land under `tmp_path/.doctor/`, and the shared `isolation_guard` (`tests/conftest.py`) gains `.doctor` beside `deploy` and `var` in its guarded repo dirs — it snapshots the checkout only, so no widening exists or is needed, and a doctor test that leaves anything under `<repo>/.doctor/` fails): per fixable FM: corrupt (chmod pin 0644 / clear flags / delete var/) → `doctor` exit 1 with the finding → `doctor --dry-run --fix` lists exactly that action and writes nothing → `doctor --fix` exit 0 → `doctor` exit 0 → `doctor undo latest` → mode/flags/bytes identical to the corrupted state (cmp + stat); idempotence: `--fix` twice → second run actions == 0; crash mid-fix: SIGKILL the child between backup and rename (a `CAIRN_DOCTOR_CRASH_AFTER_BACKUP=1` test hook) → next run completes or aborts cleanly, no `.tmp.*` files, no stale lock; concurrency: two `--fix` processes → one exit 0/2, the other 5; detector purity: `doctor` with no flags leaves every file under `--root` hash-identical except under `.doctor/` (the run directory, `latest` and the index line); `doctor --json | json.loads` works with logs on stderr only; `capabilities --json` round-trips (every declared detector id exists in code); `--robot-triage` carries a `recommended_command` that is the exact next command; planted negatives: a doctor module that writes through `open(...,'w')` outside mutate is caught by the code-search test; a fixture where the backup file is removed before `undo` → undo fails closed (exit 3) and changes nothing; a detector that mutates (fixture) is caught by the purity test.
DEPENDS: .17 (contract + exit dictionary), .10 (bundle/pin/attest shape), .4 (substrate), .7 (certificate), .3 (kat); not required by .14.

comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.7 (toy_curve self-test), a gap this bead owns.

`cairn selftest toy-curve` maps a missing gp binary to exit 3 ENVIRONMENT only by
inheritance: env.gp_binary_sha256() raises pari.GpMissing and cli.main maps that
to exits.ENVIRONMENT (src/cairn/cli.py:322-323). The selftest tests prove the
other half of exit 3, a missing bundle or pin, at
tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py::test_a_missing_bundle_exits_environment.
The gp-absent arm has no test, because faking a gp-less environment in the
selftest tests would be a stand-in for the stack fact rather than a measurement
of it.

Detecting an absent or wrong gp is this bead's territory ("pure detectors for
stack facts"). The selftest command is one of the surfaces whose exit dictionary
that detector should cover.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.14 (commit ef936a4), found while auditing m0-run's error
surface against the agent-ergonomics kernel.

cli.py's generic exception handler emits next_command "cairn doctor" for any
unhandled exception. No command named doctor is registered today: cli.registered()
returns attest, bundle, capabilities, env, gate, kat, m0-run, measure, robot-docs,
selftest and startup-scan.

So the breadcrumb an agent receives on the BACKEND path names a command that does
not exist. An agent that follows it gets "invalid choice: doctor" and learns
nothing, which is worse than no suggestion at all.

Reproduced before m0-run bounded its --bits flag: `cairn m0-run --bits 41 ...`
exited 4 with `run: cairn doctor`. That specific path is now USER_INPUT and no
longer reaches the generic handler, but every other unhandled exception still
does.

This bead is the one that makes `cairn doctor` exist, which closes the gap by
construction. Two things to check when it lands: that the generic handler's
suggestion carries the same --db/--bundle/--pin paths the failing invocation used,
and that a doctor invocation on a healthy tree exits 0 rather than reporting
findings, since the handler will send agents there routinely.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
Addendum to the doctor-breadcrumb note, from cairn-m0-e0s.14 (commit 89b7eb6).

The dangling `cairn doctor` reference is in two places, not one:

  src/cairn/cli.py:334 - the generic exception handler's next_command
  src/cairn/cli.py:221 - the robot-docs agent handbook, which reads
    "When any command refuses: cairn doctor (read-only), then cairn doctor --fix
    for the two repairs it owns."

The second is the worse of the two, because robot-docs is the paste-ready handbook
an agent reads to learn the tool. Every agent that reads it is told to run a
command `cli.registered()` does not list.

Both become correct the moment this bead registers a command named doctor, so no
separate bead owns them. Two checks when it lands: that the handbook's claim about
"the two repairs it owns" matches what --fix actually does, and that the exception
handler's suggestion carries the failing invocation's own --db/--bundle/--pin
paths, since a bare `cairn doctor` inspects the default deploy paths rather than
the ones that failed.

  only some spellings.

  same tuples, so renaming a declared id to a value no code produces was invisible.
  Nothing tied Detector.id to the Finding ids that detector emits. A test now
  asserts the real relation across all 28 fixtures: every emitted Finding.id has a
  declared detector prefix, and every Finding.fixer is a declared fixer id.

Also made load-bearing where it was not: --quick's D-kat skip was double-guarded so
neither guard alone mattered (one guard removed, the skip now asserted from the log
records); the doctor parser's 64 override was untested at the doctor level (three
cases added; the redundant second assignment removed after confirming add_subparsers
inherits parser_class); undo's restored-hash verification had no test (a backup's
content is now tampered and exit 3 asserted); doctor health had no negative case.
Coverage of cairn.doctor moved from 92 percent to 97, with the fixture corpus from
15 to 28.

DISAGREEMENTS WITH THE BEAD TEXT, all adjudicated SOUND by the audit

  --dry-run --fix exits 1, not the skill's 0, when findings remain. Returning 0 over
  a report that lists findings would make the exit code lie. It exits 0 when nothing
  is wrong.

  undo latest resolves to the newest run whose actions.jsonl is non-empty, not to
  the .doctor/latest symlink. The bead's own test sequence puts a detect run between
  --fix and undo latest, so a literal symlink read makes that undo a silent no-op.
  The symlink still moves on every run; the resolution rule is stated in
  capabilities --json and robot-docs.

  Run ids collide within one wall-clock second, since sha256(git_head + iso_seconds)
  is deterministic to the second. _claim_run_dir appends -1, -2 on exclusive-create
  collision so a run directory is one per run.

  SQLite writes -wal and -shm sidecars on a read-only open of a WAL database, so
  "a detect run leaves every file hash-identical" is false for exactly those two
  paths. The exemption is named rather than hidden, and narrowed to the substrate's
  own two names.

  --fix takes the lock before detection, closing the detect-to-fix window. Proven
  real by mutation: LOCK_EX to LOCK_SH is KILLED by 2 tests.

  A bad flag on the top-level parser still exits 1, because argparse's root
  parse_args owns unrecognized arguments and the doctor's override never sees them.
  --only typos and doctor sub-subcommand usage errors are 64.

  The bead cites cli.py:221 and :334 as the dangling doctor references; at 234a825
  they were at :303 and :326. Both are now real commands.

NO-CLAIM

The doctor detects and repairs the M0 deploy shape on this Mac: one OS user, APFS
flags, gp 2.17.4 at /opt/homebrew/bin/gp, libpari 2.17.2 through cypari2 2.2.4. It
proves nothing about any gate's verdict - a detect run checks shape, not
correctness. F-modes and F-dirs are the only automated repairs; every other finding
is a named command for the operator. Not exercised on a second machine, a non-APFS
filesystem, a multi-user checkout, or without cypari2 importable.

Four gaps, each owned by a named open bead:

  Run directories accumulate and nothing collects them, and a backup carries its
  source's uappnd flag so a run directory holding one resists removal until flags
  are cleared. The doctor performs no deletion by design, so collection has to be a
  subcommand explicitly allowed to remove. cairn-c8o owns it, together with the
  doctor diff and --since surfaces the skill names and this bead did not build.
  robot-docs carries the chflags line an agent needs meanwhile.

  Four detector findings are unreachable without a mock: D-pari-inprocess's three,
  which need cypari2 to misreport or a second libpari on the box, and D-kat/mismatch,
  which needs d_kat to take its vectors from the Context rather than a module global.
  cairn-uya owns both, including the decision on whether the cypari2 three are worth
  a fourth declared seam at all.

  The concurrency test can go red on scheduler luck. It asserts one child exits 0 or
  2 while the other exits 5, which holds only if the second reaches the lock while
  the first holds it. It is a flaky RED, never a flaky green - it cannot pass while
  the lock is broken - and closing the window needs an env-gated hold seam inside
  mutate.Lock.acquire. Adding a production sleep hook for a test was declined rather
  than done quietly. Recorded on cairn-ofk, which owns the suite's CI deadline work,
  with the note that a retry would be the wrong answer since it would mask a
  genuinely broken lock. Both new subprocess waits now carry timeout=60, which is the
  shape that bead asks for.

  Twelve lines in artifacts.py and eight in mutate.py are uncovered - git-head
  branches, latest absent, the 1000-run collision, unknown-op refusals. All are
  reachable without mocks; none is a detector finding. Not attempted here.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED

Written by one subagent, audited by a second, findings applied by a third. I
re-executed every acceptance bullet at HEAD, ran the fixable round trip by hand
against the repository's own deploy shape with cmp and stat at each step, re-ran
three planted negatives by mutation, reproduced the OSError defect and its fix, and
ran the full suite. I read the whole diff 8a4b19c..a0b27d8: no assertion was
weakened, no golden was regenerated in the audit pass, and the only test-helper
removals are renames and signature changes that tighten what they check. That is a
separation of hats within one session, not independent verification by another party.

title: M0: execute and record the stack facts M0 stands on (SQLite WAL + busy timeout, macOS append-only flag, pin/attestation write boundary, gp exit/arity facts)
description:
WHY (PLAN §16, §13 M0 first sentence): a stack fact no probe has executed is CONJECTURE until research/grounding/ records the run, and each of these sits under a gate — the single-writer contract relies on WAL + busy timeout (§3); the human path relies on the orchestrator's process user being unable to write the pin or the attestation file (§4); the M2 chain checkpoint relies on the append-only flag binding against truncation (§3). Inherited stack claims are wrong at a meaningful rate when executed.

WHAT: probes as pytest integration tests (they re-run forever) plus the human-readable brief `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` with one row per fact: fact, tag (PROVEN-by-probe / STRONG-EMPIRICAL / CONJECTURE / OPEN), exact command, observed output, date, OS (`sw_vers`, `uname -a`), filesystem (APFS). The same brief later gains the tries table (cairn-m0-e0s.6) and the rho-at-60-bits section (cairn-m0-e0s.15); each bead writes its own section.

PROBES
1. SQLite WAL (`tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py`): file DB under tmp_path; `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` returns `wal`; the writer holds `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` plus one uncommitted INSERT and a second connection's SELECT returns (WAL readers never wait on a writer). Control: the same under `journal_mode=DELETE` → the reader's SELECT raises `OperationalError: database is locked` after its timeout. The writer MUST open with `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` — probed 2026-08-21 under the Homebrew python3 (CPython 3.14.3, SQLite 3.52.0) and re-probed with the same six-cell result under the project's uv-managed interpreter (CPython 3.14.0, SQLite 3.50.4 — the one `uv run pytest` uses; the brief's row names the interpreter and SQLite version the test ran under): under DELETE a plain `BEGIN` or `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` holding an uncommitted INSERT leaves the reader unblocked (the writer holds RESERVED and readers still take SHARED), so the control arm would agree with the treatment and the probe would fail by its own rule; only EXCLUSIVE blocks readers, and under WAL all three BEGIN kinds leave the reader free.
2. Busy timeout: A holds a write txn; B with `PRAGMA busy_timeout=500` attempts a write → waits ≈0.5 s then `OperationalError: database is locked`; with A committing after 0.2 s, B succeeds. Record measured waits.
3. Append-only flag (`tests/integration/test_grounding_fs.py`, macOS `chflags uappnd` on APFS), on a file owned by the current user. Pre-probed 2026-08-21 on macOS 26.6 (the test must reproduce this table): mode 0644 + `uappnd`: `open(path,'a')`+write succeeds, `os.open(O_WRONLY|O_APPEND)` succeeds, `open(path,'w')` → EPERM, `open(path,'r+')` → EPERM, `os.truncate` → EPERM, `os.chmod` by the owner → EPERM while the flag stands; mode 0444 + `uappnd`: append → EACCES (the mode denies write before the flag is consulted), overwrite/truncate/chmod → EPERM; mode 0444 without the flag: every write → EACCES but the owner's `chmod` succeeds; mode 0644 without the flag: everything succeeds (control). Consequence: the attestation file is 0644 + `uappnd` (appendable, not overwritable, not re-modable while flagged), the pin is 0444 + `uappnd` (nothing writes it, nothing re-modes it while flagged). Record honestly: with ONE OS user (operator decision 8) the same user can `chflags nouappnd` and then chmod/truncate, so at M0 the flag refuses truncation and re-moding by the process but does not bind against a process that clears it — that half is OPEN until M3 introduces the second OS user; the Linux equivalent (`chattr +a`) is OPEN until the M1 container exists.
4. Write boundary: pin file 0444 + `uappnd` → `open(pin,'w')`, `open(pin,'a')`, `os.truncate(pin)`, `os.chmod(pin, 0o644)` all raise PermissionError for the (non-root) owner; attestation file 0644 + `uappnd` → `open(...,'w')`/`'r+'`/truncate/chmod raise, `open(...,'a')` by the same user succeeds (record: at M0 "cannot write" = cannot overwrite/truncate/re-mode; an append by the harness process is not refused until the two-user shape — the digest/offset rule in bead m0-justify (cairn-m0-e0s.12) is what makes a harness-appended forgery useless, and bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate (cairn-m0-e0s.10) tests that). Also: `os.unlink(pin)` and `os.rename(pin, …)` → EPERM while `uappnd` stands (probed 2026-08-21 on macOS 26.6 = Darwin 25.6.0, APFS: `rm` and `mv` both refused with `Operation not permitted`), the same for the attestation file, and both succeed after `chflags nouappnd` — so the pin cannot be replaced by rename while flagged, and every test that flags a file under tmp_path clears the flag in teardown or pytest's basetemp cleanup fails. Control: after `chflags nouappnd` the owner's chmod, unlink and rename succeed — the recorded gap.
5. gp facts (`tests/integration/test_grounding_gp.py`, self-contained: it ships its own probe script `tests/integration/gp/probe.gp` defining `f3(a,b,c)=print(a," ",b," ",c)`, `ok()=print("OK");quit(0)` and `fail()=print("FAIL [\"x\"]");quit(1)`, and reads no file another bead owns — `verify.gp` is cairn-m0-e0s.8's, which asserts its own `verify()` rows as noted below): gp exits 0 on `1/0` with the message on stderr; `f3(1,2)` runs with the third argument zero-filled (stdout `1 2 0`); a successful run under `gp -q -f -s 64M tests/integration/gp/probe.gp` fed the one stdin line `ok()` writes `OK` to stdout, rc 0 and 0 bytes to stderr (probed 2026-08-21 — the empty-stderr accept predicate of cairn-m0-e0s.8 is satisfiable); `fail()` yields rc 1 with the `FAIL [...]` line on stdout and empty stderr; a 60-bit `ellcard` on `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` under `-s 8M` yields rc 0, empty stdout and `*** ellcard: the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr; gp's own startup needs more than 2 MB of stack — `gp -q -f -s 2M tests/integration/gp/probe.gp` (and `-s 1M`) exits 1 with `### Errors on startup, exiting...` on stdout and `*** the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr before reading stdin; `print(ellisoncurve(ellinit([0,1],2),[0,1]))` (p = 2) dies with a fatal `ellisoncurve: incorrect type in checkell (t_VEC)` on stderr at rc 0 and empty stdout because `ellinit([0,1],2)` returns `[]` (probed 2026-08-21) — the fact behind the verifier driver's `p > 3` pre-spawn rule (cairn-m0-e0s.8); the `verify()`-OK-at-3M/8M/64M row (the verifier script never calls `ellcard`, so an 8 MB ceiling does NOT crash `verify()` — the forced-crash fixture is its `crash_selftest(p,a,b)` entry, a 60-bit `ellcard`) is asserted by cairn-m0-e0s.8's `tests/integration/test_verifier.py` on the bundle script every run, and that bead adds the row to this brief's gp-facts section at its close; reference grounding brief pari-sage-toy-curve-backend.md §3.
6. PARI PRNG consumption (same test file; the fact cairn-m0-e0s.6 pins its call sequence on): after `setrand(s)` and a fixed prefix of draws, `random(2^64)` is unchanged by an intervening 40-bit `ellcard(E)` but changed by an intervening 40-bit `ellsea(E)`, and changed by an intervening 60-bit `ellcard(E)` or `ellsea(E,1)` (probed 2026-08-21 on gp 2.17.4); the test asserts each of the four comparisons in gp and in cypari2 (libpari 2.17.2).

7. CPython reap order (`tests/integration/test_grounding_subprocess.py`; the fact cairn-m0-e0s.9 stands on): a child that exits 3 is spawned with `Popen`; after `communicate()` returns, `os.wait4(pid, 0)` raises `ChildProcessError` (`communicate()` reaps through `wait()` — subprocess.py 1212/1239/2152, CPython 3.14.0 under uv, read 2026-08-21) and `proc.returncode == 3`; control: the same child with stdout/stderr redirected to files and no `communicate()` — `os.wait4(pid, 0)` returns the status word (`os.waitstatus_to_exitcode` → 3) with rusage, and a `proc.wait()` issued afterwards returns 0 (the `_try_wait` → `ChildProcessError` → 0 path that would record every crash as exit 0).

DESIGN: the tests are the executable record; the brief is written by hand from their output with tags. Probes 3–4 skip with an explicit reason when not on macOS (the M1 Linux container gets its own probe bead). No generator script for the brief. Every probe logs its command and observed output through `cairn.log` at INFO so the brief's rows can be copied from the test log.

TEST PLAN (shapes)
- Failure-path convergence: probe 3/4's mode × flag × operation outcomes are one `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over `(mode, flagged, op, expected_errno)` rows (0644+uappnd append OK / w EPERM / r+ EPERM / truncate EPERM / chmod EPERM / unlink EPERM / rename EPERM; 0444+uappnd append EACCES / overwrite EPERM / ...; 0444 no flag → EACCES with chmod OK; 0644 no flag → all OK) with `pytest.raises(PermissionError, match=...)` per row and the control rows asserting success — one test function, the table is the evidence the brief copies; the same for probe 5's gp facts over `(stack, script_entry, expected_rc, expected_stdout, expected_stderr_fragment)` and probe 6's PRNG-consumption rows over `(bits, call, state_changes)` × `{gp, cypari2}`.
- Every probe logs through `json_test_log` so `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` rows are copied from `test.log.jsonl` (command, observed output, wall_ms), never retyped.
- Layer: all integration (real filesystem flags, real SQLite files, real gp, real CPython subprocess); no unit tests here, nothing to mock.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py tests/integration/test_grounding_fs.py tests/integration/test_grounding_gp.py tests/integration/test_grounding_subprocess.py -q` green on this Mac; `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` exists with one row per fact (fact, tag, command, observed output, date, OS/FS), including the four-row mode×flag table of probe 3, the chmod-refused-while-flagged row, the unlink/rename-refused-while-flagged row, the BEGIN-kind × journal-mode reader table of probe 1, the PRNG-consumption rows of probe 6, the gp-startup-needs->2M row, the p = 2 fatal-at-rc-0 row (raw `ellinit([0,1],2)` → `[]`, then the `ellisoncurve` fatal) and the `communicate()`-reaps row of probe 7 (the `verify()`-OK-at-3M/8M/64M row is cairn-m0-e0s.8's, added to the same gp-facts section at that bead's close).
- Planted negative: each probe has a control arm doing the same operation without the protection (no WAL / no timeout / no flag / mode 0644) asserting the opposite outcome; a probe whose control and treatment agree fails (probe 1's writer therefore holds `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` — under plain `BEGIN` the DELETE-mode reader reads and the probe fails by design); the 0444+uappnd append must FAIL (EACCES) — if it succeeds the attestation-file mode rule in cairn-m0-e0s.10 is wrong and the test fails; unlink and rename of a flagged file must FAIL (EPERM) — if either succeeds the pin is replaceable by rename and the test fails; the 60-bit `ellcard` under `gp -s 8M` must overflow (rc 0, empty stdout, the message on stderr — a success there means the stack facts moved and cairn-m0-e0s.8's crash-fixture premise must be re-grounded); after `communicate()` the `wait4` must raise `ChildProcessError` (if it returns, the runner's reap rule in cairn-m0-e0s.9 is moot and the test fails).
- No-Claim: facts hold for this Mac (arm64 macOS, APFS, one OS user, PARI 2.17.4 / libpari 2.17.2); nothing is claimed for Linux, a second OS user or another filesystem — those rows are OPEN with the milestone that grounds them.
- The mode×flag×op table, the gp-facts table and the PRNG-consumption table are each one parametrized test whose `ids=` name the row; the brief's rows cite those ids; a duplicated single-row test for any row fails the `/optimal-tests --audit` pass pasted at close.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment, so the compliance audit can re-run it without reading the session.

title: M0: canonical typed encoding + BLAKE3 content addressing: recipe key, hypothesis key, identity bundle, environment manifest; known-answer vectors for both keys
description:
WHY (PLAN §3): REFUTED-by-hash and every cache hit are exactly as sound as the canonicalizer — two logically equal recipes that hash differently are a bug that silently under-reports dead ends. The canonicalizer's known-answer vectors are one of the first gate self-tests (§13 M0) and run before any gate.

WHAT (`src/cairn/canon.py`, `src/cairn/keys.py`)
- Canonical encoding: typed, domain-separated; fields in fixed declared order; maps and sets sorted by canonical key bytes; every variable-length field length-prefixed (u64 LE length ‖ bytes); ints as sign byte ‖ big-endian magnitude, length-prefixed (arbitrary precision — curve coordinates are 60–254-bit); strings UTF-8 NFC; blob references as `(hash, size)`; NO unknown fields (a key the schema does not declare raises `CanonError` at write time); no floats in keys (numeric profiles are declared as rationals or strings).
- Hash: BLAKE3-256 over `domain_tag ‖ canonical_bytes`. Fixed domain tags: `cairn/recipe-key/v1`, `cairn/hypothesis-key/v1`, `cairn/node/v1`, `cairn/identity-bundle/v1`, `cairn/env-manifest/v1`, `cairn/selftest-cert/v1`, `cairn/gate-bundle/v1`, `cairn/instance/v1` (the verifier instance `(p,a,b,n,P,Q)` — cairn-m0-e0s.8 and .14 hash it with this tag), `cairn/chain/v1` (reserved for M2).
- Recipe key = H over `(skill_identity_hash, inputs: sorted map name → (hash,size), seed, tool_versions: sorted map, container_digest, salt)`. `skill_identity_hash` = hash of the §2 identity bundle `{interface_version, implementation_revision, tool_digests, container_digest, numeric_profile}` so a changed executable is a different recipe. On the M0 machine (no container) `container_digest` = hash of the environment manifest `{os: sw_vers+uname, python, cypari2, libpari (pari.version()), blake3, gp_binary_sha256}` — never empty (empty raises).
- Hypothesis key = H over the typed hypothesis object `{target_family, claimed_property_or_cost_model (or claim statement hash), method_identity (interface version + canonical params — NEVER implementation revision), declared_parameter_ranges, sampling_distribution?}`; per-run seeds, ladder instances and free-text fields are excluded by schema.
- Schemas: one `Schema` (ordered tuple of (name, type)) per object kind; encode walks the schema, never the dict, so undeclared keys surface as a set difference.
- Known-answer vectors `tests/vectors/canon_kat.json` (≥6): recipe key (two logically-equal spellings with different dict/set order → same expected hash), hypothesis key, identity bundle, env manifest (fixed synthetic values), node hash, and a negative vector (one byte changed in the canonical input → a DIFFERENT expected hash, asserted not-equal). Generated once, committed; origin recorded `author_supplied` (they pin the encoding against drift; they are not an external oracle).

- Golden KATs: `tests/vectors/canon_kat.json` is an exact golden of volatility 1 (pure bytes + BLAKE3; deterministic and platform-independent; the env-manifest vector uses fixed synthetic field values, never the live `pari_versions()`); generated once by `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest tests/unit/test_canon.py -k kat`, reviewed by hand once (a hex dump of each vector's canonical bytes beside its hash in `tests/goldens/PROVENANCE.md` with the generator command and blake3 version), committed; compared exactly through `assert_golden` on every run; a regenerated KAT lands only in an attributed commit whose message names the encoding change (this KAT is the canonicalizer gate self-test of cairn-m0-e0s.11, so a silent change would move every recipe key); guard test `tests/unit/test_canon.py::test_kat_guard_rejects_drift` copies the vector file to tmp_path, flips one hex byte, points the loader at the copy and asserts the KAT comparison fails without `UPDATE_GOLDENS` — the permanent form of the manual flip-one-byte step, which stays in the close comment as well.

- Fuzzing (same file, Hypothesis structure-aware, ≥ 500 examples): `encode(schema, payload)` for `payload` from `st.recursive(st.none() | st.booleans() | st.integers() | st.binary() | st.text(), lambda c: st.lists(c) | st.dictionaries(st.text(), c), max_leaves=50)` — never raises anything but `CanonError`; any payload holding a key outside the schema raises `CanonError` naming that key (`match=`); any float anywhere in a key object raises `CanonError`; every schema-valid payload round-trips through the test-only decoder (`decode(encode(p)) == p`); `st.text()` plus explicit NFC/NFD pairs: `encode('\u00e9') == encode('e\u0301')`. Seed corpus `tests/fuzz_corpus/canon/` holds the planted negatives (undeclared field, empty `container_digest`, float in key, NFD string, 300-bit int, `[]` vs `[b'']`, `['ab','c']` vs `['a','bc']`) replayed as `@example`s before random generation.
- Layer: all unit (pure library, pyramid); `uv run cairn kat canon` is the one integration touch and asserts exit code and one log record per vector only — it never re-asserts vector values.

title: M0: substrate store (SQLite + BLAKE3): nodes/blobs/lineage, recipes, attempts, execution receipts, cache bits, statuses, salt, disowned, replay grade, certificate slot; single writer + WAL; M1 column fixtures
description:
WHY (PLAN §3): a result not in the substrate does not exist to the claims DB. Provenance is a storage property: every launch appends an attempt; nothing is overwritten; a cached value is served only from a verified attempt; a failure is a record, not a memo. This schema is the shape every later milestone plugs into.

WHAT (`src/cairn/substrate.py`, SQL in `src/cairn/schema.sql`; hashes via bead m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3)
Tables
- `blobs(hash PK, size, bytes, created_at)` — the only collectable kind (bead m0-gc-roots = cairn-m0-e0s.13).
- `nodes(hash PK, kind, canonical BLOB, replay_grade CHECK IN ('Replayable','Verifiable','AuditOnly'), producer_identity, created_at)`; `lineage(child_hash, parent_hash, edge_kind)` append-only. Every content-addressed object of any typed table (claims layer included, cairn-m0-e0s.5) also has a `nodes` row with the same hash and kind, so lineage and GC see one graph.
- `roots(root_kind CHECK IN ('recipe','ledger_row','certificate','divergence'), node_hash, PRIMARY KEY(root_kind,node_hash))` — the GC roots table (§3: recipes, ledger rows, certificates and recorded divergences are roots); defined here because `mark_non_reproducible` below roots both attempts; reachability and collection are cairn-m0-e0s.13.
- `recipes(recipe_key PK, skill_identity_hash, inputs_manifest_hash, seed, tool_versions_hash, container_digest, salt, do_not_cache INT)`; inserting a recipe also inserts its `roots('recipe', recipe_key)` row.
- `attempts(attempt_id PK, recipe_key, output_manifest_hash NULL, receipt_hash NULL, status CHECK IN ('RUNNING','OK','FAIL','DISAGREE','BUDGET_EXCEEDED','SKILL_YANKED','INTERRUPTED'), replay_grade, verifier_result_hash NULL, certificate_hash NULL, skip_cache_lookup INT, disowned_at NULL, inadmissible INT DEFAULT 0, started_at, ended_at NULL)`. `RUNNING` is the in-flight status an attempt is inserted with (`ended_at IS NULL`); exactly one UPDATE is permitted per row — `RUNNING` → a terminal status, setting `ended_at`, `output_manifest_hash`, `receipt_hash` together (the runner, cairn-m0-e0s.9, performs it; its `startup_scan()` performs `RUNNING` → `INTERRUPTED` for every row with `ended_at IS NULL` before any new launch, PLAN §4); a second UPDATE raises.
- `receipts(receipt_hash PK, gate_bundle_hash, start_mono, end_mono, cpu_user_s, cpu_sys_s, wall_s, peak_rss_bytes, scratch_bytes_written, exit_status, stdout_digest, stderr_digest, tool_digests_hash)` — written by the harness writer only (bead m0-skill-runner-receipt = cairn-m0-e0s.9).
- `skill_certificates(identity_bundle_hash PK REFERENCES nodes(hash), cert_hash UNIQUE, transcript_hash, env_manifest_hash, selftest_summary, at)` — the §2 certificate slot; `selftest_summary` is canonical JSON `{corpus_origins: [per-case per-field origins], randomized_arm: bool, cross_check: {axis, independent_range (an axis-aligned interval record over the input fields, e.g. {bits:[0,50]})} | null, pass, floor}` that `justify`'s producer-standing ceiling reads (cairn-m0-e0s.12); rows are written by the skill self-test (cairn-m0-e0s.7), which first persists the identity bundle itself as `nodes(hash = identity_bundle_hash, kind = 'identity_bundle', canonical = the §2 bundle bytes)` so every `skill_identity_hash` a recipe, attempt or ticket names resolves to a stored object (a certificate row naming an identity with no `nodes` row is refused); the certificate's own content-addressed object is `nodes(hash = cert_hash, kind = 'skill_certificate')` with a lineage edge `cert_hash → identity_bundle_hash` (`edge_kind = 'certifies'`), and inserting one also inserts `roots('certificate', cert_hash)`. `cert_hash = H('cairn/selftest-cert/v1' ‖ identity_bundle_hash ‖ transcript_hash ‖ env_manifest_hash)`, each field length-prefixed per cairn-m0-e0s.3 — the identity hash is inside the certificate, so a certificate copied from one revision's row onto another's cannot verify. Predicates here: `certified(identity_bundle_hash)` ⇔ a row exists AND `cert_hash` recomputed from the row's own fields equals the stored one (a tampered or transplanted row is uncertified); `yanked(identity_bundle_hash)` ⇔ a `yank_records` row names it. The tier gate (cairn-m0-e0s.10) reads both.
- `yank_records(yank_id, skill_identity_hash, reach_predicate, ruling_ref NULL, record_digest, file_offset, created_at)`, `salts(class_key PK, salt, record_digest, file_offset)` — schema only at M0; both are human-path records (operator decision 5: yanks and salt issuance are human-only, like waivers), hence the attestation digest+offset columns that cairn-m0-e0s.10's `attestation_record_matches` reads at M1.
- `escrow(attempt_id PK, declared_production_cost, declared_verification_cost, reserved, spent_at NULL, released_at NULL, ceiling_multiplier)` — M0 writes and reads every column in a fixture; enforcement is M1 (§13).
Behavior
- Cache serve path `serve(recipe_key)`: the most recent attempt with status OK, not disowned, not inadmissible, recipe not `do_not_cache`, every referenced blob present (else None → recompute). `status ≠ OK ⇒ never cached` is part of the serve query, not a convention (RUNNING, FAIL, DISAGREE, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, SKILL_YANKED, INTERRUPTED are all excluded by that one predicate). `skip_cache_lookup` callers always record a fresh attempt.
- Replayable recipe with two OK, non-disowned attempts whose output manifests differ → `mark_non_reproducible(recipe_key)`: both attempts kept, both rooted (`roots('divergence', attempt output node)`), both `inadmissible=1`.
- Immutability: `BEFORE UPDATE`/`BEFORE DELETE` triggers → `RAISE(ABORT,'append-only')` on nodes, recipes, receipts, lineage, roots, skill_certificates, yank_records, salts; on attempts the only permitted UPDATEs are (i) the single RUNNING→terminal close, (ii) the one-time NULL→value set of `disowned_at`, (iii) the one-time 0→1 set of `inadmissible`; any other UPDATE and every DELETE raises.
- Single writer: `Substrate.open(path, role='writer'|'reader')`; writer sets `journal_mode=WAL`, `busy_timeout=5000`, `synchronous=NORMAL`; reader opens `file:...?mode=ro` URI; one writer object per process (module guard). Workers never receive the writer.
- `weaken_grade(node_hash, to)`: a grade moves only down the order Replayable > Verifiable > AuditOnly and the move is a new append-only `grade_history(seq PK AUTOINCREMENT, node_hash, from_grade, to_grade, reason, at)` row — `nodes.replay_grade` is never updated in place (the append-only trigger forbids it); `effective_grade(node_hash)` = the latest `grade_history` row's `to_grade`, else the node's column, and every grade reader (`justify`'s AuditOnly rule, the tier gate's ticket rule) reads `effective_grade`; a strengthening, or a move to the same grade, raises.
- Every write and every serve decision logs through `cairn.log` (table, hash, status / served-or-why-not).
TESTS (integration, file DB under tmp_path; `PRAGMA journal_mode` asserted `wal`): `weaken_grade` Replayable→Verifiable then →AuditOnly succeeds and `effective_grade` follows while `nodes.replay_grade` is unchanged; AuditOnly→Verifiable raises; Verifiable→Verifiable raises; a certificate row whose `cert_hash`/`transcript_hash`/`env_manifest_hash` are copied from another identity's certified row makes `certified()` false (transplant); a certificate row naming an identity_bundle_hash with no `nodes` row is refused; recipe + OK then FAIL attempts → serve returns the OK manifest; disown the OK attempt → None; `do_not_cache` recipe never serves; `skip_cache_lookup` records a new attempt on a hit; two differing OK manifests → both kept, rooted, inadmissible, serve None; a RUNNING attempt is never served; UPDATE on `attempts.status` of a closed attempt raises; DELETE on a node raises; re-inserting an identical node is a no-op while a same-hash insert with different bytes raises `HashCollision`; `disowned_at` settable once; reader connection write → OperationalError readonly; a missing blob makes serve return None; `certified()` true after a well-formed certificate row, false for an unknown identity and false for a row whose `cert_hash` was written tampered; `yanked()` true after a yank_records row; M1-column fixture (`tests/integration/test_schema_admits_m1.py`): every column of `escrow`, `yank_records`, `salts` written and read back byte-equal; one attempt each at `SKILL_YANKED`, `BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `INTERRUPTED` inserted and never served; a `disowned_at` mark excludes its attempt from serve.
DESIGN: SQL in one file; thin typed Python functions; no ORM; insert recomputes the content hash from the canonical bytes and asserts it equals the caller's hash; an insert whose hash already exists with byte-identical canonical bytes is a no-op (content-addressed idempotence — the e2e re-run of cairn-m0-e0s.14 and the gate plan's fixture rows of cairn-m0-e0s.11 depend on it), and a same-hash insert whose bytes differ raises `HashCollision`.

TEST PLAN (shapes)
- Stateful property test (`tests/integration/test_substrate_stateful.py`, Hypothesis `RuleBasedStateMachine`, real file DB under tmp_path, `max_examples=200`, `stateful_step_count=50`, WAL asserted once in setup): rules `launch(recipe, manifest)` (insert RUNNING then close OK with a manifest drawn from a pool of three), `fail_launch(recipe)`, `disown(attempt)`, `mark_inadmissible(attempt)`, `set_do_not_cache(recipe)`, `drop_blob(hash)` (simulated loss), `serve(recipe)`; shadow model: `dict[recipe -> list[(attempt_id, status, disowned, inadmissible, blobs_present)]]`; invariants checked after every step — `serve(r)` is `None` or the manifest of an OK, non-disowned, non-inadmissible, blob-complete attempt of `r` (a disowned attempt is never served under any interleaving of launches and disowns), and `serve(r) is None` whenever the model has no eligible attempt; planted mutants in `tests/mutants/substrate_mutants.py`: `serve_ignores_disowned` (the serve query without `disowned_at IS NULL`) and `serve_ignores_missing_blob` (no blob-presence join) — the machine must find a counterexample for each within 200 examples (`test_mutant_<name>_is_killed`).
- Failure-path convergence: the append-only trigger table is one `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over `(table, statement)` expecting `sqlite3.IntegrityError` with `match='append-only'`; the status-exclusion table is one parametrize over the six non-OK statuses asserting `serve` is `None`; `weaken_grade`'s refusals (strengthening, same grade) are one parametrize with `match=`.
- Each integration test calls `db_snapshot` after its act phase (row counts per table land in `test.log.jsonl`).
- Layer: integration (real SQLite); the only unit test is the serve-eligibility predicate as a pure function over an attempt row tuple, if one is factored out — otherwise none.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_substrate.py tests/integration/test_schema_admits_m1.py -q` green against a real file DB; test log shows `journal_mode=wal`; `certified()`/`yanked()` predicates exercised as named.
- Planted negative: UPDATE to a closed attempt's status must raise (append-only trigger); a FAIL attempt and a RUNNING attempt must never be served; a recipe with a missing blob must not be served (delete one blob row, assert None); a certificate row with a tampered `cert_hash` must make `certified()` false; a transplanted certificate row (fields copied from another identity's row) must make `certified()` false; a strengthening `weaken_grade` must raise; a same-hash insert with different bytes must raise `HashCollision`. Each asserted as an expected failure.
- No-Claim: M0 proves the schema admits and refuses what §3 names; the budget ceiling's wall-clock form on the direct child is the runner's (cairn-m0-e0s.9), while its process-tree form, escrow spend/release, yank reach and disowned propagation are column fixtures only — their behavior is M1's; `certified()` attests a recorded certificate, not correctness.
- `tests/integration/test_substrate_stateful.py` green at 200 examples × 50 steps with the disowned-never-served and missing-blob invariants; both mutants in `tests/mutants/substrate_mutants.py` (`serve_ignores_disowned`, `serve_ignores_missing_blob`) killed — a surviving mutant fails the bead; the trigger table, the status-exclusion table and the grade-refusal table are each one parametrized test.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.

description:
WHY (PLAN §4, §7): the tag is derived, never set; every tag, verdict and gate record names an exact content-addressed statement hash; a human verdict enters through one route and is absent unless its digest matches the attestation file. WHAT (`src/cairn/claims.py`; additions to `schema.sql`; hashes via bead m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3; every typed row below also inserts a `nodes` row with the same hash and kind, cairn-m0-e0s.4)
- `hypothesis_objects(hash PK, canonical, claim_statement_hash NULL, supersedes NULL, created_at)` immutable.
- `claim_statements(hash PK, claim_id, version, informal, formal_source NULL, scope, quantities, source_claim_hash NULL, supersedes NULL, status CHECK IN ('open','refuted','promoted','withdrawn'), created_at)` — `scope` is the typed record `{target_family (categorical), size_interval, param_ranges (axis-aligned intervals), assumption_set (content-addressed ids)}`; `quantities` is a typed record carrying, among its units, an optional `cost_model {exponent, constant, crossover}` — `cost_model IS NOT NULL` is what "a statement whose typed fields carry a cost model" means to `justify` (cairn-m0-e0s.12); immutable except a single open→terminal status transition (trigger refuses a second).

IDENTITY (the §2 bundle cairn-m0-e0s.3 hashes under `cairn/identity-bundle/v1`; `toy_curve.identity_bundle()` returns it and `skill_identity_hash` is its hash — the value cairn-m0-e0s.7 certifies, cairn-m0-e0s.9 launches under and cairn-m0-e0s.10/.14 test with `certified()`): `interface_version = 'toy_curve/1'` (the method name a hypothesis object's `method_identity` carries); `implementation_revision` = BLAKE3-256 over the length-prefixed `(path ‖ bytes)` pairs, sorted by path, of `src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py`, `src/cairn/skills/toy_curve_corpus.json` and `src/cairn/pari.py` — content-derived, never a declared string, so an edited executable, corpus or arithmetic seam is a new identity, uncertified until its own self-test passes (the property cairn-m0-e0s.7's negative (c) and the tier gate's uncertified-revision refusal rest on); `tool_digests = {gp_binary_sha256, cypari2, libpari}` from `cairn.pari.pari_versions()` and the `GP_BIN` file; `container_digest` = the environment-manifest hash of cairn-m0-e0s.3; `numeric_profile = null` (an integer-only skill). Unit test (`tests/unit/test_toy_curve_io.py`): the identity hash is stable across two computations and changes when one byte of any of the three files changes.

ALGORITHM — CALL SEQUENCE PINNED (matches the grounding brief's bench.gp / bench_cypari2.py, which gave bit-identical p,a,b,n,tries in gp and cypari2; the PARI PRNG state is part of the contract — probed 2026-08-21 on gp 2.17.4: at 40 bits `ellcard(E)` leaves the PRNG state unchanged while `ellsea(E)` advances it, and at 60 bits both `ellcard(E)` and `ellsea(E,1)` advance it, so any call added inside the loop, or reordered after it, changes every later draw): `setrand(seed)`; `p = randomprime([2^(bits-1), 2^bits])`; `tries = 0`; loop: `a = random(p); b = random(p)`; if `4a³+27b² ≡ 0 (mod p)` continue (a singular pair is not counted); `tries += 1`; `E = ellinit([a,b], p)`; bits ≤ 50 → `n = ellcard(E)` (generic path, milliseconds), accept iff `isprime(n)`; bits > 50 → `m = ellsea(E,1)` (early abort: returns 0 on a small factor), accept iff `m ≠ 0 and isprime(m)`, with `n = m`. After the loop, in this order: bits > 50 only — confirm `ellcard(E) == n` once under the 64 MB stack (a mismatch is `status='DISAGREE'` exactly like the cross-check below, though at 60 bits both calls are SEA and no independence is claimed); then `P = random(E)` (non-identity); then the postcondition arm; then, bits ≤ 50 only, the algorithm-axis cross-check — after P is drawn and never inside the loop. Expected tries for seeds 1,2,3 (the bench rows; the integration test asserts them): 30 bits 48/148/20; 40 bits 40/52/57; 50 bits 36/11/220; 60 bits 45/72/140. All order calls go through the `cairn.pari.ellcard` / `cairn.pari.ellsea` wrappers (cairn-m0-e0s.1) — the one seam where a test plants a disagreement.
Algorithm-axis cross-check (bits ≤ 50 only, once, on the accepted curve): `ellsea(E)` (SEA) must equal `ellcard(E)` (generic BSGS-family); on mismatch return `status='DISAGREE'` (never OK, never cached) carrying both transcripts and digests for a substrate node; NO silent retry with a third tool. For bits > 50 `result='untested'` (at 60 bits `ellcard` is itself SEA — agreement by construction, no independence claimed). A cross-check that has never disagreed is reported in the self-test ledger as untested-for-disagreement, never as passing.
Randomized postcondition arm on every output: `isprime(n)`; `ellmul(E,P,n)==[0]`; `n ∈ [p+1-2√p, p+1+2√p]`; `ellisoncurve(E,P)`.
Content-addressed I/O: inputs `{bits, seed}` canonicalized; output manifest = canonical bytes of the output hashed (bead m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3).
Cost-profile constant: `uv run cairn measure toy-curve-tries --sizes 30,40,50,60 --seeds 50 [--json]` (the `measure` subcommand is registered once here, `src/cairn/measure.py`, through `cli.register('measure', ..., read_only=True, json=True)` of cairn-m0-e0s.17 with a `target` positional — `toy-curve-tries` here, `rho60` added by cairn-m0-e0s.15; `--json` emits the per-size table as one document with `schema_version`; exit 0, 4 BACKEND when a launch subprocess dies or cypari2 raises `PariError`, never 1 for an empty table) records, for ≥50 seeds per size, the in-process tries and wall AND the wall of a fresh subprocess launch per seed (the `mean_wall_s` the profile declares) (60 bits included: the skill's declared range reaches the 60-bit rung and its per-try cost there is the `ellsea(E,1)` early-abort path at ≈ 0.3 ms per rejected curve, so the in-process 60-bit loop over 50 seeds finishes in well under a minute, and the per-seed subprocess launches across the four sizes add ≈ 200 × ≈ 0.3 s ≈ one more minute; the constant is declared per size) (mean, sd, min, max, wall) into its own section of `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md`; the declared profile cites that table (STRONG-EMPIRICAL on the sample), never the 3-seed table (20–220 tries; CONJECTURE on means). Expected shape: geometric, sd ≈ mean, expected tries ≈ c·ln p.
Stack: `cairn.pari` applies `allocatemem(64_000_000)` once before any 60-bit work.
Logging: every run logs (bits, seed, tries, n bit-length, cross_check result, status, wall) through `cairn.log`; a DISAGREE logs both transcript digests.
TESTS (integration, real cypari2): seeds 1,2,3 at 30/40/50 bits reproduce the grounding brief's (p,a,b,n,tries) rows bit-for-bit (pins cypari2-vs-gp agreement and the call sequence); 60-bit seeds 1,2,3 complete via ellsea(E,1)+ellcard within a minute each with tries 45/72/140 (the brief's mode-1 rows), and seed 1 equals the committed `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` (cairn-m0-e0s.1) field for field; a call-order guard: a spy on the `cairn.pari.ellsea` wrapper asserts it is invoked exactly once per ≤ 50-bit run and only after the accepted curve's P is drawn (an invocation inside the loop, or a second one, fails the test); postcondition arm asserted on every output; `CostProfile.evaluate(40).expected_wall_s` equals the committed table's `mean_wall_s` at 40 bits and `evaluate(45)` raises `ProfileUndeclared`; double run same seed → byte-identical manifests; different seed → different p; DISAGREE path via the `cairn.pari.ellsea` wrapper monkeypatched to return n+2 at 40 bits → status DISAGREE, both transcripts present, no OK output; singular pair skipped; forced composite n fails the postcondition arm; unit test (`tests/unit/test_toy_curve_io.py`): the stdin/stdout JSON contract round-trips a fixed output and rejects a malformed input with a typed error before any PARI call.

TEST PLAN (shapes)
- Goldens: the seeds-1–3 rows at 30/40/50/60 bits live in `tests/vectors/toy_curve_rows.json` (`(bits, seed) -> p, a, b, n, tries`, decimal strings) as an exact golden of volatility 3 — deterministic under pinned libpari 2.17.2 and the pinned call sequence; a libpari bump or any call-order change legitimately moves them, a cypari2 bump without a libpari change must not; `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` (cairn-m0-e0s.1) is the same class and `toy_curve(60,1)` is compared to it field for field; regeneration is `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest tests/integration/test_toy_curve.py -k rows` followed by an attributed commit that records the libpari version in `tests/goldens/PROVENANCE.md` and says why the rows moved; without the env var a differing row fails, so the call-order spy and the golden together make a silent PRNG-sequence drift unmissable.
- Differential testing, named: the `ellcard` vs `ellsea` cross-check IS a differential test on the algorithm axis, valid for bits ≤ 50 only (PLAN §2 axis rule); `test_cross_check_is_differential_on_algorithm_axis` asserts `cross_check.axis == 'algorithm'`, `independent_range == {bits:[0,50]}` and `result == 'agree'` on every ≤ 50-bit output and `result == 'untested'` at 60 bits; the gp-vs-cypari2 agreement on the rows is labeled in its test id `test_gp_cypari2_rows_agree_plumbing_one_library_twice` — it tests the binding and the call sequence, never the arithmetic (two builds of one library are one implementation).
- Property-based over the postcondition arm (`tests/integration/test_toy_curve_properties.py`, Hypothesis, real cypari2, `bits ∈ {30, 35}`, `seed ∈ st.integers(1, 2**31 - 1)`, `max_examples=30` under a local `settings` override because each example is a real curve search): for every seed, `isprime(n)`, `ellmul(E,P,n) == [0]`, `n` inside the Hasse interval, `ellisoncurve(E,P)`, `status == 'OK'` and the double run is byte-equal; planted mutant `composite_n_skill` in `tests/mutants/toy_curve_mutants.py` (accepts `n` without `isprime`) killed by the `isprime` clause; mutant `unpinned_sequence_skill` (draws `P` before the order confirm at 60 bits) killed by the `curve60_seed1` golden comparison.
- Failure-path convergence: `ProfileUndeclared` at sizes `{0, 29, 45, 61, 10**6}` is one parametrize; the malformed-stdin refusals (empty, non-JSON, missing `seed`, `bits` as string, extra key) one parametrize with `match=` and a spy asserting zero `cairn.pari` calls.
- Conformance subject: toy_curve is the first subject of the §2 skill-contract harness (cairn-m0-e0s.16); its MUST-clause checks (typed interface, content-addressed I/O, captured seed, axis declaration, no substrate handle) run there, not as duplicated assertions here.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_toy_curve.py tests/unit/test_toy_curve_io.py -q` green: 30/40/50-bit outputs for seeds 1–3 equal the grounding-brief rows (p,a,b,n,tries); double run byte-equal; 60-bit seeds 1–3 return prime n with cross_check.result='untested' and tries 45/72/140, seed 1 equal to `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json`; the ≥50-seeds-per-size measurement table (30/40/50/60 bits: tries mean/sd/min/max, per-try ms, mean subprocess wall) is committed in research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md and the declared `CostProfile.per_size` cites it; `evaluate(40)` returns that table's 40-bit `mean_wall_s` in both `expected_wall_s` and `expected_core_s` and the same value in `expected_verification_core_s`; `toy_curve.identity_bundle()` hashes to a stable `skill_identity_hash`.
- Planted negative: monkeypatched `ellsea` wrapper → n+2 must yield status DISAGREE with both transcripts and no OK; a singular pair must be skipped; a forced composite n must fail the postcondition arm; a malformed stdin input must be refused before any PARI call; a cross-check call planted inside the search loop must break tries reproduction and trip the call-order guard; `evaluate()` at an undeclared size must raise before any spawn; a one-byte change in any of the three identity source files must change `skill_identity_hash` (an unchanged hash fails the test). Each asserted.
- No-Claim: gp/cypari2 agreement is one library twice (one implementation) — it proves the binding, not the arithmetic; the algorithm cross-check is independent only for bits ≤ 50; the measured constant is for this machine and these sizes.
- `tests/vectors/toy_curve_rows.json` compares exactly through `assert_golden` for seeds 1–3 at 30/40/50/60 bits and `toy_curve(60,1)` equals `curve60_seed1.json`; a differing row fails without `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1`; its PROVENANCE.md row names libpari 2.17.2 and the volatility-3 note; `test_cross_check_is_differential_on_algorithm_axis` and `test_gp_cypari2_rows_agree_plumbing_one_library_twice` exist under those names.
- `tests/integration/test_toy_curve_properties.py` green at 30 random seeds per size with the postcondition arm; `composite_n_skill` and `unpinned_sequence_skill` in `tests/mutants/toy_curve_mutants.py` are killed (a survivor fails the bead); `ProfileUndeclared` sizes and malformed-stdin refusals are each one parametrized test.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment, so the compliance audit can re-run it without reading the session.

comments.text:
CLOSE EVIDENCE — commits 9c07701 (skill) and 3037ffb (after /optimal-tests --audit), re-executed 2026-08-21.

POSITIVE
- `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_toy_curve.py tests/integration/test_toy_curve_properties.py tests/integration/test_measure.py tests/unit/test_toy_curve_io.py tests/unit/test_toy_curve_profile.py -q` → `132 passed in 14.62s`; `uv run pytest -q` → `681 passed`.
- Files: src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py (run, _search/_settle/_draw_point, SEAM='cairn.pari.ellsea', check_postcondition, COST_PROFILE, identity_bundle/skill_identity_hash, parse_inputs/main, __main__), src/cairn/profile.py (CostProfile/Evaluation/SizeCost/Production/Verification/ProfileUndeclared), src/cairn/measure.py (registered `measure`), src/cairn/env.py, tests/integration/test_toy_curve.py, tests/integration/test_toy_curve_properties.py, tests/integration/test_measure.py, tests/unit/test_toy_curve_io.py, tests/unit/test_toy_curve_profile.py, tests/mutants/toy_curve_mutants.py, tests/_checks.py (shared curve_row/matches_vector/bench_tries), tests/vectors/toy_curve_rows.json, tests/goldens/help_measure.golden, research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md §6a.
- Bit-for-bit reproduction: the 3-seed bench rows of research/grounding/pari-sage-toy-curve-backend.md §2 are now PARSED from the brief (not hardcoded) and matched at 30/40/50/60 bits; `toy_curve(60,1)` equals tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json field for field including P and tries=45 (re-checked at close after the production reorder: True).
- Cost profile bound to evidence: `uv run cairn measure toy-curve-tries --sizes 30,40,50,60 --seeds 50 --json` (122.7 s) produced the §6a table (mean tries 39.48 / 50.60 / 63.82 / 87.90, sd 29.83 / 46.22 / 60.56 / 78.93, subprocess mean wall 0.137 / 0.134 / 0.251 / 0.878 s); tests/unit/test_toy_curve_profile.py parses §6a and asserts COST_PROFILE.per_size cell for cell, so the declared profile cannot drift from the measurement.
- Cross-check declared honestly: axis `algorithm`, independent_range {bits:[0,50]}; at 60 bits `cross_check.result` is `untested` (ellcard IS SEA there, so the two agree by construction and no independence is claimed).

PLANTED NEGATIVES (observed; the two HIGH ones mutation-proved on a scratch copy of src, restored and diff-verified IDENTICAL):
- Dropping the 60-bit confirm-disagreement branch turns `test_disagree_path_at_60_bits_via_the_ellcard_confirm_seam` red (1 failed).
- Dropping the hasse / ellisoncurve / ellmul clauses turns the three `test_each_postcondition_clause_has_a_negative[...]` rows red (3 failed, 1 passed).
- Also: `composite_n_skill` and `unpinned_sequence_skill` and `cross_check_in_loop_skill` are each killed by running their relation under the mutant; a monkeypatched `ellsea` returning n+2 at 40 bits yields status DISAGREE with both transcripts and no OK output; the call-order spy (now covering ellcard) asserts the 60-bit tail is exactly [("ellcard",None),("draw_point",None)].

TWO DECLARED PRODUCTION CHANGES (from the audit, neither silent):
1. `check_postcondition` moved ahead of the disagreement verdict so the arm runs on EVERY output, including the 60-bit confirm mismatch. The pinned call order is unchanged (confirm -> draw P -> arm -> cross-check); no clause consumes PRNG, and the goldens and curve60 vector are unmoved (verified without regeneration).
2. Clause order inside `check_postcondition` is now isprime -> hasse -> ellisoncurve -> ellmul. With `ellmul` second, hasse and ellisoncurve were UNREACHABLE on any real curve (a fake n satisfying [n]P == O is a multiple of the true order and therefore composite; an off-curve P dies inside ellmul first), so three of four clauses could not have a negative. This is a logic finding, not only a test gap.

AUDIT: /optimal-tests --audit → NOT CLEAN (4 HIGH, 6 MED, nits). All applied except `_draw_point`'s identity-retry branch (toy_curve.py:211→209), which needs `pari.pari.random` — not a declared wrapper seam; covered instead by an invariant over 50 draws (`test_drawn_point_is_always_affine`). The audit also confirmed the COST_PROFILE↔§6a binding is genuine and non-vacuous.

NO-CLAIM: green proves the skill reproduces its pinned call sequence and known answers on this machine with libpari 2.17.2; the algorithm cross-check is independent only for bits ≤ 50 (gp-vs-cypari2 is one library twice and tests plumbing, never arithmetic); the measured constants are for this machine and these sizes (STRONG-EMPIRICAL on the sample, CONJECTURE for means elsewhere); "DISAGREE is never cached" is asserted at bead .9 where a cache exists, not here.
