title: M0: toy_curve self-test: vendored known-answer corpus (4 cases, origin per field) + ledger + pass floor, randomized_postcondition arm, golden certificate, byte-equal double run, certificate recorded → revision certified
description:
WHY (PLAN §2): a skill's self-test is (i) a vendored known-answer corpus with a per-case ledger `pass | intentional_non_goal | known_gap` and a committed pass floor only an attributed update may raise; (ii) a golden certificate = hash over the canonical transcript of the corpus and the exact outputs — a changed implementation behind the same interface needs a fresh certificate and a mismatch fails closed; (iii) every nondeterminism source pinned and a byte-equal double run asserted. A corpus supplied only by the author is not a self-test (`author_supplied` alone caps results at CONJECTURE, enforced by `justify`'s producer-standing rule). A revision is launchable only once its self-test passed and its certificate is recorded; the tier gate refuses an uncertified revision exactly as a yanked one.

CORPUS (`src/cairn/skills/toy_curve_corpus.json`, origin per field; sources pinned in research/grounding/pari-sage-toy-curve-backend.md §4). Origin rule: a field copied from an upstream document is `upstream_vendored`; a field completed locally (a point chosen here, a scalar or Q computed here) is `author_supplied` and is re-checked by a postcondition at every self-test run — it is never trusted; the `randomized_postcondition` origin names only the seeded arm below (inputs drawn from a seed committed after the implementation revision is content-addressed). Field forms: the corpus file stores each field as the upstream document writes it (case 1 `a = -3`, case 4 `Px = -33`); cypari2 accepts those in-process, and whenever a corpus case is handed to the Tier-0 verifier driver (the gate plan's `corpus-1` steps, cairn-m0-e0s.11) it travels as an `Instance`, which reduces `a, b` and every coordinate into `[0, p)` (case 1 reaches gp as `a = 2`; cairn-m0-e0s.8).
1. F_5: `y² = x³ − 3x + 1`, `n = 7` — `upstream_vendored` (PARI 2.17.4 usersch3.tex:29031-29032). `P=(0,1)`, `Q=3P=(3,3)`, `x=3` derived locally — origin `author_supplied`; every self-test run asserts `ellorder(E,P)=7` and `ellmul(E,P,3)=Q`; never trusted as vendored (PLAN §13: a locally completed triple is author_supplied).
2. GF(101): `y² = x³ + 90x + 44`, `n = 89` (prime), `x = 2`, `Q = 2P` — `upstream_vendored` (Sage 10.6 ell_point.py:4529-4537 + constructor.py:790-791). `P` is not explicit upstream (`E.gens()[0]`) → chosen locally as the least-x non-identity point; origin `author_supplied` for P with the per-run postcondition `ellorder(E,P)=89`, `2P=Q`.
3. 150-bit: `p = 1427247692705959881058285969449495136382746771`, `E=[1,1]`, `P=(831623307675610677632782670796608848711856078, 42295786042873366706573292533588638217232964)`, `n = 1427247692705959881058262545272474300628281448` (composite, even) — `upstream_vendored` (Sage 10.6 ell_point.py:4680-4686); membership/cardinality/big-int path; no x.
4. Negative control: `E=[1,0]/GF(419)`, `P=(-33,8)`, order 21, card 420 — `upstream_vendored` (Sage 10.6 ell_point.py:822-827); asserts `n·Q ≠ O` for a point outside the order-21 subgroup — the must-FAIL fixture of the postcondition.
RANDOMIZED_POSTCONDITION ARM per run: generate a 30-bit curve from a seed committed AFTER the implementation revision is content-addressed (seed = first 8 bytes of H(implementation_revision ‖ 'selftest-seed')), assert the postcondition arm (`isprime(n)`, `n·P = O`, Hasse interval, on-curve). Verifier-shaped arm on the same curve, run through the real Tier-0 verifier driver (bead m0-tier0-verifier = cairn-m0-e0s.8, real gp subprocess) under the verifier config of the gate bundle — backend path, stack ceiling, timeout, accept predicate and the `verifier_script` bytes all read from `GateBundle.open(--bundle, --pin)` (bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate = cairn-m0-e0s.10; the self-test spells no verifier invocation of its own, since that invocation is a gate-bundle field, PLAN §4), so a `BundlePinMismatch` aborts the self-test before any case runs (exit 2, no certificate row); the `--json` output and the log records name the bundle hash the arm ran under (the transcript stays the §2 corpus-and-outputs record), which is why the operator sequence builds and pins the bundle before `cairn selftest` (cairn-m0-e0s.14): 20 draws `x`, `Q = xP` → driver returns OK; 20 draws `x' ≠ x` → FAIL `xP-ne-Q`; both counts are fields of the transcript. This bead owns wiring that arm (dependencies on cairn-m0-e0s.8 and cairn-m0-e0s.10); the verifier's own planted self-test belongs to the gate plan (cairn-m0-e0s.11).
LEDGER + FLOOR: each case → `pass | intentional_non_goal | known_gap`; `pass_floor` (M0: 4/4 + both arms) lives in the corpus file; only an attributed change (commit with reason) may raise it.
CERTIFICATE: `transcript` = canonical bytes of (corpus, exact outputs, ledger, arm outcomes); `cert = H('cairn/selftest-cert/v1' ‖ identity_bundle_hash ‖ transcript_hash ‖ env_manifest_hash)` (each field length-prefixed; the identity hash is inside the certificate, so it cannot be transplanted onto another revision's row); the self-test first persists the identity bundle as `nodes(hash = identity_bundle_hash, kind = 'identity_bundle')`, then writes the `skill_certificates` row `(identity_bundle_hash, cert_hash, transcript_hash, env_manifest_hash, selftest_summary, at)` together with its `nodes(hash = cert_hash, kind = 'skill_certificate')` row, the lineage edge certificate → identity bundle and `roots('certificate', cert_hash)` (table, rows and the `certified()` predicate are bead m0-substrate-core = cairn-m0-e0s.4); `selftest_summary` = `{corpus_origins (per case, per field), randomized_arm: true, cross_check: {axis:'algorithm', independent_range:{bits:[0,50]}}, pass: 4, floor: 4}` — what `justify`'s producer-standing ceiling reads (cairn-m0-e0s.12). DOUBLE RUN: the whole self-test runs twice; canonical transcripts byte-equal (no timestamps inside the transcript; seed, hashers, clock pinned). Runtime target < 5 s, Tier-0.
CLI: `uv run cairn selftest toy-curve [--json]` (the global `--db`, default `var/substrate.sqlite`, names the substrate the certificate row is written to, and the global `--bundle`/`--pin`, defaults `deploy/gate-bundle.sqlite`/`deploy/gate-bundle.pin`, name the bundle whose verifier config the verifier arm runs under — cairn-m0-e0s.1) exits 0 and prints the certificate hash; registered through cairn-m0-e0s.17 (`read_only=False, json=True, aliases=('self-test',)` — the alias spelling .17's table names, so `cairn self-test toy-curve` resolves): exit 2 GATE_REFUSED on `BundlePinMismatch` (`next_command` = the re-pin sequence of cairn-m0-e0s.10) and on any self-test failure — a floor miss, a certificate mismatch, a double-run divergence, a failed arm or ledger case (`next_command` = the same command with `--log DEBUG`, which prints the per-case transcript digests) — with no `skill_certificates` row written, 1 USER_INPUT on `CorpusSchemaError`, 3 ENVIRONMENT when gp or a bundle/pin file is missing; the `--json` document carries `schema_version`; the integration test (`tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py`) builds and pins its own bundle under tmp_path through the build/pin functions of cairn-m0-e0s.10 and clears `uappnd` in teardown; a corpus schema check requires `origin` on every field; every case and arm logs (case id, ledger entry, observed vs expected) through `cairn.log`.
UNIT (`tests/unit/test_selftest_cert.py`, no PARI): the corpus schema check refuses a case missing an `origin` on any field and a ledger value outside `pass | intentional_non_goal | known_gap`; the certificate composition over fixed synthetic identity/transcript/env hashes equals a committed vector in `tests/vectors/canon_kat.json` and changes when the identity hash is swapped (the transplant property) — `cairn.kat.compute` dispatches on `keys.SCHEMAS/HASHERS/TAGS_BY_KIND[kind]` and raises on an unknown kind, so that vector's kind `selftest_cert` needs the three entries: `keys.SELFTEST_CERT = Struct('selftest_cert', [identity_bundle_hash, transcript_hash, env_manifest_hash] as STR)` hashed by `keys.selftest_cert_hash` under `keys.TAG_SELFTEST_CERT` (`'cairn/selftest-cert/v1'`, already defined); that one function IS `cert_hash` (the Struct encoding is the length-prefixed composition cairn-m0-e0s.4 and this bead describe) — this bead mints through it and cairn-m0-e0s.4's `certified()` recomputes through it, whichever of the two lands first adding the entries and the other importing them; the seeded-arm seed (`first 8 bytes of H(implementation_revision ‖ 'selftest-seed')`) is stable for a fixed revision and differs for a bumped one.

TEST PLAN (shapes)
- Goldens: `tests/goldens/toy_curve_selftest_transcript.golden` = the canonical transcript bytes (hex, one line per corpus case and arm) and `tests/goldens/toy_curve_floor.golden` = `{pass: 4, floor: 4, arms: {postcondition: 'pass', verifier: {ok: 20, fail: 20}}}` are exact goldens of volatility 2 — deterministic because seed, hashers and clock are pinned and no timestamp enters the transcript; `tests/goldens/toy_curve_certificate.golden` holds the certificate hash with the env-manifest hash it was minted under and is volatility 4 (it folds in `env_manifest_hash`, which depends on libpari, the gp binary digest and the OS), so the test compares the transcript exactly and recomputes `cert` from (golden transcript hash, live identity hash, live env hash), asserting the live certificate equals that recomputation and equals the golden value only when the live env manifest hash equals the recorded one (otherwise it logs `env-manifest-differs` and the golden is valid for the recorded platform only); every regeneration goes through `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 uv run pytest tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py` and an attributed commit naming the reason — this IS PLAN §2's rule that only an attributed update may raise the floor or re-mint the certificate; `tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py::test_transcript_golden_guard` fails when the live transcript differs from the golden without the env var; PROVENANCE.md rows for all three.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATIONS FROM THE SPEC, EACH DELIBERATE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. The transcript golden is graded volatility 3, not the 2 the spec predicts. The
   seeded arm draws from H(implementation_revision || 'selftest-seed') and
   IDENTITY_SOURCES includes src/cairn/pari.py, so the transcript moves with any
   edit to those three files. It is exactly byte-equal within a revision, which
   is what 2 would claim. Recorded on cairn-m0-e0s.16 and cairn-m0-e0s.14.

2. The certificate golden gates its equality assertion on the identity hash as
   well as the env manifest hash. The spec gates on env alone, but the
   certificate folds in both, so an env-only gate would assert equality across a
   revision bump and fail with a message that explains nothing.

3. The certificate golden takes the .golden suffix. conftest's _golden_path
   routes any name ending in .json to tests/vectors/, the canonicalizer vector
   directory.

4. Re-certification is idempotent, which the spec does not cover. An equal
   certificate reports recorded=present and inserts nothing; a differing one
   refuses with exit 2. skill_certificates keys on identity_bundle_hash under
   append-only triggers (src/cairn/schema.sql:73,132-133), so an unconditional
   second insert raises IntegrityError and surfaces as exit 4 BACKEND.

5. The Hasse re-check named in the spec's arm description is not implemented
   separately: toy_curve.check_postcondition already raises
   PostconditionFailed("hasse") (src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py:235), so a second
   check is unreachable. Dead code reads as coverage.

6. selftest_cert_transplanted was added to VECTOR_SPECS, putting the transplant
   property behind `cairn kat canon` rather than only a unit assertion. The
   vector count literal in test_kat_runner_passes_on_committed_vectors moved
   9 -> 10.

7. Postcondition names are validated at schema time rather than run time, and
   cross-validated against the fields each needs, so an unknown name is refused
   before ellinit. p and n gained a range check; a corpus with p = 0 previously
   reached cypari2 and escaped as an unhandled error.

tests/integration/test_toy_curve.py::test_identity_hash_moves_with_the_implementation_revision
was green for an accidental reason. It copied each IDENTITY_SOURCES file into a
tmp tree with a stub fallback for any absent source, then asserted the tmp tree's
identity hash differs from the repo's. With toy_curve_corpus.json absent the copy
was unfaithful and the difference came from the stub. Creating the real corpus
made it fail. It now asserts identical bytes give an identical hash anywhere and
one flipped byte moves it, and it kills a mutant that makes
implementation_revision ignore file bytes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE TEST AUDIT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A fresh subagent ran /optimal-tests --audit and claimed eight guards had no test.
Each claim was proved rather than believed: the guard was deleted in a scratch
copy and the suite re-run. All eight stayed green, so all eight were real. Twelve
guards now have a killing test, each verified by re-running the same deletion and
watching a test go red. The repo was restored from backup and checked
byte-identical with `shasum -a 256 -c` after every mutation.

Two audit findings were declined. Deleting the unit origin and ledger tests as
subsumed by the fuzz mutations: the fuzz asserts only that the error path matches
a regex, while those tests assert the exact path per case, so they are not a
subset. Dropping the PARI spy from the unit fuzz file because check_corpus
reaches no PARI call on any input, making it unfailable today: the spec asks for
it by name and it guards against validation later growing a PARI call. The
integration ordering proof was the weak one and now asserts run_case is never
reached rather than that three helpers went uncalled.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NO-CLAIM
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Certified is not correct beyond the corpus. Four known-answer cases, one 30-bit
seeded curve and 40 verifier draws per run do not establish that toy_curve is
correct at any other size or seed.

Cases carrying author_supplied fields are capped at CONJECTURE by justify wherever
no covering arm or cross-check exists. Case 1's P, Q and x and case 2's P and Q
are author_supplied; the seeded arm and the <=50-bit algorithm-axis cross-check
are what cover them here.

The 150-bit case has no discrete-log component: it exercises membership,
cardinality and the big-integer path only.

Case 2's Q is tagged author_supplied although the relation Q = 2P is upstream,
because the coordinates derive from a locally chosen P.

The negative control uses Q = (10,163), a generator of order 420, not the least
point outside the order-21 subgroup. That least point is (0,0), where 21*Q = Q
for a parity reason unrelated to subgroup membership.

The whole integration file skips off macOS: pinned_bundle pins through the uappnd
chflags bit. On Linux the self-test has unit coverage only. Recorded on cairn-hcl.

The gp-absent arm of exit 3 ENVIRONMENT is untested; only the missing-bundle half
is proven. Recorded on cairn-m0-e0s.18.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
No independent verifier ran. The test audit was a fresh subagent with no stake in
the code, which is better than self-review but is not independent verification;
every claim it made was re-executed here before being acted on, and its report
was treated as a claim throughout.

The four corpus cases were probed against live PARI in this session and matched
the values pinned in research/grounding/pari-sage-toy-curve-backend.md section 4.
Those upstream line references were not re-fetched from PARI or Sage; they are
taken from the grounding document as written.

The certificate hash, transcript hash and bundle hash in this comment come from
this machine: macOS, the gp binary at /opt/homebrew/bin/gp, and the libpari and
cypari2 versions recorded in the env manifest. The certificate golden is valid
for that platform only.

title: M0: Tier-0 verifier subprocess (gp): membership n·Q=O then xP==Q; affirmative acceptance (rc==0 AND stdout==OK AND stderr empty); arity/field validation before spawn; explicit stack ceiling; forced crash → FAIL; gate-read instance, submitter supplies x only
description:
WHY: "No submission without a passing verifier (xP == Q) subprocess" is an invariant (CLAUDE.md). Acceptance is affirmative, never residual: gp exits 0 on fatal errors (1/0, stack overflow — PROVEN by probe) and zero-fills missing arguments, so rc==0 is not evidence of anything. The instance is gate-read: the curve, n, P, Q come from the claim statement node or dispatch record, never from the submitter, who supplies x alone — `xP == Q` on an instance the worker chose is a true statement about the wrong problem (PLAN §4).

WHAT (`src/cairn/verifier.py`, `src/cairn/gp/verify.gp`)
- `verify.gp` (shape from grounding brief §3) ships two entry points. `verify(p,a,b,n,Px,Py,Qx,Qy,x)`: `ispseudoprime(p)` → nonsingular → `ellisoncurve(E,P)` and `(E,Q)` → `ellmul(E,Q,n)==[0]` (membership FIRST — PARI's generic `elllog` can loop when no solution exists; the verifier never calls a log) → `ellmul(E,P,x)==Q`; prints exactly one line `OK` or `FAIL <reason-codes>`; `quit(0|1)`. `crash_selftest(p,a,b)`: `ellcard(ellinit([a,b],p)); print("OK"); quit(0)` — the gate's forced-backend-crash fixture, reachable only from the gate plan's crash steps (cairn-m0-e0s.11) and this bead's tests, never from `run`: on the committed 60-bit curve at the planted ceiling `8M` the real backend overflows (rc 0, EMPTY stdout, `*** ellcard: the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr — PROVEN by probe 2026-08-21), and at the bundle's `64M` it prints OK (the must-PASS control proving the entry is a live computation). `verify()` itself is NOT a crash fixture at any ceiling that starts gp: it never calls `ellcard` and prints OK on the 60-bit instance under `-s 3M`, `-s 8M` and `-s 64M` (probed 2026-08-21); below ≈ 3 MB (`-s 2M`, `-s 1M`) gp dies at startup with rc 1, stdout `### Errors on startup, exiting...` and the overflow message on stderr. The script is a gate-bundle object (kind `verifier_script`, cairn-m0-e0s.10): the driver materializes the bundle's bytes once per process to a 0444 file `verify.gp` under a per-process `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='cairn-bundle-<bundle-hash>-')` directory removed at interpreter exit — never under the repo's `var/`, which `isolation_guard` (`tests/conftest.py`, cairn-m0-e0s.1) snapshots around every test — and passes that path to gp; `src/cairn/gp/verify.gp` is the bundle source and is never read at gate time.
- Driver `Verifier.run(instance: Instance, x: int) -> VerifierResult`: validates arity (exactly 9 fields), every field a non-negative int, `p > 3` (PARI's `ellinit([a,b],2)` returns `[]` and the next call dies with a fatal error at rc 0 — probed 2026-08-21; short Weierstrass is singular in characteristic 2, and the validator never lets the backend see it), `0 ≤ a, b < p`, `Px,Py,Qx,Qy < p`, `x < n`, `n` inside the Hasse interval of p (`|n − (p+1)| ≤ 2√p`) — BEFORE spawning; `Instance` reduces `a, b, Px, Py, Qx, Qy` into `[0, p)` at construction (corpus case 1's upstream `a = -3` becomes 2; cairn-m0-e0s.7) and `instance_hash` is over the reduced values; renders the nine values as decimal integer strings on ONE stdin line `verify(p,a,b,n,Px,Py,Qx,Qy,x)` (never hex, never floats); spawns `[GP_BIN,"-q","-f","-s",stack_ceiling]` loading `verify.gp` through `cairn.pari.run_gp`; backend path, stack ceiling, timeout and accept predicate come from the gate bundle (bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate = cairn-m0-e0s.10; injected as a config object at unit level) — the accept predicate is the structured object `{rc: 0, stdout: "OK", stderr_empty: true}` evaluated field by field (no string evaluation; the shipped bundle pins exactly that triple and cairn-m0-e0s.10 asserts it; `stdout: null` or `stderr_empty: false` is a legal, weaker predicate that leaves that field unchecked — the form cairn-m0-e0s.11's re-pinned bundle copy uses to prove the crash self-test is load-bearing — and only a missing key or a non-int `rc` is refused at construction); accepts iff `rc==0 AND stdout.strip()=="OK" AND stderr==""` (satisfiable — probed 2026-08-21: `gp -q -f -s 64M verify.gp` fed one stdin line writes 0 bytes to stderr on a good instance; `quit(1)` gives rc 1 with the FAIL line on stdout and empty stderr; the 8 MB stack overflow gives rc 0, empty stdout and `*** ellcard: the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr); everything else → FAIL with `reason ∈ {p-not-prime, singular, P-off-curve, Q-off-curve, nQ-not-O, xP-ne-Q, backend-crash, timeout, bad-arity, bad-field, submitter-named-instance}`: a stdout line starting with `FAIL ` yields its reason codes; every other non-accepting outcome is `backend-crash` (a fatal message on stderr with rc 0, the `-s 2M` startup overflow with rc 1 and `### Errors on startup, exiting...` on stdout, a killed child with rc < 0, and `OK` accompanied by any stderr bytes); a `GpTimeout` raised by `cairn.pari.run_gp` (cairn-m0-e0s.1) is `timeout`; the pre-spawn refusals `bad-arity`, `bad-field` and `submitter-named-instance` return `accepted=False` and their `gate_runs` row carries `result='refused'`; default timeout 30 s.
- Instance binding: `Instance{p,a,b,n,P,Q}` has `instance_hash = H('cairn/instance/v1' ‖ canonical instance)` (domain tag from cairn-m0-e0s.3); `run` takes an `Instance` produced by the gate run (from the claim statement node / dispatch record) and a bare `x`; a `Submission` carrying its own `(P,Q)` is refused with `reason='submitter-named-instance'` before any subprocess is spawned (a spy asserts zero spawns). The result records `instance_hash`.
- Result node: a `nodes` row of kind `verifier_result` `{instance_hash, x, accepted, reason, stdout_digest, stderr_digest, rc, wall_s}` plus a `gate_runs` row (gate='verifier', result pass|fail, instance_hash, bundle + pin hash), both written by the caller's writer (bead m0-claims-schema = cairn-m0-e0s.5); a verifier run is a gate run, not a skill attempt — it writes no `attempts` row and is never served from any cache (every submission re-runs the subprocess). Every verdict logs (instance_hash, accepted, reason, rc, wall_ms) at INFO and the gp argv + stdin/stdout/stderr digests at DEBUG through `cairn.log`.
TESTS (integration, real /opt/homebrew/bin/gp; `tests/integration/test_verifier.py`): corpus case 1 (p=5,n=7,P=(0,1),Q=(3,3),x=3) → OK; the committed 60-bit instance `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` (cairn-m0-e0s.1) with a fixed x and Q=xP computed in-test via cypari2 → OK (≈17 ms); one-coordinate negative (Qy+1 → off-curve; and a different on-curve point → xP-ne-Q); one-scalar negative (x+1) → FAIL xP-ne-Q; wrong n → FAIL nQ-not-O; forced backend crash: `crash_selftest(p,a,b)` on the committed 60-bit curve at stack ceiling `8M` → rc 0, empty stdout, `*** ellcard: the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr → classified FAIL backend-crash, and its control at `64M` → OK; `verify(...)` on the same 60-bit instance at `3M`, `8M` and `64M` → OK (asserted every run, so the fixture's premise — only `ellcard` overflows 8 MB — is re-checked; this bead adds the `verify()`-OK-at-3M/8M/64M row to the gp-facts section of `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` from that test's log — the one probe-5 row cairn-m0-e0s.2 leaves to the owner of `verify.gp`); startup overflow: `verify(...)` at `2M` → rc 1, stdout `### Errors on startup, exiting...`, overflow on stderr → FAIL backend-crash; a killed child (SIGKILL mid-run, rc −9) → FAIL backend-crash; a child exceeding the timeout (config `timeout_s = 0.001` on a good instance — gp cannot start in 1 ms) → FAIL timeout; p = 2 → refused pre-spawn (bad-field, zero spawns); wrong n (n + 2, still inside the Hasse interval) → FAIL nQ-not-O; missing field / extra field / negative int / x ≥ n / n outside Hasse → refused pre-spawn (spy: no spawn); `Submission(P,Q,x)` → refused pre-spawn; randomized arm: 20 draws (x, Q=xP) → OK and 20 draws x'≠x → FAIL; caplog holds one verdict record per run.
UNIT (`tests/unit/test_verifier_validation.py`, no gp): the pre-spawn validator's table (arity, type, range, Hasse, submitter-named instance → typed refusal); the accept predicate's truth table over rc ∈ {0, 1, −9} × stdout ∈ {"OK", "OK\n", "FAIL [\"xP-ne-Q\"]", "", "### Errors on startup, exiting..."} × stderr ∈ {"", "***   stack overflow"} — exactly the (0, "OK"/"OK\n", "") cells accept; every `FAIL`-line cell maps to `xP-ne-Q`, every other non-accepting cell to `backend-crash`; the structured accept object with a missing key is refused at construction (fail closed).

title: M0: skill runner: subprocess launch with content-addressed inputs, harness-written execution receipt (CPU/wall/RSS/scratch bytes/exit/digests/bundle hash), attempt row + statuses, cache bits, 4× wall ceiling on the trivial fixture
description:
WHY (PLAN §3, §5): the execution receipt is the harness's own record of the run, written by the writer and never by the skill; its readers are the budget ceiling, the ladder's clock and memory measurements and the provenance check. A receipt the skill writes about itself is a number from the gated party. Workers are subprocesses that return artifacts to the single writer and hold no write capability.

WHAT (`src/cairn/runner.py`)
- `launch(skill_module, skill_identity, inputs, seed, *, bundle_hash, scratch_dir, declared_expectation_s, declared_verification_s, budget_remaining, ceiling_multiplier) -> Attempt` (`skill_module` is the dotted module launched with `-m`, e.g. `cairn.skills.toy_curve`; `declared_expectation_s` for the toy-curve launch is `CostProfile.evaluate(bits).expected_wall_s` — the mean subprocess wall with interpreter start included, cairn-m0-e0s.6 — so the 4× ceiling is not tripped by process start): computes the recipe key (bead m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3); honors cache bits (`skip_cache_lookup`, `do_not_cache`, serve path of bead m0-substrate-core = cairn-m0-e0s.4); inserts the attempt row with status `RUNNING` (cairn-m0-e0s.4); spawns the skill as a subprocess (`[sys.executable, "-m", "cairn.skills.<name>"]`, canonical JSON in on stdin, canonical JSON out on stdout, scratch path passed as an argument; the child receives NO substrate path or handle and an environment scrubbed of `CAIRN_DB*`; the child's stdout and stderr go to files `<attempt dir>/stdout` and `<attempt dir>/stderr` outside the scratch path whose byte delta is measured — never pipes, and `communicate()` is never called, because it reaps the child through `wait()` (subprocess.py 1212/1239/2152, CPython 3.14.0 under uv; probed by cairn-m0-e0s.2 probe 7) — so `os.wait4` is the first and only reap and the stdout/stderr digests are BLAKE3 over those two files); waits with `os.wait4(proc.pid, 0)` for rusage (ru_utime, ru_stime, ru_maxrss) and takes the exit status from the status word it returns (`os.waitstatus_to_exitcode`), setting `proc.returncode` itself and never calling `proc.wait()`/`proc.poll()` afterwards — CPython's `Popen._try_wait` turns the `ChildProcessError` of an already-reaped child into status 0 (subprocess.py `_try_wait` 2019–2029, read 2026-08-21 on CPython 3.14.0 under uv — the interpreter `uv run pytest` uses; m0-stack-facts §7), which would record every crash as exit 0; `time.monotonic()` start/end; wall; bytes written under scratch (directory-size delta); exit status; stdout/stderr BLAKE3 digests; tool digests (gp sha256, cypari2/libpari versions); bundle hash. DEVIATIONS AND DECISIONS, EACH DELIBERATE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Escrow is a separate table, not columns on attempts as the bead's text assumes.
   An UPDATE attempts SET reserved would hit the append-only trigger. The row goes
   in through add_escrow with spent_at and released_at NULL.

2. The ceiling and the escrow read one Evaluation object rather than three fields
   of it. All three fields are the same number today, so they agree by accident;
   PLAN section 5 line 599 requires the same declared profile, and one object makes
   that structural.

3. The divergence path is built, which the bead omits. PLAN section 3 lines 124-125
   name it the reason the receipt exists, and section 3 line 200 makes recorded
   divergences GC roots, so leaving it out would have let cairn-m0-e0s.13 collect
   the evidence.

4. replay is a parameter. The bead's signature had no way to supply the grade that
   section 3 line 116 puts in the attempt tuple.

5. budget_remaining implements the section 5 line 573 meet rule rather than sitting
   unused.

6. Re-certification aside, the runner never emits SKILL_YANKED. The status is in
   the schema and in PLAN sections 2 and 4; pre-launch refusal belongs to the tier
   gate and the in-flight case has no owner. Recorded on cairn-m1-cqt.4.

7. Ceiling enforcement is built at M0 though PLAN section 13 lines 1391-1394
   exercise it first at M1. This is a strengthening, and section 13's own closing
   rule is that a behavior no M0 test exercises is architecture rather than a slice.

8. The bead asks that the output manifest hash equal the skill's own manifest. It
   cannot: ToyCurveOutput.manifest_hash hashes that skill's OUTPUT schema, while the
   runner's manifest hashes a name-to-blob map and is generic across skills whose
   schemas it cannot decode. The checkable relation is asserted instead.

9. The wire contract (argv, stdin, stdout, env allowlist, scratch as argv[1]) is an
   M0 operator decision, not a PLAN section 2 clause; section 2 states none of it.
   Recorded on cairn-m0-e0s.16 so conformance does not cite an unwritten spec.

10. measure.launch is left alone rather than sharing a launch primitive. Its
    reaping contract is incompatible (subprocess.run then proc.returncode, which
    this runner must never do) and tests/integration/test_measure.py monkeypatches
    measure.LAUNCH_ARGV.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEFECTS FOUND IN MY OWN WORK DURING THIS BEAD
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A containment hole. _artifacts walked scratch with followlinks=False but read with
read_bytes(), which follows, so a symlink in scratch blobbed an outside file's bytes
into the substrate as the skill's artifact. A dangling symlink raised
FileNotFoundError after start_attempt and stranded the attempt at RUNNING. Only
regular files become artifacts now, and any exception after start_attempt closes the
attempt FAIL.

A grade mismatch. launch passed replay to start_attempt but not to
put_output_manifest, so an attempt launched Verifiable produced a node claiming
Replayable.

A dangling next_command. startup-scan's missing-substrate error named cairn m0-run,
which is cairn-m0-e0s.14 and unbuilt. The test now asserts the named command is in
the live registry rather than pinning a string.

Two of my own tests passed for the wrong reason. The grandchild sweep test used a
fixture that timed out, so the ceiling's kill did the work and the post-reap sweep
was never exercised. The grace test passed grace= explicitly, so mutating the
constant to zero changed nothing.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE TEST AUDIT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A fresh subagent ran /optimal-tests --audit with a 27-mutation battery whose two
controls were killed, and reported 17 survivors. Each was re-run here. Sixteen now
fail a test, verified by re-applying the same mutation and watching it go red; the
source was restored from backup and checked byte-identical with shasum -a 256 -c
after every run.

One survivor is left, honestly. Replacing the scratch delta with an absolute
measurement changes nothing, because launch creates a fresh empty scratch directory
per attempt so the baseline is zero by construction. The delta is kept because a
filesystem giving a new directory nonzero blocks would make the absolute wrong, and
allocated_bytes is tested directly against a pre-seeded directory.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NO-CLAIM
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
rusage covers the direct child plus whatever that child reaped, not the process
tree. Measured: a grandchild burning CPU appears only when the child waits for it
(0.320 s against 0.041 s). PLAN section 3 lines 120-122 specify "over the process
tree" and section 6 reads those fields for the ladder; the receipts table has no
field distinguishing the two, so an M0 row must not be read as a tree figure.
Recorded on cairn-m1-cqt.1.

peak_rss_bytes is normalized from the platform's unit (bytes on macOS, kilobytes on
Linux). The macOS unit is empirical, from a 300 MiB allocation moving the counter by
313720832; the macOS man page states no unit. The Linux branch is documented but not
executed here.

No sandbox. The environment is an allowlist and the child holds no substrate handle,
but nothing confines its filesystem or network. PLAN section 16 decision 6 puts a
container at M1.

Bytes written is a scratch-directory allocation delta, not I/O accounting. Hardlinks
double-count, APFS clones and compression misreport, a file rewritten in place a
thousand times counts once, and writes outside scratch are invisible.

Escrow behavior is M1. The reservation row is written; spend and release have no
substrate method.

Concurrent launches are untested. A second in-process writer is refused with
CONFLICT, and cross-process contention relies on SQLite's busy timeout.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
No independent verifier ran. Three fresh subagents contributed: a CPython reap
research pass, a PLAN reading, and a house-style review, plus the test audit. Each
report was treated as a claim and re-executed here before being acted on; the reap
facts were additionally already grounded by cairn-m0-e0s.2 in
tests/integration/test_grounding_subprocess.py.

uv, gp at /opt/homebrew/bin/gp, APFS.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.9 (skill runner), a measurement scope this bead must not misread.

PLAN section 3 lines 120-122 specifies the receipt's CPU seconds and peak RSS as
measurements "over the process tree", and section 6 lines 768-773 and 846-853 read
exactly those fields for the ladder's memory model and clock check.

The M0 runner measures with os.wait4, which reports the direct child plus whatever
descendants that child itself reaped. Probed on this machine: a grandchild burning
1.0 s of CPU appears in the parent's wait4 result only when the direct child waits
for it (ru_utime 1.212 with the reap, 0.216 without), and ru_maxrss likewise jumps
16 MB to 51 MB. start_new_session has no effect on this either way.

So for a skill that forks and reaps its own children the two quantities coincide,
and for one that leaves orphans, or that is killed at the ceiling before it can
reap, the receipt undercounts. toy_curve is single-process, so M0 has no case where
they differ.

The receipts table carries no field distinguishing the two, so nothing in the
schema tells a reader which quantity a given row holds. Before the ladder reads
peak_rss_bytes or cpu_user_s as a process-tree figure, either the measurement has
to become a real subtree measurement (cgroups on Linux; no clean macOS equivalent)
or the receipt needs a measurement_scope field. Reading an M0 row as a tree figure
is silently wrong, not loudly wrong.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.12 (justify), which ships src/cairn/justify.py at commit 8836bb1.
Three properties of justify the ladder has to know, because the ladder is its first
real producer of ladder_table evidence.

1. The producer-standing ceiling reads the attempt's inputs from the evidence node's
   own population.param_ranges (src/cairn/justify.py, context_for), not from the
   attempt's recipe. At M0 every evidence node is synthetic and the two agree by
   construction. A real ladder_table names an attempt_id whose recipe carries the
   inputs that were actually run, and those are the inputs the rule means: a node
   declaring a wide population over a narrow run would read as covered when it is
   not. When the ladder writes real ladder_table nodes, feed context_for the recipe
   inputs reached through attempt_id and drop the population fallback.

2. justify returns a sixth typed result the bead's declared signature does not name.
   The union in the bead is Justification | CoverageViolation | LatticeViolation |
   Absent | Pending; a counterexample_hunt_record with verdict KILLED returns
   Refutation(evidence_hash), because none of the five can express "this moves the
   statement to terminal refuted with this evidence pointer" without keying the
   refutation path on a string comparison. derive_tag consumes it: it lowers the tag
   to SPECULATION, writes the downgrade row with the hunt's hash as evidence_hash,
   and calls claims.transition_status(..., "refuted"). Any new caller of justify
   must handle Refutation.

3. KEEP_IN_SAMPLE and counterexample_hunt_record are exercised by construction only
   at M0 — no ladder and no hunt exist. The KEEP_IN_SAMPLE rule is: the verdict
   justifies STRONG-EMPIRICAL only when the statement's scope.size_interval is
   contained in the node's in_sample_sizes, and justifies nothing otherwise
   (tests/integration/test_justify.py, cases keep_in_sample_covering and
   keep_in_sample_not_covering). The first real ladder run is where that rule meets
   data it did not author.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.16 (the section 2 conformance harness), the registration
interface the three M1 subjects need.

tests/conformance/skill_contract.py holds SUBJECTS, a tuple of SkillSubject.
Adding rho_dp, bsgs and the gate-owned instance-maker means appending three
rows and one EXPECTED_SHOULD entry each. The fields:

  name                   the matrix column label
  module                 an importable module path, launched as python -m <module>
  corpus_path            the vendored known-answer corpus, read directly by S2-04
                         and S2-05
  floor_golden           a name under tests/goldens, read as <name>.golden by S2-06
  inputs                 the stdin document; must carry bits and seed, and bits
                         must be a size the subject's COST_PROFILE declares
  out_of_range_inputs    a stdin document whose bits lie outside INDEPENDENT_RANGE
  conforming             True means every MUST FAIL is a suite failure
  certify                module_certify, which calls module.certify(sub)
  transcript             module_transcript, which calls module.transcript()
  postcondition          a callable returning (held, refused_a_planted_answer),
                         or None; S2-14 is SHOULD and does not gate
  expected_must_failures frozenset(), for a conforming subject

So a conforming M1 skill module must expose, beyond its own entry point:
INTERFACE_VERSION matching <name>/<int>, SEAM, CROSS_CHECK_AXIS in
{implementation, algorithm}, INDEPENDENT_RANGE, COST_PROFILE, IDENTITY_SOURCES,
implementation_revision(root), identity_bundle(root), run(), main(),
certify(sub) and transcript(). toy_curve is the exception that proves the rule:
its certify and transcript live in cairn.selftest, so its registry row names
toy_curve_certify and toy_curve_transcript instead.

Two clauses need care from an M1 subject:

S2-10 launches the subject through tests/fixtures/skills/harness_child.py, which
patches the module named by the subject's SEAM to return its real answer plus 2
and then calls the subject's entry. A subject whose cross-check does not route
through a single patchable module attribute cannot be checked this way, and the
seam it declares has to be the one it actually calls.

S2-11 has a source arm that greps the subject module for the token CAIRN_DB. A
skill that legitimately needs a substrate path takes it on stdin, never from the
environment.

The harness's own checks are claim-agnostic: nothing in skill_contract.py names
toy_curve, and registering a subject is the whole of the work.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
FROM cairn-m0-e0s.15: the number operator decision 2 was waiting on.

Three invocations of `uv run cairn measure rho60 --cap-ops 100000000 --cap-minutes 30`
on one machine (Apple M4, arm64 macOS 26.6, one core; cypari2 2.2.4 / libpari 2.17.2,
CPython 3.14.0), one seed, single-threaded cypari2 `elladd`:

  ops/s          extrapolated 60-bit wall
  688598.1       1693.8 s   28.2 min     (machine shared with a pytest session)
  1171037.6       996.0 s   16.6 min     (idle)
  1294801.6       900.8 s   15.0 min     (idle)

All three stopped on the 10^8 op cap, never the 30-minute cap. Expected work is the
birthday bound sqrt(pi*n/2) = 1166326476 for the vector's order
n = 866004985024698433, so each wall is 1166326476 divided by the measured rate.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. The rates are STRONG-EMPIRICAL. The walls are CONJECTURE:
each assumes a rate measured over the first 10^8 ops of one walk holds for the
remaining ~1.07x10^9, and that the walk's expected length equals its birthday bound.
The 1.88x spread is attributed to machine load, which is an inference from the
declared conditions rather than an isolated measurement; an unloaded core sits at the
15 to 17 minute end.

WHAT IT MEANS FOR THIS BEAD. PLAN §5 tiers the 60-bit rung by its declared cost
profile, and the Tier-1 budget is one core, minutes. Fifteen to twenty-eight minutes
is not that, on any of the three runs. The interpreted rung does not finish inside a
Tier-1 budget, which is the condition operator decision 2 named for funding a
compiled rho/BSGS baseline at M1.

That is an input, not the decision. Two things it does not settle: the gmpy2
comparison is decision 1 and remains unmeasured, so how much of the gap is
interpreter overhead rather than algorithm is unknown; and nothing here says what a
compiled implementation's rate would be, only what this one's is.

A completed 40-bit rho is available as the reference point: 474179 ops, reproducible
across all three runs, its x accepted by the real Tier-0 verifier, the planted
off-by-one refused with reason `xP-ne-Q`. Detail and commands in
`research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` §9.

comments.text:
Carried forward from cairn-m0-e0s.11 (commit 4a4bb69), re-homed here because it
was first written into cairn-m0-e0s.14's comments and that bead has since closed.
This bead builds the planted fixture corpus and exercises the tier gate, so it is
the one that will make the branch below reachable.

The gate plan's two tier-gate steps use a fixture skill_identity_hash that no
substrate certifies. tiergate.predicate_reasons adds UNCERTIFIED whenever
sub.certified(identity) is false, so both fixture launches always collect at least
one reason and the gate never admits them.

Two consequences.

The tier gate collects every applicable reason rather than short-circuiting, so a
planted reason arrives alongside UNCERTIFIED. The gate plan's steps check
membership (tier-two-above in reasons, ticket-absent in reasons), never equality.
A step or fixture written against the whole reason tuple breaks the first time an
unrelated predicate fires.

gateplan._run_waiver's ticket-present branch is defensive and unreachable today: it
fires only if the gate mints a ticket for the waiver hypothesis, which requires an
admission, which UNCERTIFIED prevents. It is asserted by no test, and that is
stated rather than papered over. A planted corpus that certifies a fixture identity
makes that branch live, and it needs a test before it is trusted.

Pinned by tests/integration/test_gateplan.py::test_a_recorded_waiver_hypothesis_removes_ticket_absent_and_fails_the_waiver_step,
which reaches the neighboring branch by pre-recording the hypothesis object.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
FROM cairn-m0-e0s.15: two refusal branches this bead's fixture corpus can reach.

`rho60_report` in `src/cairn/measure.py` raises BACKEND on three conditions. One is
covered by a real test: a 40-bit walk stopped by `--cap-minutes` before it solves,
reachable with no fault injection at all (`cairn measure rho60 --cap-minutes 0.0001`
exits 4 naming the op count).

The other two have no user-reachable trigger at fixed bits and no test:

  - the Tier-0 verifier refuses the 40-bit x that the walk recovered
  - the 60-bit instance's order differs from the recorded RHO60_ORDER

Reaching either needs a planted subject rather than a mock, which is what this bead
builds. A planted instance whose recorded order disagrees with its curve, and a
planted verifier subject that refuses a correct x, would each land on one of them.

Recorded rather than left silent: the M0 close states plainly that these two carry no
test, so a later reader does not mistake the green suite for coverage of them.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
MOVED HERE FROM cairn-fur, which does not own it: a planted subject the skill-contract
harness has no fixture for.

cairn-oij (commit 58a1438) gave S2-12 an in-range arm that plants the declared seam and
requires the reported cross-check result to move. Three subject shapes now have a real
fixture: one that cross-checks (toy_curve, PASS), one that hardcodes its in-range result
(nonconforming, FAIL), and one whose axis is not in the allowed set (witness, FAIL at the
first arm).

A fourth shape has none: a subject that DECLARES a seam and never calls it on the
in-range path. The arm would report the constant-result FAIL for it, because a result
that does not move is a result that does not move regardless of why. That is the
intended verdict, but it is inference from reading the code rather than a measurement,
and it is the shape closest to a real mistake -- a skill whose cross-check is wired to
the wrong call site looks conforming everywhere else.

It belongs on this bead because this bead builds the planted fixture corpus, and that is
exactly what settling it needs: take the nonconforming fixture, give it a real comparison
against a seam it declares but does not use on the in-range path, and assert S2-12 FAILs
with the constant-result reason rather than the no-seam one. The distinction between
those two reasons is what a reader of the matrix would act on.

Recorded on cairn-fur first, under a framing of that bead as owning "the harness's
pattern surface" that was too wide. It would have been lost when cairn-fur closed.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.9 (skill runner), two behaviors this bead owns that M0 leaves as
schema only.

Escrow has no settlement path. substrate.add_escrow inserts a row and nothing sets
spent_at or released_at; the escrow table carries no append-only trigger, unlike
almost every other table, so a raw UPDATE is legal but there is no API for it. The
M0 runner writes the reservation at launch with both columns NULL, which matches
PLAN section 13 lines 1391-1396 (M0 asserts only that the schema admits these).
PLAN section 5 lines 551-570 defines the behavior: reserve the verification
component at launch, refuse a launch the remaining budget cannot cover, spend where
section 3's first check runs, release unspent only where the attempt ended with
status other than OK or the node was disowned.

The pre-launch half of that is already built: runner.launch raises BudgetRefused
when budget_remaining cannot cover the ceiling (PLAN section 5 line 573, the meet
rule). Spend and release are not.

SKILL_YANKED has no producer. The status is in substrate.STATUSES and in the
attempts CHECK constraint, and PLAN section 2 lines 84-86 say an in-flight attempt
completes with it, but nothing sets it. The M0 runner does not consult
substrate.yanked() before launching, on the grounds that the tier gate
(cairn-m0-e0s.10) owns pre-launch refusal; the in-flight case, where a yank lands
while a child is running, has no owner at all.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.14's flywheel pass (commit 044a5d9). Recorded here because this
bead enforces the budget ceiling over the process tree, so it is the bead that will
work on runner.py's signalling.

runner._signal_group (src/cairn/runner.py:149) falls back to signalling the pid
directly when signalling the process group raises. That fallback is not covered:
replacing its whole body with `pass` leaves all 72 tests in
tests/integration/test_runner.py and tests/unit/test_runner_fuzz.py green.

  scripts/mutation-check.sh src/cairn/runner.py '<fallback body>' 'pass' \
    tests/integration/test_runner.py tests/unit/test_runner_fuzz.py
  -> SURVIVED  72 passed

The ceiling path depends on it: spawn_and_wait signals the group at SIGTERM on
timeout, again at SIGKILL after the grace window, once more in the `finally` when
the child was never reaped, and a final group sweep after reaping to collect
grandchildren the skill forked. Every one of those calls goes through the
unexercised fallback if killpg raises.

Two notes for whoever writes that test. The construct on line 152 is
`except ProcessLookupError, PermissionError:`, which is a valid unparenthesized
except group under PEP 758 and catches both on Python 3.14 — verified on this
interpreter, and two separate survey agents have now misread it as a Python 2
syntax error, one calling it fatal. Do not "fix" it.

The final group sweep at src/cairn/runner.py:230 runs after the child is reaped, so
it targets a pgid whose leader has exited. That is deliberate for orphaned
grandchildren, but a test should pin the intent, since a reused pgid would be
signalled by it.

comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.12 (justify), commit 8836bb1. PROVEN is derived in exactly one
place: src/cairn/justify.py kind_class, where a lean_artifact node reaches PROVEN
only when an approve review_verdict on the same statement hash is visible through
claims.visible_review_verdicts, which matches the row's record_digest against the
record at its file_offset in the attestation file. Absent or unmatched, the node
returns Pending("human_review") and the claim keeps its pre-review tag.

At M0 both halves are synthetic: the verdict is written by a test factory and the
Lean artifact is an evidence node with no artifact behind it. The formalization gate
supplies the real half. Two things it must not break:

- A verdict whose digest does not match its record is invisible, not merely weaker.

  real row at a real offset whose digest genuinely mismatches, and the result is
  Pending, not PROVEN.
- A reject or needs_revision verdict is not an approval. case_lean_artifact_with_a_
  reject_verdict pins that; without it a mutation widening the check to any verdict
  in claims.REVIEW_VERDICTS survived the suite.

justify reads the attestation file for review_verdict records and nothing else. A
waiver record naming the statement hash moves no tag and adds no tag_history row
(test_a_waiver_naming_the_statement_moves_no_tag) — the claim half of the §4
waiver-cannot-advance fixture. The tier half belongs to cairn-m0-e0s.10.

SCOPE (PLAN §13 M2): Dead-end ledger (refuted-by-hypothesis-key vs parked) + the Formalizer worker + the statement-review workflow (the formalization gate and the pre-filters it submits to are M1's). Decompose into child beads when M1 closes; nothing here is pre-decomposed. Operator decision 7: §15 P5 (conformal surprise per claim class as an extra scrutiny trigger — a claimed effect in the top-α of its class's historical claims raises scrutiny and can never lower it, never promotes a tag and never enters the orchestrator's reward) is decided here, at its decide-by milestone: whether it adds anything beyond "bigger claim ⇒ more scrutiny". §15 P4 (operational alarms: the split-conformal anomaly flag on ladder and self-test measurements, the bounded-mean e-process on `log(measured/declared cost)`, repeated `TierRefused` records as a third input — strategy-layer drift monitors that move no tag, ticket or scrutiny class; described in the M1 epic cairn-m1-cqt) has decide-by M1–M2 and its keep-or-drop decision is recorded here by M2 close: an alarm that never fires on anything the ladder or the ceiling misses is dropped.

DONE WHEN: a parked branch auto-revives on blocker-clear; a refuted hypothesis key is `Blocked` unaided; a proposal whose declared region contains a measured REFUTED point for the same method and cost model is `Blocked` though its key is fresh; a `supersedes` edge into a REFUTED version with an unmet retry predicate parks with `supersedes_refuted_review` until the attributed difference statement is recorded; a refutation without a null arm parks the proposal with `null_control_pending`, the blocker clears when the re-measurement lands, and the preflight then answers `Allowed` — with the table as the evidence that met the retry predicate — when the re-measurement did not REJECT and `Blocked` when it did; a proposal differing from a `measured` REFUTED entry only in implementation revision is `Blocked`, while one differing from an `implementation` entry by a certified new revision is `Allowed`; a new branch opened on a key a promoted branch holds — or whose claim statement stands at STRONG-EMPIRICAL after the branch that earned it withdrew — or on a sub-region of such a holder's region with the same method identity and cost model, parks with `already_settled` until a superseding object with its difference statement is recorded; a log truncated to an earlier valid prefix fails startup verification against the checkpoint — also when the truncated log has been re-extended and its forked head appended to the checkpoint, since every older checkpointed head must remain a prefix head (§3) — and an unreachable checkpoint blocks promotion; a worker that returns with a claim it opened still open yields a `Leaked` record while a harness-terminated attempt yields none; and a green Lean artifact with no `review_verdict` stays below PROVEN while the statement-review workflow routes it to the human queue.

ADDS: the ledger preflight (`Allowed | Blocked | RequiresNullControl | AlreadySettled`) with its measured-point reach, `supersedes_refuted_review`, `null_control_pending` and `already_settled` parks with the null-control resolution rule, the hash-chained log (`chain = H(domain ‖ prior_chain ‖ canonical_record)`) and its head checkpoint (a file beside the gate-bundle pin carrying the append-only flag — M0 grounded what that flag refuses; the second OS user arrives at M3 per decision 8), the terminal-status invariant, the statement-review workflow routing green artifacts to the human queue and recording `review_verdict` nodes through the human path, and the near-duplicate advisory (64-bit SimHash over hypothesis text; advisory only) routed to the human or to a `near_dup_review` park (Librarian routing arrives at M4).
acceptance_criteria:
- Every done-when clause maps to a named test run at close; the preflight answers are typed and never default to Allowed.
- Planted negative (epic level): a log truncated to an earlier valid prefix (and the re-extended, forked-head variant) must fail startup verification; a preflight on a refuted hypothesis key must not answer `Allowed`; a green Lean artifact without a `review_verdict` must stay below PROVEN; a worker returning with an open claim must yield a `Leaked` record — any of these passing silently fails the epic.
- No-Claim: ledger teeth are proven on synthetic and M1-generated entries; the orchestrator that would walk the tree is M3.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
FROM cairn-m0-e0s.13 (GC roots + reachability), a property M2 has to know.

`src/cairn/gc.py` roots liveness in the `roots` table, whose CHECK constraint
(`src/cairn/schema.sql:24-28`) admits four kinds only: recipe, ledger_row,
certificate, divergence. `reachable()` walks `lineage` undirected from those rows,
and every blob with no path to one of them is collectable.

M2's hash-chained log and its checkpoints are therefore NOT roots. A blob whose only
reference is a log entry or a checkpoint is collectable today, and `cairn gc --yes`
will delete it. This is the No-Claim line .13 closed under, not an oversight in it.

M2 has to do two things when it lands: add its root kind(s) to the `roots` CHECK
constraint, and insert a roots row as it writes each log checkpoint. The lineage
edges from a checkpoint to the blobs it covers must exist too, since reachability
reads `lineage` and nothing else.

Verified at cairn-m0-e0s.13's close commit: a blob reachable from a rooted node
survives collection and an unrooted one does not, mutation-proved by
`scripts/mutation-check.sh src/cairn/gc.py "    return set(blobs) - reachable(roots, edges)" "    return set(blobs)" tests/integration/test_gc.py tests/unit/test_gc_properties.py tests/unit/test_gc_reachability.py`
-> KILLED by 15 test(s).

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
CLOSED 2026-08-27.

DONE WHEN, clause by clause.

  the migration lands            159 PTH findings -> 0
  PTH in the select list         pyproject.toml line 48
  scripts/check.sh stays green   1838 passed, exit 0
  the write-boundary tests pass  tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py 36 passed

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE BEAD TEXT.

The bead says 95 findings across 20 files. Measured at HEAD before touching anything: 159
across 48, the growth being the doctor module and files added since the bead was written.

The bead does not mention RE-CERTIFICATION, and it was required. `src/cairn/pari.py:60`
carried a PTH113 finding, and `pari.py` is in `toy_curve.IDENTITY_SOURCES`, which
`implementation_revision()` hashes byte-for-byte. One `os.path.isfile` call therefore moves
the skill identity. Excluding it was the alternative and was refused: a permanent per-file
lint exemption for one trivial call is not what cairn-fur's standard for exemptions allows.

THE RE-CERTIFICATION, AND WHAT MOVED.

  implementation_revision  ae2b15b0...2419 -> c2d3ec90...7ece
  skill_identity_hash      be2c3574...6a89 -> ecf24823...ad1b

Two goldens moved of 23. `toy_curve_certificate.golden`: one field, `implementation_revision`.
`toy_curve_selftest_transcript.golden`: one record of six.

The transcript's changed record, decoded from its hex rather than read from a summary:

  CHANGED  P  [644105449,676417329] -> [316664663,739552369]
  CHANGED  a  487328381 -> 854200561
  CHANGED  b  284663071 -> 744592367
  CHANGED  n  827952809 -> 998221457
  CHANGED  p  827990353 -> 998256443
  same     bits 30 | cross_check "agree" | outcome "pass" | status "OK"

Records 0-3, the vendored corpus cases, and record 5, the verifier arm at 20/20, are
byte-identical. The five that moved are the drawn curve, and `selftest.run_once` seeds it
with `blake3(implementation_revision || "selftest-seed")`, so they are a direct function of
the identity. Nothing moved that does not depend on it: no verdict, clause result, ledger
entry, count, floor or cost number.

THE NEW CURVE IS VALID, NOT MERELY DIFFERENT. Checked arithmetically rather than assumed:
p = 998256443 is prime; 4a^3 + 27b^2 is nonzero mod p, so the curve is non-singular;
P = (316664663, 739552369) satisfies the curve equation; n = 998221457 is prime and lies in
the Hasse interval [998193252, 998319636]; nP is the identity; and (n-1)P = -P, so P has
exact order n rather than a proper divisor. Since n is prime and is the only multiple of n
in an interval of width about 126000, the group has prime order n. A reseed that produced a
degenerate curve while every test still passed was the worst outcome available here, and
nothing in the suite checks it, so it was checked by hand.

The goldens were regenerated, not hand-edited: `implementation_revision()` recomputed from
the tree yields the value present in the new certificate golden and absent from HEAD's.

WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND, AND WHAT CHANGED BECAUSE OF IT.

No BLOCKING and no MAJOR: a differential over every migrated os/pathlib pair, against modes
0644/0444/0000, flags UF_APPEND and UF_IMMUTABLE, dangling symlinks, missing paths and
missing parents, comparing exception TYPE and errno, found zero semantic mismatches. The
`pytest.raises(PermissionError)` on the 0444 + append-only pin did not become vacuous.

Two MINOR findings, both real, both fixed.

  `scripts/` sat in the format gate and not the lint gate, so the rule this bead exists to
  enable did not gate it. A probe file with `os.path.join` under `scripts/` passed at exit 0.
  That directory now holds `closing_commit.py`, `audit_attribution.py`, `gate_marker.py` and
  `mutation_verdict.py` -- the logic deciding whether a commit is allowed -- so it is linted
  like the code it gates. `gate lint` reads `src tests scripts`, and the twelve pre-existing
  errors that surfaced were each dispositioned rather than blanket-ignored: two UP017 and one
  FURB167 autofixed, one PERF401 rewritten, five S607 given a `scripts/**` per-file ignore
  because `git`, `br` and `uv` come from PATH by design and `src/` must keep the rule, and
  three EXE001 resolved by removing decorative shebangs from files every call site invokes
  through `uv run python`.

  The two `# noqa: PTH100` exemptions carried a justification nothing bound. Swapping them to
  `Path.resolve()` left 122 tests green. The premise needed correcting first: pytest's
  `tmp_path` is already `/private/var/...` on this machine, so a bare `tmp_path` db cannot
  distinguish `abspath` from `resolve`, which is why the mutation survived. The property is
  now bound by a symlink alias the test builds itself, observed through a delegating spy that
  records and calls through, with two-sided assertions. Both mutations are KILLED.

THE EXEMPTIONS THAT REMAIN, and why. Two sites keep `os.path.abspath`, verified by execution
rather than recalled:

  '/var/tmp/x.db'  abspath -> /var/tmp/x.db   resolve -> /private/var/tmp/x.db
  'a/../b.db'      abspath -> .../b.db        absolute -> .../a/../b.db

`Path.resolve()` follows the symlink and `Path.absolute()` does not normalize `..`, so
neither is a drop-in. Both sites derive a sibling directory of the substrate db, and
resolving would move the tree off the db's own directory.

NO-CLAIM

CI IS NOT GREEN ON THIS TIP AND CANNOT BE. The account's Actions tier is exhausted until
2026-09-01; a dispatched job returns "The job was not started because recent account payments
have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased" in four seconds with no steps. This
project's rule is that the ship is done when CI is green on the pushed commit, and that
condition is unmet. Every gate here ran on one macOS machine only.

Green does not prove that no `Path` method raises a different exception TYPE than its `os`
counterpart on a path form this suite never constructs: a null byte, a path over PATH_MAX, a
filesystem returning ELOOP. The write-boundary matrix covers the states this repo builds.
Settled by a property test parametrizing those forms across each migrated call pair,
asserting identical exception type and errno. Not built.

The identity moved for a lint fix. That is content addressing working, and it is not free:
any cached artifact keyed on the old `skill_identity_hash` is now a miss, and any record
outside this repo that quotes the old value is stale.

`tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py:232` uses a bare `pytest.raises(PermissionError)` with
no `match=`. Pre-existing, not introduced here, and the surrounding content-unchanged and
no-sibling assertions carry the contract, so it was left alone rather than churned.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. Three Opus subagents: an implementer, an auditor sharing none of
its context, and a fixer. The operator decoded the transcript golden's hex, confirmed which
fields moved and which did not, executed the abspath comparison, re-ran the write-boundary
and PTH100 mutations, and took the full gate. That is a separation of hats within one
session, not verification by another party.

title: Harness: lift the br 0.2.22 pin now that beads_rust#457 is fixed in 0.5.7
description:
`br` was rolled back to 0.2.22 on 2026-08-28 after `beads.db` corrupted twice in two hours
under 0.5.3. That was beads_rust#457, and cairn's confirmation is posted in the thread.

THE ISSUE IS CLOSED. v0.5.7 published 2026-08-29; the issue closed and was last updated
2026-08-31. Two independent A/B confirmations in the thread, each varying only the binary:

  0.5.3  ext4    malformed after write 2, 14 recovery artifacts
  0.5.7  ext4    30/30 integrity_check ok across three runs, two families, 0 artifacts
  0.5.3  tmpfs   malformed after write 1
  0.5.7  tmpfs   10/10 ok, 0 artifacts

The fix covers the SERIAL single-mutation trigger, not only the concurrent case the issue
title names. That matters here: cairn's corruption arrived from sequential single-agent
writes, which is the trigger the fix was measured against.

WHAT THE PIN COSTS TODAY
- `br create` mints `tmp...` ids unless `issue_prefix` is set explicitly; 0.5.3 inferred it.
  Worked around in `.beads/config.yaml`, but the workaround is only needed on 0.2.22.
- `br doctor health` reports healthy on a database `integrity_check` calls malformed.
- The pin is carried in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as `BR_VERSION` and in CLAUDE.md.

WHAT TO WATCH ON THE WAY UP, and it is not the corruption
0.5.x added semantic verification on import and REFUSES a JSONL payload it considers
malformed. In the issue thread it rejected four real defects in another project's exporter
output that 0.5.3 had imported without complaint: malformed dependency prefixes, edges to
dropped records, cross-store references, and dependency timestamps lacking sub-second
precision. cairn's `issues.jsonl` has been written by 0.2.22 throughout and has never been
put through that check. A refused import is the likely first failure, and it is a finding
about our data rather than about the binary.

Also: a 0.2.x binary refuses a 0.5.x-written database permanently, so the downgrade path is
`br init` in a scratch directory, the empty `beads.db` copied in beside `issues.jsonl`, then
import. That path is proven -- it is how the rollback was done.

DONE WHEN
- `br` upgraded, `BR_VERSION` in ci.yml moved to match, and CLAUDE.md's pin note replaced by
  whatever is true after.
- `issues.jsonl` round-trips: imported by the new binary and re-exported byte-identical,
  settled by sha256 in Python rather than by shell `diff`.
- If import is refused, every defect it names is recorded here with whether it is a real
  defect in our data or a false positive.
- The `issue_prefix` workaround re-tested: confirm whether an id is still minted correctly.
- `br doctor` on the upgraded store, with its output compared against the widened predicates
  in `scripts/beads_doctor_gate.py`, since those were established by observation on 0.2.22
  and a new binary may emit statuses the gate has never seen. The gate denies on anything
  unrecognized, so a vocabulary change surfaces as a blocked commit rather than silently.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
CLOSED. br is 0.5.7 and every risk this bead named was measured rather than assumed.

THE FEARED FAILURE DID NOT HAPPEN

This bead predicted that 0.5.x's semantic import verification would be the first failure, since
`issues.jsonl` has been written by 0.2.22 throughout and had never faced that check. It passed:

  br sync --import-only    66 issues processed, 66 created, 0 rejections
  PRAGMA integrity_check   ok
  round-trip               833675 bytes, sha256 6e5b202fc3ad3866, BYTE-IDENTICAL

The round-trip was settled in Python by length and digest, not by shell `diff`.

The write path, which is what forced the rollback, was probed on the real store: `br create`
minted `cairn-yzs` rather than a `tmp...` id, and `integrity_check` stayed ok. The probe was
deleted; it leaves a tombstone row in `issues.jsonl`, which is the ninth.

`scripts/beads_doctor_gate.py` accepts the new binary's vocabulary with no change: 55 `ok`,
1 `warn`, `workspace_health: healthy`, verdict advisory, no unrecognized status. That gate's
allowlist was established by observation on 0.2.22 and denies anything it has not seen, so this
is the case where it would have blocked every commit. It did not.

scripts/check.sh: 1958 passed, all gates pass, exit 0, under 0.5.7.

TWO THINGS THIS BEAD DID NOT PREDICT

The release asset renamed. The 0.5 line publishes `beads_rust-<version>-darwin_<arch>.tar.gz`;
the 0.2 line published `br-`. A version bump that left the asset name alone would have 404'd
the install step. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` carries both changes, and its install block was
executed verbatim: asset resolved, `shasum -a 256 -c` OK, `br 0.5.7`.

`br list --json` returns an object, `{"issues": [...], "total", "limit", "offset", "has_more"}`,
where 0.2.22 returned a bare array. A caller indexing it like an array gets a dict key and no
error. Nothing under `scripts/`, `tests/` or `.githooks/` parses it, so no gate broke, but
CLAUDE.md documented the array shape and would have taught an agent to write the bug.
`br show --json` still returns an array. `ISSUE_NOT_FOUND` is unchanged, which is the code
`scripts/br_lookup.py` allowlists, though its exit code moved from 6 to 3 and the classifier
keys on the code.

A TRAP FOUND BY ACCIDENT, AND RECORDED

A second bead store sits at `~/.beads` at schema 10. br walks upward for a workspace, so a
command run while the repo's `.beads` is absent binds to that one and reports
"Schema version mismatch: expected 17, found 10" -- an error about a database nobody meant to
touch, which for several minutes read as damage to ours. The repo database is schema 17 with
66 issues and `br doctor migrate-schema plan` reports no migration needed.

This also bears on `cairn-368`: its CI recipe moves `.beads` aside before `br init`. A runner
has no home store so the recipe is sound there, but the same commands on a developer machine
bind to `~/.beads` in the window between the move and the restore.

NO-CLAIM

The upgrade is verified on macOS arm64 only; the Linux arm is untested and `cairn-hcl` owns it.
The corruption fix itself is NOT independently confirmed here -- no stress run was performed on
this machine. The evidence for it is the two A/B confirmations in beads_rust#457 plus one clean
write probe, which is not a measurement of the 408-operation harness that justified the
rollback. Concurrent multi-process writes, the condition the issue title names, were not
exercised: every command in this session was sequential and single-agent. The pre-upgrade store
and the 0.2.22 binary are preserved for rollback. `br doctor` still exits 1 for any WARN, so
`scripts/beads_doctor_gate.py` remains the gate rather than the exit code. Whether 0.5.7 emits
doctor statuses beyond the two observed is unestablished; the allowlist denies on anything new,
so a vocabulary change surfaces as a blocked commit rather than a silent pass.

title: Harness: the suite hung on a macOS CI runner with no output for 45 minutes
description:
The suite hung on a GitHub macos-latest runner and produced no output for 45 minutes.

Run 32888575222, commit a71e3a0, cancelled by the job's own timeout-minutes: 45.
The gate trace ends:

  19:16:10 [check] pass format
  19:16:10 [check] pass lint
  19:16:10 [check] pass spelling
  19:16:11 [check] pass types
  20:01:17 ##[error]The operation was canceled.

So `uv run pytest -q` ran for 45 minutes and emitted nothing. What makes this a
finding rather than a slow runner:

- The same commit passes locally: 1353 passed in 377.39 s, exit 0.
- The same job on the same runner type two commits earlier (run 32887773951,
  commit 32f8743) finished pytest in 318.53 s with 1351 passed and 2 failures.
- The only change between them widened two numeric bounds in
  tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py's BUSY_ROWS table. A bound cannot
  cause a hang; the assertion it guards runs after the worker thread is joined.

OBSERVATION, not a conclusion: I have not established what blocked. The candidates
worth checking first are the tests that spawn subprocesses and wait
(tests/integration/test_runner.py, tests/e2e/), and the two busy-timeout rows whose
worker.join() has no timeout, so a second writer that never returns hangs the suite
rather than failing it. Nothing here says which, and a single occurrence may be the
runner rather than the code.

WHAT
- Give pytest its own deadline in CI so it dies with a traceback naming the test
  rather than being killed by the job, which reports nothing. Note that macOS ships
  no coreutils `timeout`, so a bare `timeout 1200 uv run pytest` fails on the runner
  this needs to work on.
- Give every worker.join() and every subprocess wait in the suite a timeout, so a
  blocked wait fails as a test rather than as a job cancellation.
- Re-run the cancelled commit to establish whether it reproduces at all before
  treating it as a code defect.

DONE WHEN: a deliberately hanging test fails CI with the test name in the output
within its own deadline, rather than being cancelled by timeout-minutes with a
blank transcript; and either the hang reproduces and is fixed, or three consecutive
green runs on a71e3a0 or later record it as unreproduced.

Related: scripts/check.sh captured each gate's output until it exited, which is why
the transcript was blank rather than merely inconclusive. Fixed separately; the gates
now stream.
notes:
ARTIFACTS-BEGIN
source: `tests/_session_deadline.py` lines 1-122
source: `scripts/check.sh` lines 60-71
source: `scripts/mutation_verdict.py` lines 1-52
source: `scripts/mutation-check.sh` lines 40-62
source: `pyproject.toml` lines 34-38
source: `tests/conftest.py` lines 1-20
test: `tests/integration/test_session_deadline.py` lines 1-257
test: `tests/unit/test_check_gate_instruments.py` lines 1-135
test: `tests/unit/test_mutation_verdict.py` lines 1-81
command: scripts/check.sh
command: uv run pytest -q tests/integration/test_session_deadline.py
command: scripts/mutation-check.sh tests/_session_deadline.py 'faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(self.seconds + BACKSTOP_GRACE, exit=True, file=self.fd)' 'pass' tests/integration/test_session_deadline.py
ARTIFACTS-END
close_reason: Two complementary session watchdogs; both holes reproduced and closed

comments.text:

macos-latest runner: 1352 passed in 298.82 s, with only the host-bound certificate

- DONE: scripts/check.sh streams each gate instead of collecting its output, so a

- STILL WORTH DOING: pytest needs its own deadline in CI so a hang dies with a

- STILL WORTH DOING: the busy-timeout rows join a worker thread with no timeout, so
