comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
FROM cairn-m0-e0s.18: two subprocess waits this bead's deadline work should cover,
and one test that can go red for a reason that is not a defect.

`tests/integration/test_doctor.py` spawns real child interpreters in two places: the
concurrency test (two `cairn doctor --fix` children racing for the lock) and the
crash test (a child SIGKILLed between backup and apply). Both called
`communicate()` with no timeout when they landed. The audit flagged it against this
bead, and both now pass `timeout=60`, so a wedged child fails as a test rather than
as a job cancellation. That is the shape this bead asks for, applied to the two new
waits.

The second item is not fixed and wants a decision here rather than in the doctor.

The concurrency test is inherently racy. It asserts that one child exits 0 or 2 and
the other exits 5, which holds only if the second child reaches the lock while the
first still holds it. The lock is taken before detection, which makes the window
wide, but it is a window: if the first child finishes before the second acquires,
the assertion fails. That is a flaky RED, never a flaky green -- it cannot pass
while the lock is broken -- so it is honest, and the mutation proving it
(`LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` to `LOCK_SH | LOCK_NB`) is KILLED by 2 tests.

Every construction available from the test side alone either makes both children
lose, which is vacuous, or leaves the same window. Closing it needs an env-gated
hold seam inside `mutate.Lock.acquire`, in the shape of the existing
`CAIRN_DOCTOR_CRASH_AFTER_BACKUP` hook. Adding a production sleep hook for a test
was declined rather than done quietly.

So the open question belongs with this bead's deadline work: is a test that can go
red on scheduler luck acceptable in CI, or does it earn the fourth seam? A retry
would be the wrong answer -- it would mask a genuinely broken lock.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
FROM cairn-exi's session, 2026-08-26: a load-sensitive wall-clock ceiling, measured.

Not the hang this bead describes -- that signature is no output for 45 minutes, and
what happened here was slow-but-progressing output under saturation. Recorded because
the mechanism is the one this bead has to reason about, and because it is now measured
rather than hypothesized.

WHAT HAPPENED. `scripts/check.sh` ran while several subagents were each running full
pytest suites. Load average reached 131. The suite reached 46 percent, emitted nothing
for 16 minutes, and was killed at a 600-second tool timeout. A clean reproduction of
the same commit then finished in 771 seconds against a normal 240 -- four times slower,
never stalled.

THE THREE FAILURES UNDER LOAD, all in tests/integration/test_runner.py:

  test_a_real_forty_bit_launch_records_a_receipt_with_live_measurements
  test_the_manifest_carries_the_skill_s_own_output_bytes
  test_a_second_identical_launch_is_served_from_cache

each on the same assertion:

  assert attempt.status == "OK" and not attempt.served_from_cache
  AssertionError: assert ('BUDGET_EXCEEDED' == 'OK')

The runner enforces a ceiling of `ceiling_multiplier: 4` -- four times the cost
profile's predicted wall for a 40-bit launch (tests/integration/test_runner.py:35-45).
A real PARI launch exceeds it under contention.

  loaded   (load avg 131)  3 failed, 1626 passed in 771.50s
  quiet    (load avg 13)   49 passed in 8.74s   -- the whole file, exit 0

WHY IT BELONGS HERE. A GitHub-hosted runner is shared and its load is not observable
from inside the job. A ceiling calibrated against an idle machine converts contention
into a red suite that reads as a code defect, and the failure names a budget rather
than a scheduler, so the next reader chases the runner instead of the load. That is the
same class of misattribution this bead exists to stop: the transcript has to say what
actually happened.

Two things for whoever takes this bead. A per-test deadline that dies with a traceback
naming the test would have turned the 16-minute silence into a named failure in
seconds, which is already this bead's first WHAT item; and it should decide whether
`ceiling_multiplier` is the right instrument at all, since a multiplier over a
predicted wall measures the machine as much as the skill. Raising it buys green at the
cost of the budget meaning anything.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
Three of the four items are settled; the fourth is a decision for the operator.

ITEM 1 (check.sh streams) — CONFIRMED STILL TRUE. `scripts/check.sh` lines 40-56: `gate()`
runs `"$@"` directly with no capture, and appends RUN/PASS/FAIL to `.check.log` around it.
A stall now leaves a `RUN <gate>` line with no matching PASS.

ITEM 2 (pytest's own deadline) — DONE, commit 1e16fc3. pytest-timeout pinned at 2.4.0, with
`timeout = 180` and `timeout_method = "thread"` in `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`, so CI and a
local run enforce the same deadline and no coreutils `timeout` is involved.

  Derivation of 180 s. Longest single item measured here is 8.32 s
  (`tests/conformance/test_skill_contract.py::test_clause[toy_curve-S2-01]` setup, from
  `--durations=25` over 1648 passing tests in 232.44 s). The worst contention factor this
  project has measured is 4x, putting a contended worst case near 33 s. The longest chain of
  inner subprocess bounds inside one test is 120 s -- the two 60 s `communicate()` calls in
  the doctor concurrency test -- so 180 s keeps the inner, more specific bound firing first,
  and stays 15x below the job's 45-minute ceiling.

  `thread` over `signal`: signal delivery cannot interrupt a blocked C call holding the GIL
  and cannot reach a hang in a worker thread. Both candidate hangs take exactly that shape --
  a SQLite busy wait, a flock, an `os.wait4` with no timeout parameter.

  Observed against a test that sleeps for an hour, with the deadline dropped to 8 s:

    +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ Timeout +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
      File ".../tests/unit/test_deadline_demo.py", line 5, in
        test_a_test_that_blocks_past_the_deadline_is_named_in_the_output
        time.sleep(3600)

  A hang in a fixture is covered by the same budget: the same instrument against a wedged
  fixture names `File "/tmp/dl/test_setup_hang.py", line 8, in wedged`.

ITEM 3 (the unbounded worker join) — FIXED, commit 2fc25cb, and it carried a second defect.
`tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py:114` joins with the row's own declared ceiling
plus 25 s, and a worker still alive after it is an assertion naming the `busy_timeout` that
did not return. The thread is now a daemon, because a join timeout alone does not help: the
first attempt at the mutation never terminated at all, since pytest waited at interpreter
shutdown on three sleeping non-daemon threads after the assertions had already fired.

  scripts/mutation-check.sh tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py \
    'b.execute("insert into t values (2)")' 'time.sleep(3600)' \
    tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py
  KILLED  by 3 test(s): 3 failed, 6 passed, 8 warnings in 87.54s

  AssertionError: the second writer with busy_timeout=0 ms never returned within 25.1 s

ITEM 4 (the sweep) — DONE, commit 1e16fc3. Bounded at 60 s: `communicate()` and `wait()` in
`tests/integration/test_grounding_subprocess.py`, the gp version probe in
`tests/integration/test_grounding_gp.py`, the CLI child in
`tests/integration/test_cli_streams.py`, the eight validator children in
`tests/unit/test_bead_artifact_block.py`, the script child in
`tests/unit/test_scorecard_coherence.py`. Two waits stay unbounded with a reason: `os.wait4`
has no timeout parameter in Python, so the calls in `test_grounding_subprocess.py` and
`test_runner.py` rely on the per-test deadline and each reaps a child that runs `sys.exit(3)`
or `pass`; and `child.wait()` in `tests/fixtures/skills/forks_a_grandchild.py` runs inside a
skill the runner spawns under `ceiling_s` plus grace and a SIGKILL, so the runner bounds it
and a timeout there would change what the fixture models.

`scripts/bead_artifact_block.py` calls `git cat-file` and `br show` with no timeout. That is
the commit gate, not the suite, so it is outside this bead's WHAT and is left alone rather
than changed unasked.

SECOND HALF OF DONE WHEN — CONFIRMED. `gh api` on the three runs after the incident:
32895819844 (2bdbda8), 32896614987 (5faab01), 32898412001 (5ce45fe), all `success`, all on
commits `git merge-base --is-ancestor a71e3a0` confirms are descendants of a71e3a0. Their
`Gates` step, which is the whole of `scripts/check.sh`, took 245 s, 259 s and 266 s
respectively -- the same order as the 318 s and 298 s baselines the bead already records, not
a run that scraped in under the ceiling. Raw job logs for all three now return 404, so the
pytest line itself is no longer recoverable; the step duration is the bound that survives.

THE OPERATOR'S OPEN QUESTION, now measured rather than worried about. Over 25 back-to-back
trials of the doctor concurrency scenario, reading `lock_taken` / `lock_released` /
`lock_held` timestamps out of both children's JSON stderr:

  hold_ms     min 58.66   median 66.20   max 124.37
  arrival_ms  min -0.19   median  1.12   max  11.17
  outcomes    25 of 25 gave (0, 5)

`arrival_ms` is how far after the winner took the lock the loser reached it. The window is the
hold; the risk is the arrival exceeding it. Worst observed pairing is a 58.66 ms hold against
an 11.17 ms arrival, so the loser would have to be 5.3x later than its own worst observed
offset to miss. The median margin is 65 ms. Both children pay the same interpreter startup,
which is why they converge within a millisecond, and contention slows both together rather
than staggering them.

Recommendation, and it is a recommendation only: leave the seam out. A production sleep hook
inside `mutate.Lock.acquire` buys a margin that is already 5x on the worst of 25 trials, and
it is the kind of hook that outlives its reason. Stated limit: n=25 on one machine at load
average ~6, not on a GitHub runner, and I have no way to measure the arrival spread under
runner contention from here.

THE DEADLINE COSTS NOTHING. `scripts/check.sh` run alone, both times on this machine:

  before  fefd33e   1648 passed in 232.44 s   exit 0   load average 5.68 at the end
  after   1e16fc3   1648 passed in 232.15 s   exit 0   load average 6.51 at the end

Commits: 2fc25cb, 1e16fc3. Not closed: the first DONE WHEN clause is demonstrated locally,
not yet observed on a runner, and nothing here has been pushed.

     `tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py:113-117` now joins with the row's own
     declared ceiling plus 25 s and asserts `not worker.is_alive()` with a message
     naming what did not return. Mutation re-run by me at HEAD:

       $ bash scripts/mutation-check.sh tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py \
           'b.execute("insert into t values (2)")' 'time.sleep(3600)' \
           tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py
       KILLED  by 3 test(s): 3 failed, 6 passed in 86.12s          EXIT=0

  4  SWEPT. Every unbounded wait in the suite is now bounded or explicitly justified:

       bounded to 60 s: test_grounding_subprocess.py:18 and :43, test_grounding_gp.py:76,

         test_scorecard_coherence.py:192
       already bounded: test_doctor.py:660,661,671 (60 s, from cairn-m0-e0s.18),

         tests/fixtures/skills/forks_a_grandchild.py:21 `child.wait()` runs inside a

       production, already bounded: runner.py:212, measure.py:229, pari.py:70-73,
         doctor/mutate.py:56 (SIGKILL-after, explicit timeout, LOCK_NB).

The doctor's concurrency test asserts one child exits 0 or 2 while the other exits 5,

  hold_ms      min 58.66   median 66.20   max 124.37
  arrival_ms   min -0.19   median  1.12   max  11.17
  outcomes     25 of 25 gave (0, 5)

have to be 5.3 times later than its own worst observed offset to miss. Both children
pay the same interpreter startup, which is why they converge within a millisecond, and
contention slows both together rather than staggering them.

already 5x at the worst of 25 trials, and a hook like that outlives its reason. A retry

THE SUITE

  1648 passed, 9 warnings in 218.83s

Unchanged at 1648 from fefd33e. The per-test deadline costs 0.3 s across 1648 tests,

This work hardens against a class of failure. It does not explain the instance: what

`scripts/bead_artifact_block.py:166,178` runs `git cat-file` and `br show` with no

REOPENED 2026-08-27: it recurred, on this bead's own instruction to reopen if it did.

  05:14:26Z [check] pass theater
  05:14:26Z [check] run tests
  05:29:33Z (job cancelled by timeout-minutes)

Fifteen minutes and eighteen seconds, no output after `run tests`. The same shape as
run 32888575222: four gate lines and then silence. It reads shorter only because the
ceiling had been lowered from 45 to 15 in the same session.

WHAT IS NEW SINCE THE ORIGINAL INCIDENT, and what each instrument said:

  `scripts/check.sh` streams. It named the gate: the suite, not a linter. That is the
  half of this bead that was already done, working.

  `pytest-timeout` at 180 s, thread method, DID NOT FIRE. That is information, not a
  failure of the instrument: no single test exceeded three minutes. The suite was
  uniformly slow rather than stuck on one item, so a per-test deadline cannot catch
  this shape. A per-SESSION deadline would.

  The failure-artifact upload was SKIPPED, because `if: failure()` does not match a
  cancelled job, and a job killed by the ceiling is cancelled. Fixed alongside this
  note: `if: failure() || cancelled()`. The run whose artifacts are hardest to get any
  other way was the one uploading none.

  `timeout-minutes` raised 15 -> 30. Fifteen was set on the reasoning that a green run
  takes five minutes and three times that is headroom. This run measured a slow runner
  at fifteen-plus, so that reasoning was right on the numbers and wrong on the variance.
  Thirty distinguishes slow from stuck; 45 was what the original incident burned.

WHAT IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED. Nothing here explains what consumed the time. The local
suite runs 1702 tests in about 230 s on a quiet machine; CI's own green runs sit at
245-300 s. This run was at least 3.5x that with no per-test outlier.

The candidates this bead already names are unchanged and unexcluded: the tests that
spawn subprocesses and wait, now bounded at 60 s each, and anything contending for the
runner. A third is worth adding: this session measured on the local machine that
contention alone produces exactly this profile -- 1648 tests at 771 s against a normal
230 s, four times slower, never stalled, with three BUDGET_EXCEEDED failures that
passed 49/49 once quiet. A shared runner is not observable from inside the job.

NEXT STEP, for whoever takes this. A session-level deadline is the missing instrument:
something that kills pytest a few minutes before the job ceiling and dumps every
thread's stack, so a uniformly slow run leaves a profile rather than a silence. That is
the same instrument this bead's first WHAT item asked for, applied to the whole session
rather than one test. `--durations=25` in CI would also make a slow-but-progressing run
diagnosable after the fact, and costs nothing.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
CLOSED 2026-08-27 at the commit this comment ships with.

THE SHAPE THE SECOND HANG HAD, and why the shipped instrument did not catch it.

The reopen note asked for a session-level deadline: something that kills pytest before the
job ceiling and dumps every thread's stack, so a uniformly slow run leaves a profile rather
than a silence. That is built. It took two instruments rather than one, and the reason is
the finding worth carrying forward.

WHAT WAS BUILT

  tests/_session_deadline.py arms two independent watchdogs from pytest_configure, both
  writing to an os.dup of the real stderr taken before pytest's fd capture redirects fd 2.

  PRIMARY: a private daemon thread waiting on a threading.Event. On expiry it prints a
  Timeout (H:MM:SS)! banner, calls faulthandler.dump_traceback(all_threads=True) and exits
  124. Deadline from CAIRN_SESSION_DEADLINE, default 1500 s.

  BACKSTOP: faulthandler.dump_traceback_later at deadline + 15 s, exit code 1, which
  faulthandler fixes and does not let a caller change. pyproject.toml blocks pytest's
  bundled faulthandler plugin so nothing can cancel it.

  A malformed or non-positive value raises pytest.UsageError at configure time and runs zero
  tests, rather than falling back to no deadline. The one way to run unbounded is
  CAIRN_SESSION_DEADLINE_SKIP='<reason>', which prints its reason to stderr.

  scripts/check.sh adds --durations=25 and logs the armed deadline and both exit codes to
  .check.log, so a reader who tails the log after a hang can tell the instrument was on.

THE TWO HOLES, EACH REPRODUCED

An independent audit found the first and the operator reproduced the second. Neither
instrument alone is sufficient, and each covers exactly the other's gap.

  A single-instrument thread watchdog is STARVED by a GIL-holding C call. Child body
  re.match(r"(a+)+$", "a" * 40 + "b") under a 4 s deadline: alive at 30 s, killed by an
  external SIGKILL at exit 137, zero Timeout banners.

  A single-instrument faulthandler timer is CANCELLED by the first test failure. pytest's
  bundled plugin registers pytest_exception_interact as tryfirst and calls
  cancel_dump_traceback_later unconditionally; runner.py fires it on every reported failure
  and every collection error. Child whose first test fails and whose second sleeps 3600,
  under a 4 s deadline: alive at 20 s, SIGKILL, exit 137, zero banners.

  So the instrument evaporated in exactly the case it exists for: a long session that is
  both slow and failing.

BOTH REPRODUCTIONS RE-RUN AT THIS COMMIT, by the operator

  GIL-STALL        EXIT=1   wall=19s  banners=1   (4 s deadline + 15 s backstop grace)
  FAIL-THEN-HANG   EXIT=124 wall=5s   banners=1   (thread, at its own deadline)

  The GIL profile names the frame: re/__init__.py line 167 in match. The fail-then-hang
  profile names tests/_session_deadline.py line 95 in _watch and the hanging test.

  Live on the real suite through the repository conftest, not the -p path:
  CAIRN_SESSION_DEADLINE=2 uv run pytest -q tests/integration/test_gc.py -> EXIT=1,
  Timeout (0:00:02)!, two thread stacks, one naming test_gc.py line 192 and
  src/cairn/substrate.py line 248 in _tx.

WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND, and what each mutation says now

Twelve findings, all accepted and fixed, each proven red by scripts/mutation-check.sh:

  BLOCKING  the faulthandler cancellation above.
  BLOCKING  nothing proved the real suite loaded the plugin at all. Every test passed it by
            hand with -p, so deleting the conftest import left 13 of 13 green while
            check.sh kept logging DEADLINE 1500s -- a false line in the artifact a reader
            tails after a hang. Now KILLED by 1 test.
  MAJOR     next(...) at module scope raised StopIteration on a renamed gate and took the
            whole collection down, running zero tests session-wide.
  MAJOR     the 1500 s default was asserted as a constant and never armed; mutating it to
            999999 survived all 13 tests.
  Seven more: a spelling-only --durations assertion that a harmless line-wrap turned red;
  no proof the durations table appears; uncovered teardown; uncovered blank-value branch; a
  leaked hung child; a marker oracle correct only by luck; a duplicate parametrize case.

  Incidental, outside the bead and fixed here because it under-reports on every future
  bead: scripts/mutation-check.sh scored a pytest COLLECTION ERROR as SURVIVED, because it
  matched only "N failed" and pytest prints "1 error". Verdict logic moved to
  scripts/mutation_verdict.py with 13 tests of its own.

SUITE: 1702 at ab4b033 -> 1744 here, exit 0, run by the operator on a quiet machine.
--durations=25 immediately named its own most expensive test at 19.08s.

NO-CLAIM

This does not explain either hang. What consumed the time on runs 32888575222 and
33041862321 is unestablished and is not established here. The bead's DONE WHEN asked for
either a fix or three green runs recording it unreproduced; neither happened. What is
delivered is the instrument the reopen note asked for: the NEXT occurrence leaves a
thread-stack profile and a durations table instead of a blank transcript.

Nothing here has run on a GitHub runner. Every measurement is macOS arm64 on one machine.
The first CI run on this commit is the first exercise of both instruments on a runner.

The 15 s backstop grace and the 1500 s default are judgment calls, not measurements. The
two slow runs were cancelled before finishing, so their true duration is unknown. If a
healthy CI run ever exceeds 25 minutes, the default converts a slow-but-fine run into a red
one, and the tell will be a Timeout banner with a profile showing progress rather than a
block.

Blocking the bundled faulthandler plugin gives up its dump-on-fatal-signal behavior for
this suite. The two watchdogs cover a deadline, not a segfault. Owned by no bead; if a
segfault ever goes undiagnosed here, that is the cause to check first.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED

Three Opus subagents: one implementer, one auditor that shared no context with it, one
fixer. The operator re-executed both hang reproductions, the live-conftest probe, the
malformed-value denial, the bypass, the full gate, and read every diff line. The audit's
own suggested fix for the BLOCKING finding -- re-arming inside a trylast
pytest_exception_interact -- was declined and replaced, because it races the same global
slot it is trying to defend. That is a separation of hats within one session, not
verification by another party.

title: Harness: S2-12 passes a skill that hardcodes its in-range cross-check result
description:
The section 2 conformance harness (cairn-m0-e0s.16) extracts S2-12 as: axis in
{implementation, algorithm}, independent_range an interval record over the input
fields, result == untested outside that range, and the certificate's
selftest_summary.cross_check block carrying only axis and independent_range.

A subject satisfies all four while performing no cross-check at all. It declares
an axis, declares a range, reports untested outside it, and hardcodes a string
inside it. tests/fixtures/skills/nonconforming.py is exactly that shape and
scores PASS on S2-12.

What catches such a subject is S2-10, which plants a disagreement at the declared
seam through the real runner and requires the status to move to DISAGREE. The
nonconforming fixture fails S2-10 for that reason. So the harness as a whole is
not fooled; S2-12 alone is.

The gap is that the two clauses interlock without saying so. A skill that
declares no seam, or declares one it does not call, fails S2-10 and passes S2-12,
and a reader of the matrix cannot tell from the S2-12 column whether a
cross-check exists.

The change: give S2-12 an in-range arm that requires the reported result to move
when the declared seam is planted, and let a constant string fail. The verdict
reasons then say which of the two clauses carries the evidence.

Cost of doing it inside cairn-m0-e0s.16 rather than here: the bead specifies the
nonconforming fixture must fail exactly S2-01, S2-04, S2-10 and S2-11. The
stronger arm adds S2-12 to that set, which is a change to that bead's acceptance
criteria rather than a fix inside them.

Evidence, at commit 1fe8d6c:

  uv run python <scratch>/dump.py

  nonconforming
  S2-10 MUST   FAIL  a planted disagreement at cairn.pari.ellsea still returned OK
  S2-12 MUST   PASS  axis algorithm, range {'bits': [0, 50]}, untested outside it
                     and in the ledger

Recorded in tests/conformance/COVERAGE.md under "What these checks do not decide".

ARTIFACTS-END
close_reason: S2-12 gained an in-range arm at 58a1438: the reported cross-check result must move when the declared seam is planted, so nonconforming drops from 8/12 to 7/12 while toy_curve holds at 12/12, and the S2-12 column now carries its own evidence rather than leaning on S2-10

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
CLOSED AT 0e56023. Two commits: 58a1438 (the in-range arm), 0e56023 (the record on
cairn-m0-e0s.16, whose acceptance this changes).

THE DEFECT, REPRODUCED AND INVERTED

S2-12 extracted four conditions -- an axis in {implementation, algorithm}, an
independent_range interval, `untested` outside that range, and the certificate's
cross_check block carrying only axis and range. A subject satisfies all four while
performing no cross-check at all: declare an axis, declare a range, report untested
outside it, and hardcode a string inside it. `tests/fixtures/skills/nonconforming.py`
is exactly that shape.

  before   S2-12 MUST  PASS  axis algorithm, range {'bits': [0, 50]}, untested
                             outside it and in the ledger
  after    S2-12 MUST  FAIL  in range the cross-check reports 'agree' whether or not
                             cairn.pari.ellsea is planted, so it compares nothing and
                             S2-12 carries no evidence that a cross-check exists

THE THREE-SUBJECT MATRIX, re-executed by me at HEAD through scripts/check.sh

  clause         nonconforming  toy_curve      witness
  S2-10 MUST     FAIL           PASS           FAIL
  S2-11 MUST     FAIL           PASS           PASS
  S2-12 MUST     FAIL           PASS           FAIL
  nonconforming MUST score 7/12   (was 8/12)
  toy_curve MUST score 12/12      (unchanged)
  witness MUST score 3/12         (unchanged)

Exactly one cell moves. `toy_curve` performs a real cross-check and still scores
12/12, which is the half that matters: the arm passes a conforming subject rather
than failing everything. `witness` fails S2-12 at the first arm on
`cross_check.axis 'vibes' is not one of ['implementation', 'algorithm']`, so the new
arm is never reached and its score is untouched.

  $ scripts/check.sh          (run alone; load 7.93 before)
  1648 passed, 8 warnings in 227.70s
  [check] all gates pass                              EXIT=0

Unchanged at 1648: the arm lives inside an existing clause and adds no test.

ONE MECHANISM, TWO CLAUSES

S2-10's planting was reusable as-is. It launches `skills.harness_child` with
CAIRN_HARNESS_SUBJECT and CAIRN_HARNESS_MODE=seam, and the child monkeypatches
`subject.SEAM` to `real(...) + 2` before delegating; the only per-clause difference
is the recipe salt. It is extracted verbatim into
`_launch_with_planted_seam(subject, ctx, salt)` and `_declared_seam(module)`, and
S2-10 now calls the helper. Two clauses, one implementation, no second planting path
to drift.

THE VERDICT REASONS NOW CARRY THE EVIDENCE

That was the bead's actual purpose: a reader of the S2-12 column could not tell
whether a cross-check existed, because S2-10 was silently carrying that weight.

  toy_curve PASS   ...untested outside it and in the ledger; in range 'agree' moves
                   to 'disagree' when cairn.pari.ellsea is planted, so S2-12 itself
                   carries the evidence that a comparison runs
  no seam   FAIL   the subject declares no seam, so its in-range result answers to
                   no second opinion

PROVED ABLE TO FAIL

  `if planted == inside:` -> `if False and planted == inside:`
      KILLED by 2 test(s): 2 failed, 47 passed
  `_launch_with_planted_seam(...)` -> `_launch(...)`  (the plant removed)
      KILLED by 2 test(s): 2 failed, 47 passed

The second is the one that matters. With the plant removed, `toy_curve` itself fails
S2-12, so its PASS is carried by observed movement rather than by an arm that cannot
fail.

NO GOLDEN MOVED

`matrix()` is a `pytest_terminal_summary` section, not a golden, and the MUST-failure
set lives in code (`expected_must_failures`) rather than in a captured file. The four
`*_floor.golden` files are read by S2-05 and S2-06, which this arm does not touch.
`toy_curve.IDENTITY_SOURCES` is untouched, so no transcript or certificate golden
reseeded.

A CLOSED BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE CHANGES, AND IS SAID SO

`cairn-m0-e0s.16` is closed, and its acceptance says the nonconforming fixture fails
exactly S2-01, S2-04, S2-10 and S2-11. That set is now five. The bead is not reopened
or edited; a comment on it records the change so a later reader of its close evidence
is not misled.

ONE DISAGREEMENT WITH MY OWN DIRECTION, AND IT WAS RIGHT

I asked for the COVERAGE.md matrix row for S2-12 to gain the new arm. The clause
table's third column is a verbatim PLAN §2 quote, and
`test_clause_table.py::test_coverage_table_matches_clauses` binds only id, level and
check-function name. Editing the quote would have misattributed the arm to PLAN. The
arm is documented instead under "Where a check reads more than the sentence", beside
S2-10's and S2-11's extra arms, and the quoted row is intact. Settled by
`uv run pytest tests/conformance/test_clause_table.py -q`, green.

NO-CLAIM

This proves S2-12 no longer passes a subject whose in-range result cannot move. It
does not prove the arm is right for a subject that declares a SEAM and never calls it
on the in-range path: no such fixture exists, and the arm would report the
constant-result FAIL for it, which is the intended verdict but is inference rather
than measurement. Recorded on cairn-fur, which owns the harness's pattern surface.

The arm adds two launches per subject to S2-12. The conformance module runs 53 passed
in 8.94 s after the change; the before figure was not timed, so no claim is made about
its cost.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED

Implemented by one subagent. I re-ran the full suite at HEAD and read the printed
matrix myself, read the arm and both verdict reasons in the source, and confirmed the
one-cell movement and that toy_curve holds at 12/12. I did not re-run the two
mutations. That is a separation of hats within one session, not independent
verification by another party.

title: Harness: CI has no br, so the artifact-block gate and the pre-commit hook are tested only where they already work
description:
CI installs pari and nothing else, so `br` is absent on the runner. The
artifact-block gate refuses without it -- correctly, since reporting a block as
valid without reading the body would be a silent fail-open -- and the consequence
is that the gate's happy path is never exercised anywhere but a developer machine.

Measured 2026-08-27 at commit 4ec8697: 22 of the 23 tests in
`tests/unit/test_bead_artifact_block.py` pass with `br` off PATH, because they
drive validation over a body file. The twenty-third drives the gate by bead id and
therefore needs `br show`. Its oracle was corrected to assert the parity deny by
its reason rather than by an exit code with two causes, which is right on its own
terms, but it does not restore the coverage: on CI nothing reads a real bead body
through the gate.

The same holds for `.githooks/pre-commit` as a whole. It runs `bead-test-plan.sh`,
`bead-artifact-block.sh` and the compliance audit, every one of which shells out to
`br`, and none of them runs on the runner. The hook is tested only where it is
already known to work.

WHAT: give CI a real `br`. It is `beads_rust` on crates.io (0.5.1 published; 0.2.10
is what this machine has, so pin deliberately rather than taking latest). A
`cargo install` compiles a 10 MB binary and will dominate the job unless the
resulting binary is cached on the cargo bin path across runs, so the cache is part
of the work rather than an optimization.

Do NOT satisfy this with a stand-in `br` that returns canned JSON. The thing under
test is the gate reading a real bead, and a fake `br` would make the test pass
while proving nothing -- the same fail-open shape the gate itself refuses.

DONE WHEN: `test_a_matching_extractor_regex_does_not_deny` exercises a real `br
show` on the runner; a CI run's log shows the artifact-block gate reading a bead
body and passing; and the added install does not lengthen the job by more than a
minute on a warm cache, measured across three runs.

Surfaced by the first push of the M0 straggler session: 43 commits, all green
locally, one red on the runner for exactly this reason.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
SECOND HALF OF THE SAME GAP: the compliance skill is absent on CI too, so the
extractor-parity cross-check never runs there.

Observed in run 33037689499 (commit 98333ee, green):

  PARITY-UNKNOWN artifact-block: the compliance skill is not installed;
                 the extractor regex was not compared

repeated on every invocation the suite makes. `scripts/bead_artifact_block.py:281-289`
prints that to stderr and CONTINUES.

The warn-rather-deny choice is deliberate and, on its own terms, right. The two
missing-infra cases are not the same:

  br absent            DENY (exit 3). The gate cannot do its job at all -- reporting a
                       block as valid without reading the body is a silent fail-open.
  skill absent         WARN. The gate can still do its job; it loses one auxiliary
                       cross-check. Denying would make the gate unrunnable on every
                       machine that does not vendor the skill, CI included.

What it costs: the parity check exists to catch drift between this repo's copy of
`PATH_HINT_RE` and the vendored extractor's. An upstream skill update that changes
that regex would make cairn accept blocks the audit cannot read -- the appearance of
a gate with none of its effect. On CI that drift is undetectable, so the protection
is a developer-machine-only property, and the log line is its only trace.

This is the same root cause as this bead's `br` half: the runner carries neither, so
`.githooks/pre-commit` and everything it invokes are exercised only where they are
already known to work. Whatever gives CI a real `br` should give it the vendored skill
as well, and the DONE WHEN should require a CI log showing `PASS artifact-block <id>`
rather than `PARITY-UNKNOWN`.

Same prohibition as the br half: do not satisfy this with a stub skill carrying a
copy of the regex. That would compare cairn's regex against a fixture cairn also
controls, which is a check that cannot fail.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
A second surface for this bead's thesis, found while closing cairn-fi7.

The pre-commit and post-commit hooks grew real decision logic: a closing-commit resolver
whose git failures must DENY, an attribution corrector whose exit code the hook gates on,
and a gate-coverage record that decides whether post-commit is allowed to push. The Python
holding those decisions is covered at 94-98 percent.

The bash that calls it is covered at zero, and not by oversight: `tests/conftest.py`'s
`isolation_guard` refuses a subprocess whose argv0 is not `sys.executable` or the gp
binary, so no test in this suite can spawn `bash` to exercise a hook. The uncovered call
sites are `record_gate`, the coverage `check`, the `CLOSING_RC` branches and the
`ATTRIBUTION-DENY` case.

That is the same shape this bead already names for CI: the gate is exercised only where it
already works. Whatever answer this bead reaches for running the hooks where `br` and the
compliance skill are absent should also say how the hook shell gets exercised anywhere.

cairn-rof carries the other half, the record attesting to a parent rather than to the
staged tree.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
CLOSED 2026-08-27. All three DONE-WHEN clauses are settled on real runner evidence, taken
before the account's Actions tier ran out.

DONE WHEN, clause by clause.

1. `test_a_matching_extractor_regex_does_not_deny` EXERCISES A REAL `br show` ON THE RUNNER.

   The runner installs the published darwin binary for the version pinned in
   `BR_VERSION`, checked against the sha256 published beside it, cached on the cargo bin
   path and keyed on the version.

   The test's prior oracle was two negative assertions -- "no longer matches" not in stderr,
   "DENY artifact-block parity" not in the log -- and both hold VACUOUSLY when the gate exits
   3 for want of `br`, which is exactly what CI did. It now requires exit 0, the
   `pass cairn-exi (closed):` line on stdout, and `PASS artifact-block cairn-exi` in
   `.check.log`. None of those can be produced by a run that never read a bead.

   Mutation proof that the new oracle gates, explicit single target:

     scripts/mutation-check.sh scripts/bead_artifact_block.py \
       'if shutil.which("br") is None:' 'if shutil.which("br") is not None:' \
       tests/unit/test_bead_artifact_block.py
     KILLED  by 2 test(s): 2 failed, 24 passed

   Under the prior oracle the same mutation SURVIVED.

2. A CI RUN'S LOG SHOWS THE GATE READING A BEAD BODY AND PASSING.

   Run 33104091974, commit 6e876e7, macos-latest, green. From the step that cats
   `.check.log`:

     2026-08-27T18:38:22Z PASS artifact-block cairn-exi
     2026-08-27T18:38:22Z BYPASS artifact-block cairn-exi: proving the bypass is logged
     2026-08-27T18:38:22Z DENY artifact-block infra: br not on PATH

   and from the step before it: `br 0.5.3`.

   Both arms are exercised there: the gate reads a real bead and passes, and the
   absent-`br` deny still fires, asserted by its reason rather than by an exit code with two
   causes. The gate is no longer tested only where it already worked.

3. THE INSTALL COSTS UNDER A MINUTE ON A WARM CACHE, ACROSS THREE RUNS.

   Step timings, `Restore br` + `Install br` + the version print:

     33104091974  cold   1s + 1s + 0s = 2s   (Install br ran)
     33105687625  warm   2s + 0s + 0s = 2s   (Install br SKIPPED, cache hit)
     33105703637  warm   3s + 0s + 0s = 3s   (Install br SKIPPED, cache hit)

   Three seconds against a sixty-second budget. The skipped step in runs two and three also
   settles the implementer's UNVERIFIED note about whether `actions/cache` v6.1.0's
   `cache-hit` output behaves as assumed on this runner: it does.

THE PROHIBITION WAS HONORED. No stub `br`, no canned JSON, no stub compliance skill, no
skip and no platform conditional. The gate reads the real `cairn-exi` out of the real
`.beads/issues.jsonl` that `br` imports. `scripts/theater-patterns.sh` passes.

A DEVIATION FROM THE BEAD TEXT, ON EVIDENCE. The bead specifies `cargo install beads_rust`.
That route does not hold on a stable toolchain, and both lines fail differently:

  0.2.10  a dependency is gated behind a nightly-only feature (`#![feature(portable_simd)]`)
  0.5.3   declares a rustc floor of 1.95/1.96, above the 1.94 available

Either failure would be a red run about Rust rather than about cairn. The published release
binary is the route taken, and the version swap was proven safe rather than assumed:
`br show <id> --json` is byte-identical between 0.2.10 and 0.5.3 on this repository's beads,
compared by sha256 under a pristine HOME in a fresh clone.

Checkout takes full history, because the gate resolves every commit an ARTIFACTS block
names and a depth-1 clone reads all five of cairn-exi's as absent.

SUITE: 1835 passed at the pwj commit, exit 0. 1836 at the tip after the cost caps.

NO-CLAIM

CI IS NOT GREEN ON THE TIP, AND CANNOT BE. The account's Actions tier is exhausted and
refreshes on 2026-09-01; a job dispatched after that point returns "The job was not started
because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased"
in four seconds with no steps. This project's standing rule is that the ship is done when CI
is green on the PUSHED commit, and that condition is unmet for every close after run
33104091974. The evidence above comes from runs that completed before the tier ran out; the

This does not establish that the compliance skill runs in CI. It does not: the skill lives

title: Harness: three unexercised paths in the missing-items corrector
description:

title: Harness: four doctor detector findings are unreachable without a mock, and d_kat has no vectors seam
description:
Four of `cairn doctor`'s detector findings cannot be reached by any test, because
the thing they detect cannot be made to fail without a mock, and the doctor's tests
take no mocks.

After cairn-m0-e0s.18's audit pass the doctor sits at 97 percent line coverage
(`cairn.doctor` 798 statements, 24 uncovered) with 28 fixtures. Every remaining
detector gap is one of these:

  detectors.py:158  D-pari-inprocess/stack
  detectors.py:172  D-pari-inprocess/ellcard
  detectors.py:185  D-pari-inprocess/libpari-version
  detectors.py:480  D-kat/mismatch

The first three need cypari2 itself to misreport: a failed 64 MB allocatemem, an
`ellcard` on corpus-1 returning something other than 7, or a `pari.version()` that
is not 2.17.x. Reaching them needs either a mock of `pari.pari` / `pari.pari_versions`
or a second libpari build on the machine to point cypari2 at.

The fourth is closer. `d_kat` calls `kat.run()` with no argument, so its vectors come
from the repo-wide `kat.DEFAULT_VECTORS`. There is no way to hand it a corrupt vector
file, and corrupting the repo's own is not an option -- the isolation guard fails any
test that leaves the checkout modified, correctly.

WHAT: give `d_kat` its vectors through the doctor's `Context` rather than reading a
module global, so a fixture can point it at a deliberately corrupt vector file under
`tmp_path` and `D-kat/mismatch` becomes reachable with no mock at all. This is the
same shape as the `GP_BIN` seam the doctor already declares, which lets the gp
fixtures point at real `/bin/sh` scripts.

The three cypari2 findings are a different problem and may not be worth solving. A
second libpari on the machine is real work for three refusal branches. Decide
deliberately: either declare a fourth seam for `pari.pari_versions` and say so where
the other seams are declared, or record that these three are unreachable by design
and stop counting them as a gap.

DONE WHEN: `D-kat/mismatch` has a fixture that corrupts a vector file under `tmp_path`
and asserts the finding, with no mock; and the three `D-pari-inprocess` findings either
have fixtures or a recorded decision that they stay unreachable, with the reason.

Surfaced by cairn-m0-e0s.18's audit as F11. The 28 fixtures that bead does ship cover
every other declared finding.

title: Harness: a refused attempt's receipt does not record the threshold that refused it
description:
cairn-x72 split the budget ceiling into two: the verdict reads CPU time and refuses with
BUDGET_EXCEEDED, and a generous wall cap catches a stuck child and refuses with BLOCKED.

The receipt records cpu_user_s, cpu_sys_s and wall_s. It does not record ceiling_s or
wall_cap_s. So a reader holding a refused attempt's receipt can see what the attempt spent
but not what it was allowed to spend, and cannot tell from the receipt alone whether the
refusal was correct.

The kill log line names wall_cap_s, so the information exists in the run log. A receipt is
the durable artifact and the log is not.

WHY THIS WAS NOT DONE IN cairn-x72: receipt fields are hashed content. Adding one moves
every receipt hash and the goldens that carry them, which is a different change with a
different blast radius from re-pointing a clock.

DONE WHEN
- A decision, recorded, on whether the threshold belongs in the receipt at all, given that
  the recipe plus tiers.json already determine it and a receipt that repeats a derivable
  number can drift from it.
- If it goes in: the goldens that move are named before the change, not discovered during it.

title: Harness: the tier budget ceiling reads wall time, so a busy CI runner reads as a refused gate
description:
`runner.status_for` refuses an attempt when `wall_s > ceiling_s`, and the ceiling is
`ceiling_multiplier * expected_wall_s`: 4 from `bundle/tiers.json` times 0.1338 from
`src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py:32`, so 0.5352 seconds of WALL time for the 40-bit toy curve.

That number was measured on a developer machine. A shared CI runner does not honor it, and
the refusal it produces reads as a gate finding rather than as a slow neighbor.

OBSERVED 2026-08-27, run 33105687625, commit 4005439, macos-latest:

  ceiling_s  0.5352
  wall_s     0.600659   <- refused
  cpu_s      0.235461   <- less than half the ceiling

The attempt used 0.235 s of CPU to spend 0.601 s of wall. That ratio IS the contention, and
the receipt already records both numbers. The gate reads the one that measures the machine.

The same commit is green locally at 1835 passed in 270 s on a quiet machine, and the two CI
runs on it failed DIFFERENTLY -- one BUDGET_EXCEEDED at 388 s, one wedged until the session
deadline fired at 25 minutes naming `tests/e2e/test_m0_slice.py::test_the_derivation_`.
Different failures on one unchanged commit is the signature of contention, not of a defect.

Prior instance, recorded in a previous session: a load spike produced three BUDGET_EXCEEDED
failures on tests that then passed 49/49 on a quiet machine.

WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY A NUMBER TO RAISE

The budget ceiling is a real tier control, and PLAN section 5 states Tier-1 as "one core,
minutes". A gate that refuses genuinely runaway work is doing its job, and widening the
multiplier until CI stops complaining would retire the control rather than fix it. The
defect is the CLOCK, not the threshold: wall time on a shared runner measures the runner.

Note `src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py` is in `IDENTITY_SOURCES`, so editing the profile
constant reseeds the randomized arm and moves the transcript and certificate goldens. A fix
that lives in `runner.py` and `bundle/tiers.json` costs nothing there; a fix that edits the
profile is a re-certification.

DONE WHEN
- A decision, recorded, on which clock the ceiling reads. CPU time is already on the
  receipt and is the honest measure of the work; wall time measures the work plus whoever
  else is on the box.
- Whatever clock is chosen, a test that fails while the defect is present: an attempt whose
  CPU is inside the ceiling and whose wall is outside must not be refused, and one whose
  CPU is genuinely outside must still be refused.
- If wall time is kept for any reason, that reason is written down along with what CI is
  expected to do on a slow runner, so the next red run is diagnosable rather than puzzling.

comments.author: jr843u
comments.text:
CLOSED. The clock decision is recorded below, and the defect was reproduced on this machine
before anything was changed.

THE REPRODUCTION, WHICH THIS BEAD PREDICTED

A full suite run on 2026-08-31 under machine load returned 17 failures; re-run in isolation,
12 still failed. The errors are this bead verbatim:

  AssertionError: assert ('BUDGET_EXCEEDED' == 'OK')
  AssertionError: assert -15 == 0                      SIGTERM, the launch loop's own kill
  parsed=ParsedOutput(well_formed=False, status=None, reason='stdout is empty')

The suite had been red for the reason this bead names. It was not flakiness: the ceiling is a
fixed 0.5352 s of wall, so a loaded box blows it deterministically.

THE DECISION, WHICH CLOCK THE CEILING READS

The verdict reads CPU time, user plus system. A separate and much larger wall cap remains as
a liveness net, and it carries its own status.

  ceiling_s   4 x 0.1338 = 0.5352 s, unchanged in arithmetic, now compared against
              cpu_user_s + cpu_sys_s rather than wall_s
  wall_cap_s  max(wall_cap_multiplier x ceiling_s, ceiling_s + wall_cap_floor_s)
              = 120.5352 s for the toy curve, from bundle/tiers.json

Both are needed. CPU is the honest measure of the work, and wall measures the work plus
whoever else is on the box. But a child that is genuinely stuck burns no CPU, so a pure CPU
budget alone never fires on the case that most needs a timeout. Two ceilings, and critically
two statuses: BUDGET_EXCEEDED for work that is too expensive, BLOCKED for work that is stuck.
A single status over two causes is the conflation this project has now been bitten by three
times.

WHAT CI DOES ON A SLOW RUNNER NOW. The observed CI datum from run 33105687625 -- wall
0.600659, cpu 0.235461, ceiling 0.5352 -- reads OK: cpu is inside the ceiling and wall is far
inside the cap. A runner would have to be roughly 225 times slower in wall than in CPU before
the net fires, and the status would then read BLOCKED, so a future red run says stuck rather
than over budget. The tier control is not widened. BUDGET_EXCEEDED now requires real CPU,
which contention does not manufacture.

Precedence when both fire: BUDGET_EXCEEDED wins. That was the implementer's judgment, not an
instruction, and it is pinned by a test so it can be flipped deliberately rather than drifting.

A SECOND SITE OF THE SAME DEFECT, FOUND AND FIXED

Eight of the twelve failures went green on the runner change alone. The other four were a
different instance of the same shape: the grace-window and group-sweep tests hard-code their
own wall constants, 0.2 s, measured on a quiet box. A CPython interpreter cannot boot and
install a SIGTERM handler in 0.2 s on a loaded machine, so SIGTERM arrived before the handler
existed and the fixture's whole point never ran. Raised to a named HANDLER_INSTALLS_WITHIN_S
of 3.0 against fixtures that loop for 30 s. No assertion was weakened to buy it: exit_status
== -9, the grandchild existence check and sigterm_seen == "term" all still hold.

VERIFICATION, RE-EXECUTED BY THE SESSION

The four new clock tests were observed failing against the unfixed code before the fix.
The 12 isolation failures: 81 passed, 0 failed, no survivors.
scripts/check.sh: 1937 passed, all gates pass, exit 0.
No re-certification: implementation_revision is unchanged and zero files in
toy_curve.IDENTITY_SOURCES were modified, verified by execution.
tests/goldens/gate_bundle_hash.golden moved because bundle/tiers.json is one of its hashed
sources; it is the only golden that moved.
Each half reverted separately leaves the new tests red, so neither half is untested.

NO-CLAIM

The fix was verified at load 5, not at the load 15-25 that produced the failure, so the green
is weaker evidence than the red it replaces. The 120 s wall-cap floor is adopted from the
design, not measured; no test exercises the cap at its shipped value, only at an injected
1.0 s, and that the same code path fires at 120.5 s is arithmetic inference over unit-tested
code. schema.sql uses CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so a substrate created before this change
keeps the old CHECK and will raise on a BLOCKED close; fresh substrates are unaffected.
BUDGET_EXCEEDED was grepped for in Python files only, so prose or JSON elsewhere enumerating
runner statuses may now be incomplete. test_a_slower_tick_still_stops_the_child still uses a
0.2 s cap and belongs to the same family as the four constants raised here if it ever flakes.
The receipt records what an attempt spent but not the threshold it was allowed to spend, so a
refused attempt is diagnosable from the kill log rather than from the receipt alone; that is
owned by cairn-wdg, opened for it.

title: Harness: CI runs on macos-latest and bills at 10x, which is what exhausted the quota
description:
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` line 24 is `runs-on: macos-latest`. GitHub bills macOS runners at
10x the Linux rate, so a run whose wall time is 8 minutes costs 80 of the 2000 free minutes.

MEASURED 2026-09-01 from `gh run list`, summing each run's created-to-updated interval:

  30 runs listed              216 wall minutes    2161 billed at 10x
  3 runs on 2026-09-01         14.6 wall minutes   146 billed at 10x

The quota exhaustion on 2026-08-27 was 23 runs spending about 2020 of 2000. On ubuntu-latest
the same 216 wall minutes bill 216, and the quota is never reached.

WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINE CHANGE

`toy_curve.identity_bundle()` hashes tool digests and the container digest into
`implementation_revision`, and the certificate and transcript goldens bind to it. If cypari2
or PARI digests differently on Linux, the goldens move, and that is a re-certification rather
than a configuration edit. The question is empirical and one run answers it.

`research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` records the stack probes; `cairn-hcl`, deferred to M1,
already states the gold tier needs Linux, so a Linux runner moves toward that rather than away.

WHAT ELSE SPENDS MINUTES

`.githooks/post-commit` pushes every bead-closing commit, so three beads closed in ten minutes
produced three runs. `cancel-in-progress` is on for main and did kill one of them, which is
the mechanism working, but a batched close would not have started them. Closing several beads
in one commit costs one run.

DONE WHEN
- A decision, recorded, on the runner, with the golden movement measured rather than predicted.
- If the goldens move: named before the change, with whether the movement is a real identity
  change or an artifact of the build.
- If macos-latest is kept, the reason is written down along with the per-run cost, so the next
  quota exhaustion is a known price rather than a surprise.
- A decision on whether every bead-closing commit still pushes, or whether a session batches.
close_reason: duplicate: cairn-hcl owns the runner matrix and measured the Linux blockers first

title: Harness: three unexercised paths in the missing-items corrector
description:
Three gaps left open by cairn-8jm, all in scripts/audit_missing_items.py, none of which
that bead's acceptance criteria reached.

1. THE `- check` LINE SHAPE IS A PARSE GAP OF UNESTABLISHED FREQUENCY.

score-bead.py:1241 emits `- check \`<id>\` (<verdict>) — <reason>` into the same section for
every compliance check with verdict FAIL or MISSING. cairn-8jm extended spec_item_id_of to
both shapes, so a given id classifies identically whichever producer wrote its line, and both
shapes are tested. What is unestablished is whether Phase 4 ever emits FAIL for an item the
gatherer never searched: every compliance.json in this repo is the stub with an empty checks
list, and a scan of all recorded passes finds 710 `- spec item` lines, 241 `- theater` lines
and zero `- check` lines. So the handling is correct by construction and unexercised by any
real artifact.

DONE WHEN a real Phase 4 has run at least once under the orchestrator and the resulting
compliance.json is either shown to contain no such row, or is used as the fixture for a test
that exercises the shape against real output.

2. ONLY ONE UNREADABLE-INPUT PATH HAS A NAMED OUTCOME.

EXIT_UNREADABLE_SPEC covers json.JSONDecodeError from spec.json. An unreadable scorecard.md,
a permissions error on either file, and a spec.json that parses to a non-dict all raise
uncaught. The direction is safe -- a traceback exits nonzero and the hook denies -- but it is
not one of the three named outcomes, and the enforcement discipline this project follows asks
for a distinct log line per outcome so an agent can confirm which path fired. This is the
same defect class cairn-8jm fixed for the missing heading, one layer out.

DONE WHEN each unreadable-input path has its own verdict, exit code and .check.log line, with
a test per path.

3. THE FROZEN GATHERER EXCERPT CANNOT DETECT A LAUNDERED REGENERATION.

tests/fixtures/compliance_skill/ holds a point-in-time cut of gather-evidence.sh with the
source digest, and tests/integration/test_audit_missing_items_drift.py compares the live file
against it. Someone who edits the vendored gatherer AND regenerates the fixture in one step
passes both the hermetic assertions and the live comparison. Only the GATHERER_* constants
failing to match the new excerpt would catch it, and a regeneration that preserves the
structures those constants name would slip through entirely.

DONE WHEN either the fixture's digest is pinned somewhere a regeneration cannot silently
rewrite, or the classifier's constants are derived from the excerpt at import time so a
structural change cannot leave them stale.

TEST PLAN

- tests/unit/test_audit_missing_items.py — one test per newly named unreadable-input outcome,
  each asserting the exit code, the verdict on stdout and the .check.log line.
- tests/unit/test_audit_missing_items_gatherer.py — the laundered-regeneration guard, run
  hermetically so it holds on a machine with no vendored skill.
